## A note on the dated result blocks

Several chunks below carry comment blocks headed `RESULT, <date> 2026`. These
are contemporaneous records: the numbers each run produced on the day it was
run, kept so that a later reader can see what was known when a decision was
taken. **They are not the paper's numbers and are not maintained.**

Sixteen of them date from September 2026 and were computed on a 47-patient
input. The analysis set later became 48 patients, and the manuscript, the
deposited Supplementary Tables and this document's own code all report the
48-patient result. The clade gap is the clearest instance: the September blocks
record +0.310, the reported value is +0.3291, and the difference is one patient,
not a change of method.

The narrative sections are in the same position wherever a number is written
out rather than wrapped in `v()` or `vc()`: those recompute at knit time, a bare
literal does not, and §0's `v_audit()` counts how many remain. §11a and §11b are
the ones to know about — their coupling and conditional-response numbers were
computed on the 47-patient paired set, and the patient counts in them are that
set's.

Run against the input named in `../data/README.md`, the code here reproduces the
published values. Where a dated block or a written-out number disagrees with the
manuscript, the manuscript is correct and the document is a historical record.

```{r knitr-opts, include=FALSE}
## FALSE: render the code only. TRUE: run top to bottom from the input bundle
## (§0b). FALSE is the documented default (§0, "Running it") and is what this
## deposit ships, so that knitting the file renders it rather than launching a
## full analysis against data the reader may not have. Spelled FALSE, not F:
## T and F are ordinary variables in R and can be rebound, and this one switch
## controls `eval` for all 101 chunks.
RUN <- FALSE
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = RUN, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5)
options(width = 110)

## ===== numeric registry ======================================================
## The HEADLINE numbers in the narrative are drawn from the objects that
## computed them: 85 inline calls, every one of them v() or vc(). The narrative
## also carries several hundred numbers that are not -- thresholds, draw
## counts, set sizes, and a tail of coefficients that were written out when
## they were measured. Those are hard-coded, v_audit() counts them, and the
## note at the top of this document about the 47-patient vintage is about
## them. This block is the mechanism and the audit, not a guarantee that no
## literal remains.
##
##   `r v(expr, recorded)`        value computed EARLIER in this document
##   `r vc("key", recorded)`      value computed LATER (§0 summary table only);
##                                served from .vcache, checked against the live
##                                value when vc_put("key", expr) runs later
##
## `recorded` is the number currently written in the text. It is the fallback
## when the expression cannot be evaluated, and it sets the number of decimals.
## Nothing is silent: v_report() at the end lists every DRIFT (live value differs
## from the text) and every UNCOMPUTED (expression did not resolve, text used).
## A number with no v() around it is still hard-coded and v_audit() counts it.
.V <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
.V$log   <- list()
.V$cache <- local({
  f <- ".vcache.rds"
  if (file.exists(f)) tryCatch(readRDS(f), error = function(e) list()) else list()
})
.V$fresh <- list()

## The minus sign is emitted as the HTML entity &minus;, never as a UTF-8
## character. R's inline output is then pure ASCII, so the rendered sign is the
## same whatever locale R was started in: a C-locale R mangles a raw U+2212 into
## three latin-1 bytes and pandoc escapes them into the page as <e2>&lt;88&gt;.
## Tied to html_document, this document's only output format.
.v_fmt <- function(x, digits, pct, big) {
  s <- formatC(abs(x), format = "f", digits = digits,
               big.mark = if (big) "," else "")
  paste0(if (x < 0) "&minus;" else "", s, if (pct) "%" else "")
}
## `recorded` may be given as a string ("9.70") to keep trailing zeros, which a
## numeric literal loses: 9.70 is 9.7 to R, and the table needs two decimals.
.v_digits <- function(recorded) {
  s <- gsub("[^0-9.]", "", as.character(recorded), useBytes = TRUE)
  if (grepl(".", s, fixed = TRUE)) nchar(sub("^.*\\.", "", s)) else 0L
}
## Reads the recorded literal whether its sign is an ASCII hyphen or U+2212, and
## without depending on the locale being able to decode the latter.
.v_num <- function(recorded) {
  s   <- as.character(recorded)
  neg <- grepl("^(-|\xe2\x88\x92)", s, useBytes = TRUE)
  x   <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9.eE+]", "", s, useBytes = TRUE)))
  if (isTRUE(neg)) -abs(x) else x
}
.v_record <- function(src, recorded, live, kind, digits) {
  status <- if (is.na(live)) "UNCOMPUTED"
            else if (abs(live - recorded) > 0.5 * 10^(-digits)) "DRIFT" else "ok"
  .V$log[[length(.V$log) + 1L]] <- list(
    chunk = tryCatch(knitr::opts_current$get("label"), error = function(e) NA_character_),
    src = src, recorded = recorded, live = live, status = status, kind = kind)
  status
}
.v_scalar <- function(z) {
  if (is.null(z) || length(z) != 1L) return(NA_real_)
  z <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(z))
  if (!is.finite(z)) NA_real_ else z
}

v <- function(expr, recorded, digits = NULL, pct = FALSE, big = FALSE) {
  src  <- paste(deparse(substitute(expr)), collapse = " ")
  live <- .v_scalar(tryCatch(expr, error = function(e) NULL))
  rec  <- .v_num(recorded)
  if (is.null(digits)) digits <- .v_digits(recorded)
  .v_record(src, rec, live, "inline", digits)
  .v_fmt(if (is.na(live)) rec else live, digits, pct, big)
}

## §0 summary table: the value is computed further down the document, so it is
## served from the previous knit's cache and verified when vc_put() reaches it.
vc <- function(key, recorded, digits = NULL, pct = FALSE, big = FALSE) {
  rec  <- .v_num(recorded)
  live <- .v_scalar(.V$cache[[key]])
  if (is.null(digits)) digits <- .v_digits(recorded)
  .v_record(paste0("cache:", key), rec, live, "cache", digits)
  .v_fmt(if (is.na(live)) rec else live, digits, pct, big)
}
vc_put <- function(key, expr) {
  live <- .v_scalar(tryCatch(expr, error = function(e) NULL))
  .V$fresh[[key]] <- live
  invisible(live)
}

v_report <- function(write_cache = TRUE) {
  L <- .V$log
  if (!length(L)) { cat("v(): no calls recorded.\n"); return(invisible(NULL)) }
  d <- do.call(rbind, lapply(L, function(r) data.frame(
    chunk = if (is.null(r$chunk) || is.na(r$chunk)) "" else r$chunk,
    source = r$src, in_text = r$recorded, computed = r$live,
    status = r$status, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)))

  ## cached §0 values: compare this knit's live value against what was printed
  for (k in names(.V$fresh)) {
    i <- which(d$source == paste0("cache:", k))
    if (!length(i)) next
    live <- .V$fresh[[k]]
    d$computed[i] <- live
    dig <- nchar(sub("^.*\\.", "", format(d$in_text[i[1]], scientific = FALSE,
                                          trim = TRUE)))
    if (!grepl("\\.", format(d$in_text[i[1]], scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE))) dig <- 0L
    d$status[i] <- ifelse(is.na(live), "UNCOMPUTED",
                   ifelse(abs(live - d$in_text[i]) > 0.5 * 10^(-dig),
                          "DRIFT (printed from cache)", "ok"))
  }

  cat(sprintf("v() calls %d  |  ok %d  |  DRIFT %d  |  UNCOMPUTED %d\n",
              nrow(d), sum(d$status == "ok"),
              sum(grepl("^DRIFT", d$status)), sum(d$status == "UNCOMPUTED")))
  bad <- d[d$status != "ok", ]
  if (nrow(bad)) {
    cat("\n--- numbers that do NOT reproduce ---\n"); print(bad, row.names = FALSE)
  } else cat("every narrative number drawn by v() reproduces.\n")

  if (write_cache && length(.V$fresh)) {
    keep <- .V$fresh[!vapply(.V$fresh, is.na, logical(1))]
    if (length(keep)) saveRDS(keep, ".vcache.rds")
    cat(sprintf("\n.vcache.rds written: %d headline values for the next knit.\n",
                length(keep)))
  }
  invisible(d)
}

## Accessors used by the narrative tables. Each returns NULL when the object it
## reads is absent (a guarded chunk that did not run), so v() falls back to the
## recorded number and v_report() names it instead of the knit failing.
## `sp` is REASSIGNED at top level at L4504 (a Sheba path table) and SETS_P at
## L7320 (SETS_FULL). spv()/szp() therefore only resolve ABOVE those lines; an
## inline call placed below prints its recorded value and logs UNCOMPUTED rather
## than drifting silently. Verified 14 Oct: no such call exists. Keep it that way.
spv <- function(pw, col) { s <- get0("sp", ifnotfound = NULL)
  if (is.null(s) || !col %in% names(s)) NULL else s[[col]][match(pw, s$pathway)] }
szp <- function(pw) { S <- get0("SETS_P", ifnotfound = NULL)
  if (is.null(S) || !pw %in% names(S)) NULL else lengths(S)[[pw]] }
tk7 <- function(set, col) { x <- get0("tab7k", ifnotfound = NULL)
  if (is.null(x) || !col %in% names(x)) NULL else x[[col]][match(set, x$set)] }
jav <- function(row, col) { x <- get0("JA", ifnotfound = NULL)
  if (is.null(x) || !row %in% rownames(x)) NULL else x[row, col] }

## How much of the narrative is still typed by hand.
v_audit <- function(rmd = knitr::current_input()) {
  if (is.null(rmd) || !file.exists(rmd)) { cat("v_audit: source not found.\n"); return(invisible(NULL)) }
  L <- readLines(rmd, warn = FALSE); inch <- FALSE; nar <- character(0)
  for (l in L) {
    if (grepl("^```", l)) { inch <- !inch; next }
    if (!inch) nar <- c(nar, l)
  }
  drawn <- sum(vapply(gregexpr("`r v[c]?\\(", nar), function(m) sum(m > 0), integer(1)))
  strip <- gsub("`[^`]*`", "", nar)
  typed <- sum(vapply(gregexpr("(?<![\\w.$/-])\\d[\\d,]*\\.?\\d*%?(?![\\w.])",
                               strip, perl = TRUE),
                      function(m) sum(m > 0), integer(1)))
  cat(sprintf("narrative numbers: %d drawn by v() | %d still typed | %.0f%% drawn\n",
              drawn, typed, 100 * drawn / max(1, drawn + typed)))
  invisible(c(drawn = drawn, typed = typed))
}
## =============================================================================
```

# 0. What this document is

The analysis of two gut metaproteomic cohorts of stage-IV melanoma patients on
immune checkpoint blockade. Every number reported in the manuscript is produced
by code here or by a companion script listed in the Appendix.

| | Pittsburgh | Sheba |
|---|---|---|
| role | discovery | pre-specified test |
| stool sampling | **on treatment** (49 of 55 samples after start; 6 on or before it) | **before treatment** |
| TMT plexes run / analysed | 8 / **6** | 5 / **4** |
| analysed samples | **`r vc("pitt.n", "55")`** (one per patient) | **`r vc("sheba.n", "35")`** (one per patient) |
| R / NR | **`r vc("pitt.R", "25")` / `r vc("pitt.NR", "30")`** | **`r vc("sheba.R", "27")` / `r vc("sheba.NR", "8")`** |
| acquisition | TMT-11 (MS level to confirm) | TMT-11; mixture 1 SPS-MS3, mixtures 3–5 MS2 |
| response definition | ever progressed | RECIST best overall response |
| paired metagenome | 82 samples (74 labelled) | 46 profiles (33 patients) |

Plexes are dropped when they carry no within-plex contrast (fewer than 2 R or
2 NR): Pittsburgh's `pitt_ontx` arm is 75 samples before that rule and **55**
after it; Sheba's mixture 2 is excluded for the same reason.

**Sample corrections, 13 October 2026** (`pitt_sample_corrections.R`, applied in
§0a and nowhere else). TMT1_126, annotated under the corrupted name MF001A3A817,
is MF0017. **That relabel is the only correction that survives.** Two channels were
excluded on 13 October and both were restored the same day: TMT8_126 (MF1640) on the
trial registry, which marks a repeat sample by reusing the study ID and gives MF1640
and MF1672 consecutive registrations with treatment starts four weeks apart; and
TMT7_127N (MF1529) by decision, after the identity test put a trace of the right
patient in a channel the magnitude evidence had called empty. The arm is therefore
the full 75 / 55, with 25 R and 30 NR, as it was before. What the relabel does change
is the PAIRED set, 47 to 48: MF0017's metagenome had been filed under the corrupted
name and so was never linked to its channel. Every permutation null made before
13 October, and every one made on the 53- and 54-sample intermediates, was made on
another design and is not scored here.

**Two conventions that govern everything below.**

*Sign.* Enrichment is scored R − NR, so **NES < 0 means higher in
non-responders**.

*p-values.* Every enrichment p is a **within-plex permutation p**: response
labels are shuffled inside each plex and the whole chain — aggregation,
normalisation, model, enrichment — is re-run per draw. The per-sample share
(§8e), the Bacillota-internal test (C3) and the time-on-treatment tests (§8d) are
within-plex permutations of plex-adjusted models. Other checks (§8b, §11b) are
plex-adjusted linear models with parametric p unless a permutation is stated,
and metagenome comparisons, which have no plexes, are Wilcoxon tests. `fgsea`'s
internal p-values are **not used anywhere**; §7a gives the measurement that rules
them out.

**Annotation and taxonomy.** Both were completed part-way through the study.
Every reported set, every enrichment result and every permutation null uses the
completed versions (§5), and §5 runs before any reported set is built. A few
specificity checks in §8b were recorded before completion; each is labelled with
what it was measured on. The five-layer landscape scan on the initial annotation
is kept in §6a, labelled as such; no reported number comes from it.

**Running it.** The first chunk holds one switch. With `RUN <- FALSE`, the
default, knitting renders the code without executing it. With `RUN <- TRUE`, the
document runs top to bottom in a fresh R session from the input bundle and the
raw data described in §0b; §0c asserts the inputs before anything else runs.
That mode has not yet been run end to end (§13).

## 0a. Libraries — load order is load-bearing

Bioconductor first, tidyverse last: `QFeatures` / `SummarizedExperiment` attach
the S4 stack above `dplyr`, and a masked verb can return its input unchanged
rather than erroring. The masking check is fatal, not a warning.

```{r libs}
## ---- LOAD ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING --------------------------------------------
## QFeatures / SummarizedExperiment attach the whole S4 stack ABOVE dplyr:
## loaded the other way round, `count` resolves to matrixStats and `rename`
## to an S4Vectors generic.
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  ## 1. Bioconductor and its S4 stack
  library(QFeatures); library(msqrob2); library(SummarizedExperiment)
  ## 2. everything else that is not tidyverse
  library(here); library(httr); library(ggplot2); library(broom)
  ## 3. tidyverse LAST, so its verbs win
  library(readr); library(stringr); library(tibble)
  library(tidyr); library(purrr); library(dplyr)
})

## ---- MASKING CHECK — fatal, not a warning ----------------------------------
## A masked verb can return its input UNCHANGED rather than erroring. Later
## chunks call dplyr verbs BARE, so every verb they use is guarded.
check_masking_v15 <- function(fatal = TRUE) {
  need_dplyr <- c("count","filter","select","mutate","summarise","group_by",
                  "arrange","rename","pull","n_distinct","bind_rows","left_join",
                  "inner_join","distinct","transmute","case_when","first","lag")
  where <- vapply(need_dplyr, function(f)
    tryCatch(environmentName(environment(get(f))), error = function(e) "MISSING"),
    character(1))
  bad <- need_dplyr[where != "dplyr"]

  need_purrr <- c("map_dfr","map_dbl","map_int","imap_dfr","walk")
  wp <- vapply(need_purrr, function(f)
    tryCatch(environmentName(environment(get(f))), error = function(e) "MISSING"),
    character(1))
  bad_p <- need_purrr[wp != "purrr"]

  if (length(bad) || length(bad_p)) {
    msg <- paste0("MASKED — reattach tidyverse above the S4 stack.\n",
                  if (length(bad))   paste0("  dplyr: ",
                    paste(sprintf("%s->%s", bad, where[bad]), collapse = ", "), "\n"),
                  if (length(bad_p)) paste0("  purrr: ",
                    paste(sprintf("%s->%s", bad_p, wp[bad_p]), collapse = ", "), "\n"),
                  "  fix: for (p in c('readr','stringr','tibble','tidyr','purrr','dplyr')) {\n",
                  "         detach(paste0('package:',p), character.only=TRUE, unload=FALSE)\n",
                  "         library(p, character.only=TRUE) }")
    if (fatal) stop(msg) else warning(msg)
  }
  ## base set ops must also be intact — S4Vectors can override union()
  stopifnot(identical(union(c("a","b"), c("b","c")), c("a","b","c")))
  invisible(TRUE)
}
check_masking_v15()
cat("load order OK — dplyr at position", which(search() == "package:dplyr"), "\n")
```

```{r clean-run}
## Handles BOTH forms. basename() does not split on backslashes on macOS/Linux,
## so the Windows path is stripped explicitly first. A no-op on bare names.
clean_run <- function(x) {
  x |> sub("^.*\\\\", "", x = _) |>
    basename() |>
    sub("^interact-", "", x = _) |>
    sub("\\.pep\\.xml$", "", x = _)
}
```

## 0b. Inputs: the bundle and the raw data

A fresh session needs two things.

**The input bundle**, written once by the first chunk below from the analyst's
session, and verified against its checksums on every load:

| in the bundle | what it is | produced by |
|---|---|---|
| `inputs.rds` | `mp` (5 slots), `annot`, `SAMP`, `SAMP_PRIMARY`, `TIER_PRIMARY`, `PARAMS` (per-arm minimum 2), `RESP_LEVELS` | `analysis_v11.Rmd` §0–§4; MSstatsTMT processing (`02_metaproteomics_Sheba_Pitt.Rmd` §5–§9); metaannot export |
| `files/` | the metaannot tables; the Unipept caches (`unipept_lca.rds`, `unipept_lca_gained.rds`, `unipept_fill/`); the clinical table `Lior_UPF_data.csv`; the Sheba collection records; the Pittsburgh null draws (`nulls_pitt/`); the pooled Sheba null input; optionally the database prefix counts | the analysis session and the null server |
| `MANIFEST_md5.csv`, `package_versions.csv`, `sessionInfo.txt`, `renv.lock` | checksums, and the package environment the analysis ran in | the export chunk |

**The raw data**, under `DATA_ROOT` with its original layout: the FragPipe PSM
tables (`Metaproteomics/`), the three Prokka FASTAs and emapper annotations
(`Proteomic_databases/`, `metagenomics/…/prokka_output/`), and the metagenome
profiles and logs (`metagenomics/`).

Nothing is queried over the network while `OFFLINE` is `TRUE`: Unipept results
come from the frozen caches, and KEGG pathway names from a fixed dictionary.

```r
## LISTING ONLY under Run All. Execute this ONCE, deliberately, in the session
## that holds the upstream objects — see the run order in REPRODUCTION_PROTOCOL.md.
## It is fenced as plain `r` so a Run All cannot rewrite the bundle mid-analysis.
## Run ONCE, on its own, in the analyst's session that already holds the upstream
## objects — before any other chunk here, since the next chunk redefines `paths`
## and `PROJ`. Writes everything a fresh session needs into BUNDLE_DIR.
BUNDLE_DIR <- Sys.getenv("ICB_BUNDLE_DIR", here::here("input_bundle"))
FILES_DIR  <- file.path(BUNDLE_DIR, "files")
dir.create(FILES_DIR, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

## 1. the upstream objects. Taken from the live session when there is one, and
## otherwise from bundle_objects.rds, which §13 writes on every knit — knitting
## runs in its own process, so a console started afterwards has no `mp`.
OBJ <- if (exists("mp")) {
  MP_SLOTS <- c("pitt_mat_f", "pitt_annot_use", "sheba_annot_use",
                "pitt_pw_map_obs", "host_state")
  stopifnot(all(MP_SLOTS %in% names(mp)))
  list(mp = mp[MP_SLOTS], annot = annot, SAMP = SAMP,
       SAMP_PRIMARY = SAMP_PRIMARY, TIER_PRIMARY = TIER_PRIMARY,
       PARAMS = PARAMS, RESP_LEVELS = RESP_LEVELS)
} else {
  f <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "bundle_objects.rds")
  if (!file.exists(f))
    stop("no live session and no ", f, ".\nKnit the document once (§13 writes ",
         "it), or run the chunks in the console before this listing.",
         call. = FALSE)
  message("no `mp` in the session — using ", f)
  readRDS(f)
}
stopifnot(all(c("mp","annot","SAMP","SAMP_PRIMARY","TIER_PRIMARY",
                "PARAMS","RESP_LEVELS") %in% names(OBJ)))
saveRDS(list(bundle_version = 1L, created = Sys.time(), objects = OBJ),
        file.path(BUNDLE_DIR, "inputs.rds"))

## 2. the small files, from where the analysis session keeps them
## Paths corrected 24 Sep 2026. Three were wrong and the combined stopifnot
## reported none of them: `Lior_UPF_data.csv` and `nulls_pitt` were relative to
## the working directory rather than to the metadata and output directories, and
## the re-annotation TSVs used PROJ (= OUT_DIR) rather than REANNOT_DIR — the
## same mistake §5c already carries a note about.
src  <- c(file.path(paths$out_dir, c("unipept_lca.rds", "unipept_lca_gained.rds",
                                     "sheba_sample_timing_all_records.csv")),
          file.path(REANNOT_DIR, c("pitt_psm__annotation_final.tsv",
                                   "sheba_psm__annotation_final.tsv")),
          meta_file(META_PITT, "Lior_UPF_data.csv"))
dirs <- c(file.path(paths$out_dir, c("unipept_fill", "nulls_pitt")))
pool <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "sheba_pooled", "null_input.RData")

## Report WHICH input is missing. The combined assertion cost a run per fault.
.miss_f <- src[!file.exists(src)]; .miss_d <- dirs[!dir.exists(dirs)]
if (length(.miss_f) || length(.miss_d) || !file.exists(pool))
  stop("cannot build the bundle; missing:\n  ",
       paste(c(.miss_f, .miss_d, if (!file.exists(pool)) pool), collapse = "\n  "),
       call. = FALSE)
stopifnot(all(file.copy(src,  FILES_DIR, overwrite = TRUE)),
          all(file.copy(dirs, FILES_DIR, recursive = TRUE, overwrite = TRUE)))
dir.create(file.path(FILES_DIR, "sheba_pooled"), showWarnings = FALSE)
stopifnot(file.copy(pool, file.path(FILES_DIR, "sheba_pooled"), overwrite = TRUE))
## optional: without it, §1a rebuilds the counts from the FASTAs with grep
dbchk <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "DB_prefix_counts.rds")
if (file.exists(dbchk)) file.copy(dbchk, FILES_DIR, overwrite = TRUE)

## 3. package versions and the session; an renv lockfile if renv is installed
## EVERY PACKAGE THE FIVE DOCUMENTS USE, not the subset this document loads.
## This list was 25 names and recorded versions for a quarter of the stack: a
## reader installing from it still had no version for ALDEx2, ANCOMBC,
## maaslin3, microeco, vegan, ComplexHeatmap, phyloseq, clusterProfiler, goseq,
## MSstatsTMT, survival, coxphf, pwr, ragg, systemfonts or msigdbr -- most of
## what 01, 02 and the briefs run on. Derived by parsing every chunk in all
## five documents and collecting each `pkg::`, `library(pkg)` and
## `requireNamespace("pkg")`, minus base R. Re-derive it the same way after
## adding a dependency; tools/record_environment.R does exactly that. The
## script derives 58; lme4 is the one name here it does not, because lme4
## reaches this analysis through msqrob2 rather than through a call of ours.
PKGS <- c(
  "ALDEx2", "ANCOMBC", "AnnotationDbi", "Biostrings", "ComplexHeatmap",
  "EnsDb.Hsapiens.v86", "KEGGREST", "MSstatsTMT", "MicrobiomeStat", "MsCoreUtils",
  "QFeatures", "SummarizedExperiment", "ape", "ashr", "broom",
  "circlize", "clusterProfiler", "coxphf", "dplyr", "ensembldb",
  "fgsea", "file2meco", "forcats", "ggbeeswarm", "ggplot2",
  "ggpubr", "ggrepel", "goseq", "here", "httr",
  "httr2", "jsonlite", "knitr", "limma", "lme4",
  "maaslin3", "magrittr", "matrixStats", "microeco", "msigdbr",
  "msqrob2", "org.Hs.eg.db", "patchwork", "phyloseq", "png",
  "purrr", "pwr", "ragg", "readr", "readxl",
  "rlang", "scales", "stringr", "survival", "systemfonts",
  "tibble", "tidyr", "vegan", "vroom")
ver <- vapply(PKGS, function(p) tryCatch(as.character(packageVersion(p)),
                                         error = function(e) NA_character_), "")
write.csv(data.frame(package = PKGS, version = ver),
          file.path(BUNDLE_DIR, "package_versions.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
writeLines(capture.output(sessionInfo()), file.path(BUNDLE_DIR, "sessionInfo.txt"))
if (requireNamespace("renv", quietly = TRUE))
  try(renv::snapshot(lockfile = file.path(BUNDLE_DIR, "renv.lock"),
                     packages = PKGS[!is.na(ver)], prompt = FALSE))

## 4. checksums of everything in the bundle
rel <- setdiff(list.files(BUNDLE_DIR, recursive = TRUE), "MANIFEST_md5.csv")
write.csv(data.frame(file = rel, md5 = unname(tools::md5sum(file.path(BUNDLE_DIR, rel)))),
          file.path(BUNDLE_DIR, "MANIFEST_md5.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
cat("bundle written:", length(rel), "files,",
    round(sum(file.size(file.path(BUNDLE_DIR, rel))) / 1e6, 1), "MB\n")
```

```{r config-load}
## ---- the only lines to edit ------------------------------------------------------
DATA_ROOT  <- Sys.getenv("ICB_DATA_ROOT",  "/Volumes/Extreme Pro")   # raw data, below
BUNDLE_DIR <- Sys.getenv("ICB_BUNDLE_DIR", here::here("input_bundle"))
OUT_DIR    <- Sys.getenv("ICB_OUT_DIR",    here::here("final_run"))
OFFLINE    <- TRUE    # never query Unipept or KEGG; the bundle carries what was used

## ---- the bundle accelerates a run; it does not gate one -------------------------
## The FIRST run has no bundle — it cannot, since the bundle is written from the
## objects a run produces. So the bundle is optional here: when it is absent the
## document builds everything from DATA_ROOT through §1-§5 as it originally did,
## and `export-bundle` is run deliberately at the end to create it for next time.
##
## WHAT THE BUNDLE DOES AND DOES NOT REMOVE. It carries the upstream objects and
## the slow caches, so §0a, §2e and §5c do not have to be rebuilt. It does NOT
## remove the DATA_ROOT dependency: §2b reads the PSM tables, §5b the FASTAs and
## §6a the emapper annotations, all from the raw tree. A bundle-only run is not
## possible and the bundle should not be described as making one so.
## Set ICB_CACHE_DIR to an existing results directory to bring the frozen Unipept
## and KEGG caches across, which is what the bundle would otherwise supply.
## KNITTING SPAWNS A NEW R PROCESS. It does not inherit Sys.setenv() from the
## console, so every ICB_* variable set interactively is invisible here and each
## falls back to its default. Put them in .Renviron at the project root instead,
## which every R process reads — one KEY=value per line, no quotes, no export —
## and restart R. This guard used to fail with "dir.exists(DATA_ROOT) is not
## TRUE", which says nothing about either cause.
if (!dir.exists(DATA_ROOT)) {
  vols <- if (dir.exists("/Volumes")) list.dirs("/Volumes", recursive = FALSE) else character(0)
  near <- vols[agrepl(basename(DATA_ROOT), basename(vols), max.distance = 0.4)]
  stop("raw data root not found:\n  ", DATA_ROOT,
       "\n\nICB_DATA_ROOT is ",
       if (nzchar(Sys.getenv("ICB_DATA_ROOT"))) paste0("set to '", Sys.getenv("ICB_DATA_ROOT"), "'")
       else "NOT SET, so the default above was used",
       ".\n",
       if (length(near)) paste0("\nSimilar volumes are mounted — macOS renames a volume that was not\n",
                                "ejected cleanly:\n  ", paste(near, collapse = "\n  "), "\n") else
       if (length(vols)) paste0("\nMounted volumes:\n  ", paste(vols, collapse = "\n  "), "\n") else "",
       "\nIf you set the ICB_* variables in the console, note that knitting starts a\n",
       "NEW R process that does not inherit them. Put them in .Renviron at the\n",
       "project root and restart R.", call. = FALSE)
}

## The other four paths fail later and one at a time, which wastes a knit each.
## Report all of them here.
.icb_paths <- c(ICB_CACHE_DIR = Sys.getenv("ICB_CACHE_DIR", ""),
                ICB_META_DIR  = Sys.getenv("ICB_META_DIR", ""),
                ICB_MP_STATE  = Sys.getenv("ICB_MP_STATE", ""),
                ICB_REANNOT_DIR = Sys.getenv("ICB_REANNOT_DIR", ""))
.icb_set <- .icb_paths[nzchar(.icb_paths)]
.icb_bad <- .icb_set[!file.exists(.icb_set)]
if (length(.icb_bad))
  stop("these ICB_* paths are set but do not exist:\n  ",
       paste(sprintf("%s = %s", names(.icb_bad), .icb_bad), collapse = "\n  "),
       call. = FALSE)
message("paths OK: DATA_ROOT and ", length(.icb_set), " of 4 optional ICB_* variables set")
dir.create(OUT_DIR, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
FROM_BUNDLE <- file.exists(file.path(BUNDLE_DIR, "inputs.rds"))

if (FROM_BUNDLE) {
  man <- read.csv(file.path(BUNDLE_DIR, "MANIFEST_md5.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  stopifnot(identical(unname(tools::md5sum(file.path(BUNDLE_DIR, man$file))), man$md5))
  B <- readRDS(file.path(BUNDLE_DIR, "inputs.rds"))
  stopifnot(identical(B$bundle_version, 1L))
  list2env(B$objects, envir = environment())
  ## The bundle stays untouched: its files are copied into OUT_DIR, where the
  ## analysis reads its caches and writes its results.
  stopifnot(all(file.copy(list.files(file.path(BUNDLE_DIR, "files"), full.names = TRUE),
                          OUT_DIR, recursive = TRUE, overwrite = TRUE)))
  rm(B, man)
  message("bundle loaded and verified from ", BUNDLE_DIR)
} else {
  message("no bundle at ", BUNDLE_DIR, " — building from DATA_ROOT. Run the\n",
          "`export-bundle` listing at the end of §0b once this finishes, to make\n",
          "the next run reproducible from the bundle alone.")
  CACHE_SRC <- Sys.getenv("ICB_CACHE_DIR", "")
  ## A typo'd cache path was indistinguishable from an unset one: the copy was
  ## skipped in silence and n_peptides.rds never arrived. If it is SET it must
  ## resolve.
  if (nzchar(CACHE_SRC) && !dir.exists(CACHE_SRC))
    stop("ICB_CACHE_DIR is set but does not exist:\n  ", CACHE_SRC,
         "\nFix the path or unset it.", call. = FALSE)
  if (nzchar(CACHE_SRC)) {
    ok <- file.copy(list.files(CACHE_SRC, full.names = TRUE), OUT_DIR,
                    recursive = TRUE, overwrite = TRUE)
    message("copied ", sum(ok), " entries from ", CACHE_SRC, " into ", OUT_DIR)
  } else if (isTRUE(OFFLINE)) {
    warning("OFFLINE is TRUE and ICB_CACHE_DIR is not set: the frozen Unipept and ",
            "KEGG caches must already be under ", OUT_DIR, " or §5 will fail. ",
            "Point ICB_CACHE_DIR at the results directory that holds them.")
  }
}
paths <- list(out_dir = OUT_DIR)
PROJ  <- OUT_DIR
```

## 0c. Session guard

Checked by type and named slot, not by bare `exists()`.

## 0a. Upstream state and design constants {#upstream}

**Restored 23 September 2026, and this is a provenance repair rather than a new
section.** `mp`, `SAMP`, `SAMP_PRIMARY`, `TIER_PRIMARY`, `PARAMS` and
`RESP_LEVELS` are used throughout this document — `RESP_LEVELS` by nine chunks,
`SAMP_PRIMARY` by `qfeatures`, `arm-objects` and `null-prep` — but they were last
*defined* in `analysis_v12.Rmd`. The rewrite at v13 dropped the definitions and
kept the usage, so from v13 to v17 they survived only as live session state. The
consequence is blunt: **this document has never been runnable from a fresh
session**, and every number in it was produced in a session descending from a
v12-era pipeline. `session-guard` below is what caught it.

The code is ported from v12 with its comments, which carry decisions that are not
obvious from the code (the `>= 0` baseline threshold, the exact-then-fallback
Sheba join, the `annot2024` timing leak). Two cautions. `mp` itself is not built
by any document — v12 reads it from a serialised state, and so does this — so the
chain to raw spectra runs through a file, not through code; that is a limitation
to state in the methods, not something this section fixes. And v11 and v12
disagree on `TIER_PRIMARY$K`: v12 adds `"K2a"` and v11 does not. v12's is used
here because it is the later record, and it matters only if a chunk reads `$K` —
protein selection in §6 reads `$R`.

Nothing is rebuilt if it is already present, so a session that still holds the
legacy objects is left alone; the assertions run either way.

```{r upstream-constants}
## The clinical metadata sits OUTSIDE the project tree, so there is no default
## that is right for two machines. The default below is a convention, not a
## location: `Patient_metadata/` under the project root. Set ICB_META_DIR to
## wherever the workbooks actually are -- on the machine this analysis was run
## on, that is a `Patient_metadata` folder under the Sheba project directory.
## The resolver below names the file and the directory it looked in, so an
## unset variable fails with something a reader can act on.
META <- Sys.getenv("ICB_META_DIR", here::here("Patient_metadata"))
## Pittsburgh's clinical CSV is not necessarily beside the Sheba workbooks; it
## defaults to the same directory and is separately overridable.
META_PITT <- Sys.getenv("ICB_META_PITT", META)

## Every metadata read goes through this, so a missing file reports WHICH file
## and WHERE it looked instead of failing inside readxl three calls deeper.
meta_file <- function(dir, name) {
  f <- file.path(dir, name)
  if (!file.exists(f))
    stop("metadata file not found:\n  ", f,
         "\nSet ICB_META_DIR (Sheba workbooks) or ICB_META_PITT (Pittsburgh CSV).",
         call. = FALSE)
  f
}
MP_STATE <- Sys.getenv("ICB_MP_STATE",
              here::here("Results_for_combined_Sheba_Pitt/metaproteomics",
                         "metaproteomics_post14.rds"))
COHORTS     <- c("pitt", "sheba")
RESP_LEVELS <- c("NR", "R")          # NR first: respR is R - NR, the sign every memo uses

## Defined here rather than in §1's `helpers` because the metadata joins below
## run first and every one of them keys on it. `helpers` no longer defines it.
norm_id <- function(x) tolower(gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]", "", as.character(x)))

## USABLE, not merely present. Four separate failures in this session came from
## `exists()` accepting a stale object: `kos` redefined as a function, `stat`
## overwritten by §8b, SAMP built by older code, annot without its peptide
## counts. Every guard in §0a tests CONTENT.
MP_SLOTS_NEEDED <- c("pitt_mat_f", "pitt_annot_use", "sheba_annot_use")
if (!exists("mp") || !all(MP_SLOTS_NEEDED %in% names(mp))) {
  if (exists("mp"))
    message("rebuilding mp: missing slots ",
            paste(setdiff(MP_SLOTS_NEEDED, names(mp)), collapse = ", "))
  if (!file.exists(MP_STATE))
    stop("upstream state not found at ", MP_STATE, ". Set ICB_MP_STATE. Without it ",
         "nothing downstream can be built: no document creates `mp`.")
  mp <- local({ s <- readRDS(MP_STATE); if (!is.null(s$mp)) s$mp else s })
  message("upstream state loaded from ", MP_STATE)
}

## ---- Pittsburgh sample corrections, 13 Oct 2026 -------------------------------
## TMT1_126 is MF0017, annotated under a corrupted name. That relabel is the only
## correction that survives: TMT7_127N and TMT8_126 were both excluded on 13 Oct
## 2026 and both restored the same day, and PITT_RESTORED records why. The arm is
## the full 75 channels / 55 samples.
## The channel table and every Pittsburgh matrix are corrected HERE, once, so everything below
## inherits it. The definitions and their evidence are in pitt_sample_corrections.R.
## A SAMP built before the corrections -- the bundle's, or an earlier session's --
## is removed so that `upstream-samp` rebuilds it from the corrected table.
## ICB_PITT_SENSITIVITY=TMT4_127C additionally drops TMT4_127C (sensitivity run).
source(here::here("pitt_sample_corrections.R"))
mp <- apply_pitt_corrections(mp)
if (exists("SAMP") && pitt_samp_stale(SAMP)) {
  message("SAMP predates the Pittsburgh corrections: rebuilding it")
  rm(SAMP)
  if (exists("SAMP_PRIMARY")) rm(SAMP_PRIMARY)
}
## Sample channels in the corrected matrix, and in the analysed arm after §2's
## plex rule (every dropped channel sits in an analysed plex).
PITT_N_CHANNELS <- 75L - length(pitt_drop_list())
PITT_N_ARM      <- 55L - length(pitt_drop_list())

PARAMS <- list(
  ## design
  min_mixtures           = 3L,     # usable mixtures per protein, WITHIN ARM
  min_mixtures_small_arm = 2L,     # arms with <3 mixtures (sheba_MS3 has 2)
  min_per_arm_mixture    = 2L,     # samples per arm for a mixture to be usable
  min_per_arm_protein    = 2L,     # observations per arm for a protein to use that mixture
  ## evidence tiers
  tier_primary_R         = c("R1", "R2"),
  tier_primary_K         = c("K1", "K2", "K3"),
  tier_coverage_gate     = 0.60,
  ko_profile_gate        = 0.70,
  tier_cell_dominance    = 0.60,
  reality_min_len        = 100L,
  reality_min_peptides   = 2L,
  ## taxonomy
  tax_resolution_cap     = "genus",
  ## inference
  primary_level          = "KO",
  ko_min_proteins        = 3L,
  omnibus_levels         = c("protein", "KO"),
  omnibus_min_features   = 2000L,
  ko_min_features        = 100L,
  n_perm                 = 1000L,
  fdr_method             = "BH",
  fdr_q                  = 0.05,
  ## effect size
  delta_min_MS2          = 0.50,
  delta_min_MS3          = 0.30,
  compression_MS2        = 2.5,
  power_delta_grid       = c(0.10, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75),
  power_pi_grid          = c(0.01, 0.05, 0.10),
  ## estimation
  weight_scheme          = "n_eff",
  weight_efficiency_gate = 0.20,
  meta_model             = "FE",
  estimator_agree_rho    = 0.95,
  estimator_agree_top    = 0.90,
  impute                 = FALSE,
  ## Phase M
  gene_present_min_cov   = 0.5,
  shrinkage_agree_rho    = 0.80)

TIER_PRIMARY <- list(R = PARAMS$tier_primary_R,
                     K = union(PARAMS$tier_primary_K, "K2a"))   # v12; v11 had no K2a

get_mat <- function(cohort, want = c("prefilter", "filtered")) {
  want <- match.arg(want)
  nm <- paste0(cohort, if (want == "prefilter") "_mat" else "_mat_f")
  if (is.null(mp[[nm]])) stop("`", nm, "` absent from the upstream state")
  mp[[nm]]
}
sample_table <- function(cohort, mat = get_mat(cohort, "filtered")) {
  an <- mp[[paste0(cohort, "_annot_use")]]
  tibble::tibble(sample = colnames(mat)) |>
    tidyr::separate(sample, c("Mixture", "Channel"), sep = "_", remove = FALSE) |>
    dplyr::left_join(dplyr::distinct(an, Mixture, Channel, Condition_bin),
                     by = c("Mixture", "Channel")) |>
    dplyr::mutate(resp = factor(Condition_bin, levels = RESP_LEVELS))
}
```

```{r upstream-samp}
## Rebuild when SAMP is missing OR when it lacks a column this section now
## produces. `exists()` alone accepts a stale object built by an older version of
## this code — which is how the previous run reached the diagnostics below with
## no `join_src` column. Test for a USABLE object, not a present one.
## EVERY column this section produces. A column added below but not listed here
## leaves the guard satisfied by a stale SAMP and the rebuild silently skipped —
## which is exactly what happened when n_chan was introduced.
SAMP_COLS <- c("sample", "resp", "arm", "bio", "cohort", "is_baseline",
               "join_src", "n_chan", "days_before", "src", "best", "protocol",
               "probe_join", "resp_pfs12")
if (!exists("SAMP") || !all(SAMP_COLS %in% names(SAMP))) {
  if (exists("SAMP"))
    message("rebuilding SAMP: missing ", paste(setdiff(SAMP_COLS, names(SAMP)), collapse = ", "))
  sheba_ann <- readxl::read_excel(meta_file(META, "Melanoma_Sheba_2024_annotation.xlsx")) |>
    rlang::set_names(c("sample", "index1", "index2", "pfs", "tmt")) |>
    dplyr::transmute(probe = norm_id(sample),
                     resp_meta = suppressWarnings(as.integer(pfs)) == 1L,
                     src = "annot2024") |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(resp_meta))        # drops the legend rows at the sheet foot
  sheba_pre <- readxl::read_excel(
      meta_file(META, "all patients with stool before tx deidentified.xlsx")) |>
    dplyr::transmute(probe = norm_id(sub("\\s*\\(old\\)", "", `Name/number of probe`)),
                     resp_meta   = `best response` %in% c("Complete response", "Partial response"),
                     days_before = `days sampling before first treatment`,
                     protocol    = Protocol,
                     best        = `best response`,
                     src         = "pre_tx")
  sheba_all <- dplyr::bind_rows(sheba_ann, sheba_pre) |>
    dplyr::distinct(probe, .keep_all = TRUE)
  ## `Response_PFS_12` occurs MORE THAN ONCE in this CSV, so name repair makes
  ## Response_PFS_12...7 and ...17. v12 took the first silently. If the two
  ## disagree that is a choice between two response definitions and must not be
  ## made by column order — so compare them and stop if they differ.
  pitt_raw <- readr::read_csv(meta_file(META_PITT, "Lior_UPF_data.csv"),
                              show_col_types = FALSE, name_repair = "unique")
  pfs_cols <- grep("^Response_PFS_12", names(pitt_raw), value = TRUE)
  if (!length(pfs_cols)) stop("no Response_PFS_12 column in Lior_UPF_data.csv")
  if (length(pfs_cols) > 1) {
    same <- vapply(pfs_cols[-1], function(cc)
      identical(as.character(pitt_raw[[pfs_cols[1]]]), as.character(pitt_raw[[cc]])), TRUE)
    message("Response_PFS_12 appears ", length(pfs_cols), " times (",
            paste(pfs_cols, collapse = ", "), "); identical to the first: ",
            paste(same, collapse = ", "))
    if (!all(same)) {
      ## MEASURED 23 Sep 2026: they disagree. This does NOT affect any result —
      ## the analysis response is Condition_bin from the upstream state, and
      ## `resp_pfs12` is carried into SAMP but read by nothing. It is recorded
      ## rather than resolved, because PFS-12 is the endpoint a cross-cohort
      ## harmonisation would use, and then the choice becomes load-bearing.
      warning("the duplicated Response_PFS_12 columns DISAGREE. Nothing downstream ",
              "reads resp_pfs12 today, so the run continues; BOTH are kept as ",
              "resp_pfs12_1 / resp_pfs12_2. Set ICB_PFS_COL before using PFS as an ",
              "endpoint.", call. = FALSE)
      print(table(pitt_raw[[pfs_cols[1]]], pitt_raw[[pfs_cols[2]]],
                  dnn = pfs_cols[1:2], useNA = "ifany"))
    }
  }
  PFS_COL <- Sys.getenv("ICB_PFS_COL", pfs_cols[1])
  ## Keep every duplicate, named by its position in the sheet, so the discarded
  ## one is still inspectable and no information is lost to a rename.
  pitt_raw <- pitt_raw |>
    dplyr::rename_with(~ paste0("resp_pfs12_", seq_along(pfs_cols)), dplyr::all_of(pfs_cols))
  PFS_KEEP <- paste0("resp_pfs12_", match(PFS_COL, pfs_cols))
  pitt_meta <- pitt_raw |>
    dplyr::mutate(resp_pfs12 = .data[[PFS_KEEP]]) |>
    dplyr::transmute(MF_ID = norm_id(MF_ID), resp_pfs12,
                     dplyr::across(dplyr::starts_with("resp_pfs12_")),
                     timepoint = Timepoint_discrete, tp_days = Timepoint_days,
                     rx = Rx, cohort_pd = Pitts_cohort, upf = PCT_NOVA4,
                     irae = suppressWarnings(as.integer(dplyr::na_if(irAE_dichot, "N_A"))),
                     dplyr::across(c(Rx_start, Prog_date, Death_date, LFU_date),
                       ~ suppressWarnings(as.Date(dplyr::na_if(.x, "N_A"),
                           tryFormats = c("%m/%d/%y", "%m/%d/%Y", "%Y-%m-%d")))))

  SAMP <- purrr::map_dfr(COHORTS, function(ch) {
    mat <- get_mat(ch, "filtered")
    an  <- mp[[paste0(ch, "_annot_use")]] |> dplyr::distinct(Mixture, Channel, BioReplicate)
    sample_table(ch, mat) |>
      dplyr::left_join(an, by = c("Mixture", "Channel")) |>
      dplyr::mutate(cohort = ch, bio = norm_id(BioReplicate))
  }) |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(resp)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(probe_join = sub("[ab]$", "", bio))

  ## Sheba metadata: EXACT match first, suffix-stripped only as fallback.
  ## `sheba_ann` holds 94a and 94b as SEPARATE samples (two treatment lines,
  ## different outcomes) while `sheba_pre` holds a single "94". Stripping
  ## the suffix unconditionally matched 94a to the wrong record.
  SAMP <- SAMP |>
    dplyr::left_join(sheba_all, by = c("bio" = "probe")) |>
    dplyr::left_join(sheba_all |> dplyr::rename_with(~ paste0(.x, "_fb"), -probe),
                     by = c("probe_join" = "probe")) |>
    ## `.data[[...]]`, not get(): get() resolves in the calling frame rather than
    ## the data mask, so under current dplyr it does not reliably return the _fb
    ## column. That is almost certainly why v12's counts are exact-match-only —
    ## the fallback it appears to apply may never have fired. RECORD which join
    ## won, per row, rather than leaving that to be inferred later.
    dplyr::mutate(join_src = dplyr::case_when(
                    !is.na(src)    ~ "exact",
                    !is.na(src_fb) ~ "fallback",
                    TRUE           ~ NA_character_)) |>
    ## Written out rather than across(): `.data[[cur_column()]]` is not a
    ## supported combination — the pronoun and cur_column() resolve at different
    ## times — and the across() form is what silently dropped the fallback in the
    ## first place. Five explicit lines cannot fail quietly.
    dplyr::mutate(resp_meta   = dplyr::coalesce(resp_meta,   resp_meta_fb),
                  days_before = dplyr::coalesce(days_before, days_before_fb),
                  best        = dplyr::coalesce(best,        best_fb),
                  protocol    = dplyr::coalesce(protocol,    protocol_fb),
                  src         = dplyr::coalesce(src,         src_fb)) |>
    dplyr::select(-dplyr::ends_with("_fb")) |>
    dplyr::left_join(pitt_meta, by = c("bio" = "MF_ID"))

  ## Arms by SAMPLING DESIGN where it is known. Mixture membership is a PROXY:
  ## 94a sits in mixture 5 but was collected 14 days BEFORE treatment.
  SAMP <- SAMP |>
    ## `annot2024` has no timing column, so any days_before on those rows is a
    ## leak from the suffix-stripped fallback join — that is what put 94a in the
    ## baseline arm on the first attempt.
    ## !is.na(src) guard: if_else returns NA when the CONDITION is NA, so a row
    ## whose src failed to join had its days_before wiped and fell through to the
    ## mixture fallback.
    ## channels per patient, needed by the baseline rule below
    dplyr::group_by(cohort, bio) |> dplyr::mutate(n_chan = dplyr::n()) |> dplyr::ungroup() |>
    dplyr::mutate(days_before = dplyr::if_else(!is.na(src) & src == "annot2024",
                                               NA_real_, days_before),
      ## >= 0, NOT > 0. Four samples (122a, 141, 182, 177) were collected on the
      ## day treatment started, which is baseline in any practical sense; a strict
      ## > 0 threshold cut sheba_base from 12 to 9.
      ## TIMING IS PER PATIENT, NOT PER SAMPLE. `sheba_pre` is keyed on probe and
      ## records when that patient's PRE-TREATMENT stool was taken. One probe
      ## contributed TWO channels — 1_131N in the baseline-dominated mixture 1 and
      ## 3_128C in on-treatment mixture 3 — so applying one days_before to both
      ## marked the on-treatment sample as baseline. Mixture 3 then held 1 NR / 8 R,
      ## failed the 2/2 plex rule, and the whole plex dropped: OS went 29 -> 19.
      ## For a patient with more than one channel, mixture membership is the better
      ## evidence of which sample is which; timing overrides it only when the
      ## patient contributed a single sample, where the two cannot disagree.
      ## (v12's fallback happened to be right here because it had no timing for 96.)
      is_baseline = dplyr::case_when(
        cohort != "sheba"     ~ FALSE,
        n_chan > 1            ~ Mixture %in% c("1", "2"),
        !is.na(days_before)   ~ days_before >= 0,
        TRUE                  ~ Mixture %in% c("1", "2")),
      arm = dplyr::case_when(cohort == "pitt" ~ "pitt_ontx",
                             is_baseline      ~ "sheba_base",
                             TRUE             ~ "sheba_ontx"))
}
SAMP_PRIMARY <- dplyr::filter(SAMP, bio != "11")

## ---- verification. These are the numbers the restoration has to reproduce ----
stopifnot(identical(dim(mp$pitt_mat_f), c(1857L, PITT_N_CHANNELS)))   # 75 before 13 Oct 2026
stopifnot(is.character(RESP_LEVELS), identical(RESP_LEVELS, c("NR", "R")))
stopifnot(all(c("sample", "resp", "arm", "bio", "cohort") %in% names(SAMP)))
print(dplyr::count(SAMP, arm))
cat(sprintf("SAMP %d rows, SAMP_PRIMARY %d; Pittsburgh %d\n",
            nrow(SAMP), nrow(SAMP_PRIMARY), sum(SAMP_PRIMARY$cohort == "pitt")))
## EXPECTED, and RECONCILED with v12 on 23 Sep 2026.
##   pitt_ontx  75  — SAMP is pre-filter; 55 is OP$d after §2's plex rule
##   sheba_base 12, sheba_ontx 30  — matching v12 once per-patient timing is
##               not applied to a patient with two samples (see the rule above)
## v12 recorded 12/30 and this is the same data, not a discrepancy. Sheba has 42
## channels from 41 patients: sample 96 occupies TWO channels (1_131N and 3_128C,
## both NR, both pre_tx, both days_before = 0). v12 had no timing for 96 — its
## note calls it "1 via fallback" — so its mixture-3 channel fell to
## is_baseline = FALSE and counted as on-treatment. Here both channels match
## sheba_pre exactly and both are baseline under v12's own documented rule
## (">= 0, NOT > 0": collected on the day treatment started is baseline). The
## timing appeared because sheba_all keeps the first hit per probe and 96 now
## resolves to pre_tx, so the metadata workbooks have been updated since v12.
## That probe remains TWO channels, one per arm, which is what it should be: a patient
## sampled before and during treatment contributes to both. What must not happen
## is one patient occupying two channels of the SAME arm — the §0a duplicate
## check reports that case, and the superseded episode-level run was rejected for
## it (a different probe).
stopifnot(all(SAMP_COLS %in% names(SAMP)))
sheba_chk <- SAMP |> dplyr::filter(cohort == "sheba") |>
  dplyr::select(bio, Mixture, src, join_src, days_before, is_baseline, arm)
print(dplyr::count(sheba_chk, Mixture, is_baseline, has_days = !is.na(days_before)))
print(dplyr::count(sheba_chk, join_src))
## Any sample whose timing came from the SUFFIX-STRIPPED join is the case the
## v12 comment warns about: 94a and 94b are different treatment lines with
## different outcomes, and the base probe "94" is a third record. Timing taken
## from a fallback match on a suffixed id is not that sample's timing.
print(sheba_chk |> dplyr::filter(join_src == "fallback" | grepl("[ab]$", bio)))
print(sheba_chk |> dplyr::filter(Mixture == "3", is_baseline))   # the 13th baseline

## ---- one patient, more than one channel --------------------------------------
## MEASURED 23 Sep 2026: one probe sits in the Sheba annotation TWICE — mixture 3
## channel 128C and mixture 1 channel 131N, in the SAME response group — so SAMP
## carries a row for each. This is the hazard behind the superseded episode-level
## Sheba run, which counted one probe twice; it is checked here rather than
## discovered later.
## A repeated patient is not necessarily an error (a genuine repeat sample is
## legitimate), but it must be a decision, not an accident: any analysis treating
## rows as independent patients has to collapse or drop these first.
dup_bio <- SAMP |> dplyr::count(cohort, bio) |> dplyr::filter(n > 1)
if (nrow(dup_bio)) {
  message(nrow(dup_bio), " patient id(s) appear in more than one channel:")
  print(SAMP |> dplyr::semi_join(dup_bio, by = c("cohort", "bio")) |>
          dplyr::select(cohort, bio, Mixture, Channel, resp, days_before,
                        is_baseline, arm) |>
          dplyr::arrange(cohort, bio, Mixture))
  ## Do they at least agree on arm and response? Disagreement means the two rows
  ## are being treated as different things, which no downstream code expects.
  incons <- SAMP |> dplyr::semi_join(dup_bio, by = c("cohort", "bio")) |>
    dplyr::group_by(cohort, bio) |>
    dplyr::summarise(arms = dplyr::n_distinct(arm),
                     resps = dplyr::n_distinct(as.character(resp)), .groups = "drop") |>
    dplyr::filter(arms > 1 | resps > 1)
  if (nrow(incons)) {
    print(incons)
    warning("a repeated patient id carries DIFFERENT arm or response across its ",
            "channels. Downstream code treats rows as samples, so this changes ",
            "arm counts and any patient-level n. Resolve before reading results.",
            call. = FALSE)
  }
}
```

## 0d. Annotation schema

The archived table carries two schemas. Normalise by **adding** what is
missing, never by renaming.

```{r upstream-annot}
## `annot` is the third object no document builds — `annot-schema` below
## NORMALISES it (adds the missing half of the dual schema) and would fail on an
## absent object, which is what it just did. Built here from the metaannot
## exports, as v12 did.
ANNOT_PITT  <- Sys.getenv("ICB_ANNOT_PITT",
                          here::here("metaannot_export/pitt_annotation_final.tsv"))
ANNOT_SHEBA <- Sys.getenv("ICB_ANNOT_SHEBA",
                          here::here("metaannot_export/sheba_annotation_final.tsv"))
## protein ids carry trailing descriptions and ';'-separated groups; keep the
## first token only. Defined here because §0a runs before `helpers`.
norm_pid <- function(x) trimws(sub("\\s.*$", "", sub(";.*$", "", as.character(x))))

## Rebuild when annot is absent OR lacks n_peptides — the column the tier gates
## depend on. `exists()` alone left a previously built annot in place and the
## join below never ran.
if (!exists("annot") || !"n_peptides" %in% names(annot)) {
  if (exists("annot")) message("rebuilding annot: no n_peptides column")
  af <- c(pitt = ANNOT_PITT, sheba = ANNOT_SHEBA)
  gone <- af[!file.exists(af)]
  if (length(gone))
    stop("metaannot export not found:\n  ", paste(gone, collapse = "\n  "),
         "\nSet ICB_ANNOT_PITT / ICB_ANNOT_SHEBA.", call. = FALSE)
  annot_raw <- purrr::map(af, ~ readr::read_tsv(.x, show_col_types = FALSE,
                                                guess_max = Inf))
  ## guess_max = Inf and this assertion together: a column typed from the first
  ## 1000 rows silently truncates the rest.
  stopifnot("column-type guessing failed; inspect problems()" =
              all(purrr::map_int(annot_raw, ~ nrow(readr::problems(.x))) == 0))
  annot <- purrr::imap_dfr(annot_raw, function(a, ch)
    dplyr::mutate(a, cohort = ch, protein = norm_pid(protein_id)))

  ## n_peptides comes from F0, as a cached file in the output directory — not
  ## from the metaannot export. Without it the peptide-count reality gate cannot
  ## be applied, so say so rather than proceeding with a silent NA column.
  np <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "n_peptides.rds")
  if (file.exists(np)) {
    annot <- dplyr::left_join(annot, readRDS(np), by = c("cohort", "protein"))
    ## A left_join adds the column whether or not anything MATCHED. If the ids in
    ## n_peptides.rds were normalised differently, every value is NA and the
    ## peptide gate is inactive while looking present. Coverage, not presence.
    cov <- annot |> dplyr::group_by(cohort) |>
      dplyr::summarise(matched = mean(!is.na(n_peptides)), .groups = "drop")
    print(cov)
    if (any(cov$matched < 0.5))
      stop("n_peptides matched fewer than half the proteins in at least one ",
           "cohort — the join keys disagree, so the peptide gate would be ",
           "silently inactive. Check how protein ids were normalised when ",
           "n_peptides.rds was written.", call. = FALSE)
  } else {
    ## STOP, not warn. Without this column pep_ok is NA for every protein,
    ## PARAMS$reality_min_peptides drops out of the tier gates, and the protein
    ## universe differs from the recorded run — which changes every set size and
    ## every NES, with nothing downstream reporting it. An earlier version of
    ## this chunk warned and continued; that was wrong.
    stop("n_peptides.rds not found in ", paths$out_dir, ".\n",
         "PARAMS$reality_min_peptides cannot be applied without it and the ",
         "protein universe would silently differ from the recorded analysis.\n",
         "Set ICB_CACHE_DIR to the results directory that holds it, or locate it ",
         "with list.files(<cache>, \"n_peptides\", recursive = TRUE).", call. = FALSE)
  }
  message("annot built: ", nrow(annot), " rows, ",
          paste(names(af), collapse = " + "))
}
stopifnot(is.data.frame(annot), "cohort" %in% names(annot),
          any(c("protein", "protein_id") %in% names(annot)))
```

```{r upstream-tiers}
## The evidence tiers — the FIFTH upstream step v13 dropped, and the one that
## fails most quietly. §6a builds the analysis universe with
## `annot$R %in% TIER_PRIMARY$R`; with no R column that is `NULL %in% ...`, which
## is logical(0), so the universe comes back EMPTY and every set is empty — no
## error, no warning, just zero. Ported from analysis_v12.Rmd's `tiers` chunk
## with its measured notes, applied to the annot §0a already built.
has_any <- function(x) !is.na(x) & nzchar(as.character(x)) & as.character(x) != "-"
is_true <- function(x) !is.na(x) & as.logical(x)

if (!"R" %in% names(annot)) {
  needed <- c("pfam_accs", "ncbifam_accs", "interpro_ipr", "duf_only",
              "small_protein", "n_peptides")
  gone <- setdiff(needed, names(annot))
  if (length(gone))
    stop("cannot assign evidence tiers: annot lacks ", paste(gone, collapse = ", "),
         ".\nThe R axis decides the analysis universe, so this must not be skipped.",
         call. = FALSE)
  ## Measured 15 Sep 2026 on the real export: has_profile_hit is FALSE for all
  ## 10,576 Pittsburgh proteins, so it is unusable and excluded from every tier.
  if ("has_profile_hit" %in% names(annot))
    stopifnot("has_profile_hit is uniformly FALSE; do not use it" =
                !any(is_true(annot$has_profile_hit)))

  ## Axis R: protein reality, from metaannot's own flags. `small_protein` is the
  ## tool's criterion rather than a hand-set length rule; `duf_only` separates
  ## "has a domain" from "has an INFORMATIVE domain".
  annot <- annot |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      dom_any  = has_any(pfam_accs) | has_any(ncbifam_accs) | has_any(interpro_ipr),
      dom_info = dom_any & !is_true(duf_only),
      ## Median n_peptides is 2 (Pitt) and 1 (Sheba); 49.0% / 63.5% are identified
      ## on a SINGLE peptide by design, so pep_ok caps R1+R2 at ~51% / ~36%
      ## before any other criterion.
      pep_ok   = !is.na(n_peptides) & n_peptides >= PARAMS$reality_min_peptides,
      len_ok   = !is_true(small_protein),
      R = dplyr::case_when(
        pep_ok &  len_ok &  dom_info ~ "R1",
        pep_ok & (len_ok |  dom_any) ~ "R2",
        !pep_ok & len_ok &  dom_info ~ "R3",
        TRUE                         ~ "R0"))

  ## Axis K prep. ko_source carries eggNOG/KOfam concordance directly; KOfam's
  ## adaptive-threshold flag is NOT exported, so K1 is unreachable and K1/K2
  ## collapse — five levels, not six.
  if (all(c("ko_source", "ko", "kofam_ko") %in% names(annot))) {
    annot <- annot |>
      dplyr::mutate(
        ko_egg = dplyr::if_else(ko_source %in% c("both", "eggnog"),
                                sub("^ko:", "", sub(",.*$", "", ko)), NA_character_),
        ko_kof = dplyr::if_else(ko_source %in% c("both", "kofam"),
                                sub(",.*$", "", kofam_ko), NA_character_),
        ## a FUNCTIONAL source, not merely any hit
        func_src = (has_any(interpro_ipr) & is_true(interpro_informative)) |
                   (has_any(ncbifam_accs) & !is_true(ncbifam_uninformative)) |
                   has_any(dbcan_hits) | has_any(merops_hit))
    if (!"ko_primary" %in% names(annot))
      annot <- dplyr::mutate(annot, ko_primary = dplyr::coalesce(ko_egg, ko_kof))
  } else {
    warning("annot lacks ko_source/ko/kofam_ko: the K axis is not assigned.",
            call. = FALSE)
  }
  message("evidence tiers assigned")
}
print(table(annot$cohort, annot$R))
if ("bin" %in% names(annot)) print(table(annot$cohort, annot$bin))
## MEASURED 23 Sep 2026:
##   pitt   R0 1,182  R1 4,478  R2 792  R3 4,124   -> R1+R2 = 5,270 of 10,576 (49.8%)
##   sheba  R0 1,068  R1 1,973  R2 411  R3 3,373   -> R1+R2 = 2,384 of  6,825 (34.9%)
## v12 predicted pep_ok would cap R1+R2 near 51% (Pitt) and 36% (Sheba) because
## half the proteins are identified on a single peptide; 49.8% and 34.9% land
## there, which is an independent check that this port computes the same axis.
##
## bin totals match the annot row counts exactly (10,576 and 6,825), so no
## protein drops out of the tier assignment:
##   pitt   ko_pathway 5,897 | ko_orphan 2,085 | annotated_no_ko 1,662 |
##          duf_only 152 | structure_only 35 | dark 745
##   sheba  3,990 | 1,121 | 1,083 | 61 | 14 | 556
## The universe §6a builds is annot$R %in% c("R1","R2"); if the R1+R2 total is
## zero or implausibly small, STOP — every downstream set derives from it.
stopifnot(sum(annot$R %in% TIER_PRIMARY$R) > 1000)
```

```{r annot-schema}
## The archived annot carries BOTH schemas — `protein_id` AND `protein`,
## plus `ko` AND `ko_primary`. Renaming `protein_id` blind fails with
## "Names must be unique", because `protein` already exists.
##
## Normalise by ADDING what is missing, never by renaming blind.
if (!"protein" %in% names(annot) && "protein_id" %in% names(annot))
  annot <- dplyr::rename(annot, protein = protein_id)
if (!"ko_primary" %in% names(annot) && "ko" %in% names(annot))
  annot <- dplyr::mutate(annot, ko_primary = sub("^ko:", "", sub(",.*$", "", ko)))

## Drop the duplicate only after confirming it IS a duplicate.
if (all(c("protein_id","protein") %in% names(annot))) {
  stopifnot(identical(annot$protein_id, annot$protein))
  annot <- dplyr::select(annot, -protein_id)
}

stopifnot(all(c("protein","cohort","cog_cat","ko_primary") %in% names(annot)),
          !anyDuplicated(names(annot)))
c(rows = nrow(annot), cols = ncol(annot))        # 17,401 for the full table
table(annot$cohort)                              # pitt 10,576 / sheba 6,825
```

**The guard runs here, not before §1.** It checks `annot`, which `annot-schema` builds immediately above; run earlier it fails on an object the document is about to create. Everything else it checks now comes from §0a.

```{r session-guard}
## Every external object this document reads, checked by name and by slot.
need_obj <- c("mp", "annot", "SAMP", "SAMP_PRIMARY", "TIER_PRIMARY", "paths",
              "PARAMS", "RESP_LEVELS", "PROJ")
miss <- need_obj[!vapply(need_obj, exists, logical(1))]
if (length(miss)) stop("missing from session: ", paste(miss, collapse = ", "))

## and the named slots, which a bare exists() does not reach
need_slot <- list(
  paths  = c("out_dir"),
  PARAMS = c("min_per_arm_protein"),
  mp     = c("pitt_mat_f", "pitt_annot_use", "sheba_annot_use",
             "pitt_pw_map_obs", "host_state"))
for (o in names(need_slot)) {
  m <- setdiff(need_slot[[o]], names(get(o)))
  if (length(m)) stop(o, " missing slots: ", paste(m, collapse = ", "))
}
stopifnot(is.character(RESP_LEVELS), length(RESP_LEVELS) == 2)
stopifnot(identical(dim(mp$pitt_mat_f), c(1857L, PITT_N_CHANNELS)))   # 75 before 13 Oct 2026
stopifnot(
  all(c("protein_id", "cohort", "cog_cat", "ko") %in% names(annot)) ||
  all(c("protein",    "cohort", "cog_cat", "ko_primary") %in% names(annot))
)
## Shape and names are not enough: the run that prompted this check had the
## right row count and no n_peptides column at all.
if (!"n_peptides" %in% names(annot))
  stop("annot has no n_peptides column — the peptide-count gate is inactive ",
       "and the protein universe will not match the recorded analysis.", call. = FALSE)
if (mean(!is.na(annot$n_peptides)) < 0.5)
  stop("n_peptides is present but NA for most proteins: the gate is inactive.",
       call. = FALSE)
cat(sprintf("session OK — annot: %d rows, n_peptides on %.0f%% of proteins\n",
            nrow(annot), 100 * mean(!is.na(annot$n_peptides))))
```

# 1. Setup

## 1a. Paths, search databases, constants

The three FASTAs are the databases the searches used. Identity is verified by
**sequence-ID prefix**, not filename: all three Sheba candidates open with the
same human contaminant block, so reading the first header identifies the wrong
file. Cached per machine.

```{r constants}
PRIMARY_LEVEL <- "protein"     # the analysis unit throughout
CROSS_COHORT  <- FALSE         # the two assemblies share no protein IDs
N_PERM        <- 1000L         # draws per within-plex null

## ---- THE SEARCH DATABASES — CANONICAL, DO NOT RE-DERIVE -------------------
## The FASTAs the searches actually used. Canonical: not re-derived by
## globbing the database tree, where near-namesakes exist.
## For Pittsburgh the distinction matters: `gut_meta.faa` is the raw
## Prokka output; `..._90_removed_gaps.faa` is the 90%-clustered, gap-removed
## version that was SEARCHED. A count taken from the raw file (1,691,432
## OIDECCNN headers) describes the wrong database.
DB <- c(
  pitt   = file.path(DATA_ROOT, "Proteomic_databases/ICB_melanoma_Pittsbourgh/prokka_gut_meta/prokka_ICB_Pittsbourgh_90_removed_gaps.faa"),
  sheba1 = file.path(DATA_ROOT, "Proteomic_databases/ICB_melanoma_Sheba/ICB_study_matched_metagenome_1_2/ICB_study_matched_metagenome.fasta"),
  sheba2 = file.path(DATA_ROOT, "Proteomic_databases/ICB_melanoma_Sheba/ICB_study_matched_metagenome_3_4_5/ICB_3_4_5_proteome.fasta"))
stopifnot(all(file.exists(DB)))

## VERIFY BY PREFIX, not by filename — all three Sheba candidates begin with the
## human contaminant block, so reading header 1 identifies the wrong thing.
## Run ONCE per machine, not per session; cache the result.
DBCHK <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "DB_prefix_counts.rds")
if (!file.exists(DBCHK)) {
  saveRDS(purrr::imap_dfr(DB, function(f, nm) {
    h <- system(paste0("grep '^>' '", f, "' | sed 's/^>\\([A-Z]\\{8\\}\\)_.*/\\1/'"),
                intern = TRUE)
    tibble::tibble(db = nm, n = length(h),
                   OIDECCNN = sum(h == "OIDECCNN"),
                   KMMIBAFL = sum(h == "KMMIBAFL"),
                   PPAAKGPG = sum(h == "PPAAKGPG"),
                   other = sum(!h %in% c("OIDECCNN","KMMIBAFL","PPAAKGPG")))
  }), DBCHK)
}
readRDS(DBCHK)
```

## 1b. Helpers {#helpers}

Identity normalisation; arm and mixture selection with its sample-count guard;
four denominators on the log2 protein matrix; the `msqrob2TMT` fit; both
`limma` specifications; set membership; the frozen KO lists.

**The two frozen sets.** `RIBO_KO` (54) and `CHAPERONE_KO` (19) are literal
lists, never re-derived from either cohort's data — a pattern over KO numbers
admits non-ribosomal KOs.

```{r helpers}
## ---- identity ---------------------------------------------------------------
## norm_id moved to §0a's `upstream-constants`: the metadata joins there run
## before this chunk and cannot wait for it. Defined once, there, not here.
strip_old <- function(x) norm_id(sub("\\s*\\(old\\)\\s*$", "", as.character(x)))

## ---- arm / mixture selection -------------------------------------------------
## `arm_name`, NOT `a`: a global `a` (the PSM matrix) inside dplyr's data mask
## recycles against the `arm` column and silently drops a plex. Hence:
##   - formal renamed to `arm_name`, so no global can shadow it
##   - !!arm_name forces evaluation OUTSIDE the data mask
##   - a row-count assertion is built in
arm_mix_v13 <- function(arm_name, expect_n = NULL) {
  stopifnot(is.character(arm_name), length(arm_name) == 1)
  sub <- SAMP_PRIMARY |> dplyr::filter(arm == !!arm_name)
  if (!is.null(expect_n) && nrow(sub) != expect_n)
    stop("arm '", arm_name, "' has ", nrow(sub), " samples, expected ", expect_n)
  sub |>
    dplyr::count(Mixture, resp) |>
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = resp, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
    ## The NR >= 2 / R >= 2 plex rule is a literal 2/2, the value behind every
    ## reported result. TIER_PRIMARY holds identifiability tier names, not plex
    ## thresholds, so it is not a parameter source here.
    dplyr::filter(NR >= 2, R >= 2) |>
    dplyr::pull(Mixture)
}

## 55 after the NR>=2/R>=2 plex rule (TMT2 at 9 NR/1 R and TMT5 at 0 NR/10 R are dropped).
stopifnot(length(arm_mix_v13("pitt_ontx", expect_n = PITT_N_CHANNELS)) == 6L)   # 75 before 13 Oct 2026

## ---- denominator choice ------------------------------------------------------
## ALDEx2's four denominators, implemented directly on the log2 protein matrix.
## ALDEx2 itself expects COUNTS and does Dirichlet Monte-Carlo sampling; forcing
## summarised intensities into it would misrepresent the uncertainty model. The
## denominator LOGIC transfers; the sampling does not.
pick_denom <- function(ap, denom = c("all", "iqlr", "lvha", "median")) {
  denom <- match.arg(denom)
  clr <- sweep(ap, 2, colMeans(ap, na.rm = TRUE), "-")
  v   <- apply(clr, 1, var, na.rm = TRUE)
  ab  <- rowMeans(ap, na.rm = TRUE)
  switch(denom,
    all    = seq_len(nrow(ap)),
    ## features with CLR variance in the interquartile range
    iqlr   = which(v >= quantile(v, .25, na.rm = TRUE) &
                   v <= quantile(v, .75, na.rm = TRUE)),
    ## low variance AND high abundance — "similar to the features that would be
    ## chosen as internal standards in qPCR"; ALDEx2's docs say metagenomic and
    ## metatranscriptomic datasets benefit from this choice
    lvha   = which(v <= quantile(v, .25, na.rm = TRUE) &
                   ab >= quantile(ab, .75, na.rm = TRUE)),
    median = seq_len(nrow(ap)))
}

## DIAGNOSTIC — run BEFORE choosing. If every candidate denominator carries the
## same shift, no internal reference can anchor the analysis and the problem is
## identifiability, not denominator choice.
denom_check <- function(ap, fc) {
  map_dfr(c("all", "iqlr", "lvha"), function(dn) {
    idx <- pick_denom(ap, dn)
    tibble(denom = dn, n = length(idx),
           median_effect = median(fc[idx], na.rm = TRUE))
  })
}

## ---- the model ---------------------------------------------------------------
## EVERY parameterisation that might be compared MUST be in the signature.
## An argument missing from it is swallowed by `...` and silently ignored, so two
## 'different' fits come back identical (rho = 1). Hence the explicit arguments
## and the assertion pattern below.
fit_arm <- function(q, keep_mix, label,
                    min_psm = 2L, min_per_arm = PARAMS$min_per_arm_protein,
                    min_mix = 2L, summariser = MsCoreUtils::robustSummary,
                    formula = ~ resp + (1 | Mixture), denom = "all",
                    robust = TRUE) {

  keep <- colData(q)$Mixture %in% keep_mix &
          !colData(q)$is_norm & !colData(q)$excluded & !is.na(colData(q)$resp)
  qs <- q[, keep, ]
  ## QFeatures keeps ORIGINAL factor levels on subset — drop them or
  ## model.matrix fails on levels with zero samples.
  colData(qs)$Mixture <- droplevels(factor(colData(qs)$Mixture))
  colData(qs)$resp    <- droplevels(factor(colData(qs)$resp))
  stopifnot(nlevels(colData(qs)$resp) == 2, nlevels(colData(qs)$Mixture) >= 2)

  ## FILTER 1 — PSMs per protein, within this arm's retained columns.
  np <- rowsum(as.integer(rowSums(!is.na(assay(qs, "psmsLog"))) > 0),
               rowData(qs[["psmsLog"]])$Protein)
  qs <- qs[rowData(qs[["psmsLog"]])$Protein %in% rownames(np)[np[, 1] >= min_psm], , ]

  ## Muffle robustSummary's two known warnings. `rlm` objects to `na.rm` passed
  ## through the dots, and fails to converge in 20 IRLS steps for 7.6% of
  ## proteins — together ~17,000 conditions per call, which R retains and which
  ## measurably slows a permutation loop.
  ##
  ## TWO SEPARATE HANDLERS, not one wrapping the function. Each muffles only
  ## messages that have been characterised; anything new stays visible.
  qs <- withCallingHandlers(
    aggregateFeatures(qs, i = "psmsLog", fcol = "Protein", name = "protein",
                      fun = summariser, na.rm = TRUE),
    warning = function(w) {
      m <- conditionMessage(w)
      if (grepl("do not match|failed to converge", m)) invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
    })

  ## FILTER 2 — identifiability for the response model. Same rule as
  a   <- assay(qs, "protein"); cdq <- colData(qs)
  nmx <- apply(!is.na(a), 1, function(z) dplyr::n_distinct(cdq$Mixture[z]))
  ok  <- rowSums(!is.na(a[, cdq$resp == "R",  drop = FALSE])) >= min_per_arm &
         rowSums(!is.na(a[, cdq$resp == "NR", drop = FALSE])) >= min_per_arm &
         nmx >= min_mix
  message(label, ": ", sum(ok), " of ", nrow(a), " estimable")
  qs <- qs[ok, , ]

  ## OPTIONAL re-referencing (the denominators, §1b). "all" leaves the §3a normalisation in place.
  if (denom != "all") {
    ap  <- assay(qs, "protein")
    idx <- pick_denom(ap, denom)
    assay(qs[["protein"]]) <- sweep(ap, 2, colMeans(ap[idx, , drop = FALSE],
                                                    na.rm = TRUE), "-")
  }

  ## (1 | Channel) is NOT included: every (Mixture, Channel) cell is exactly 1,
  ## so channel is perfectly nested in sample.
  ##
  ## Singular-fit warnings muffled. They have been characterised: the
  ## random-intercept and fixed-effect
  ## parameterisations agree at rho = 0.981 on logFC across the 3,213 commonly
  ## fitted proteins, so a zero mixture variance is not distorting the estimate.
  ## ~17k such conditions per permutation iteration would otherwise slow the loop.
  ##
  ## NOT wrapped around the whole function: rank-deficiency and hypothesisTest
  ## warnings are uncharacterised and stay visible.
  qs <- withCallingHandlers(
    msqrob(qs, i = "protein", formula = formula, ridge = FALSE, robust = robust),
    warning = function(w) {
      if (grepl("singular", conditionMessage(w))) invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
    })
  L  <- makeContrast("respR = 0", parameterNames = c("respR"))
  qs <- hypothesisTest(qs, i = "protein", contrast = L)
  list(qs = qs,
       res = rowData(qs[["protein"]])[["respR"]] |>
         as_tibble(rownames = "feature") |> dplyr::mutate(arm = label))
}

## ---- limma, both specifications ----------------------------------------------
## Conditioned (plex term) and unconditioned (`nomix`) specifications.
limma_da <- function(mat, annot_use, label = "", conditioned = TRUE) {
  sm <- tibble::tibble(Sample = colnames(mat)) |>
    tidyr::separate(Sample, into = c("Mixture","Channel"), sep = "_", remove = FALSE) |>
    dplyr::left_join(annot_use |>
      dplyr::distinct(Mixture, Channel, Condition_bin, BioReplicate),
      by = c("Mixture","Channel"))
  keep <- sm$Condition_bin %in% c("R","NR") & !is.na(sm$Condition_bin)
  sm <- sm[keep, , drop = FALSE]; y <- mat[, sm$Sample, drop = FALSE]

  cond <- factor(sm$Condition_bin, levels = c("NR","R"))
  design <- if (conditioned) {
    mix <- factor(sm$Mixture); model.matrix(~ 0 + cond + mix)
  } else model.matrix(~ 0 + cond)
  colnames(design) <- sub("^cond", "", colnames(design))
  contr <- limma::makeContrasts(R_vs_NR = R - NR, levels = design)
  fit2  <- limma::eBayes(limma::contrasts.fit(limma::lmFit(y, design), contr),
                         trend = TRUE, robust = TRUE)
  tt <- limma::topTable(fit2, coef = "R_vs_NR", number = Inf, sort.by = "none")
  list(res = tibble::tibble(Protein = rownames(y), logFC = tt$logFC,
                            t = tt$t, p_limma = tt$P.Value, q_limma = tt$adj.P.Val),
       design = design, sm = sm, y = y)
}

## ---- set membership ----------------------------------------------------------
prot_of <- function(pw, map = mp$pitt_pw_map_obs)
  map$ProteinID[map$Pathway == pw]

## `cog` not `cat` — the formal shadowed base::cat() inside the body scope.
cog_prot <- function(cog, coh = "pitt")
  annot$protein[annot$cohort == coh & !is.na(annot$cog_cat) & annot$cog_cat == cog]

ko_prot <- function(kos, coh = "pitt")
  annot$protein[annot$cohort == coh & annot$ko_primary %in% kos]

## ---- Bacillota-internal fractions ------------------------------------------
## Defined once here; used by §5c and §11b.
frac_bacillota_internal <- function(OPx, pep_ph_x, prots) {
  bac  <- pep_ph_x$row[pep_ph_x$tax == "Bacillota"]
  rows <- which(OPx$rd$Protein %in% prots)
  num <- colSums(OPx$a[intersect(bac, rows), OPx$d$sample, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
  den <- colSums(OPx$a[bac,                  OPx$d$sample, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
  OPx$d |> dplyr::mutate(frac = num / den) |>
    dplyr::filter(is.finite(frac), frac > 0, frac < 1)
}

## coefficient extractor used by the Bacillota-internal test and its null (§5c)
resp_coef <- function(y, mix, rsp) {
  cf <- coef(summary(lm(qlogis(y) ~ mix + rsp))); cf[grep("^rsp", rownames(cf)), 1]
}
