# 2. PSM → QFeatures, and the cohorts

## 2a. Inputs

Annotation channel coverage is incomplete for some Sheba mixtures — mixture 1
has 9 annotated channels, mixture 2 has 6 — while `psm.tsv` always writes 11.
Unannotated channels are dropped by the join, not by position.

```{r channels}
TMT11 <- c("126","127N","127C","128N","128C",
           "129N","129C","130N","130C","131N","131C")

## Annotation channel coverage is INCOMPLETE for some mixtures — Sheba mixture 1
## has 9 annotated channels, mixture 2 has 6. The psm.tsv always writes 11, so
## the unannotated ones are dropped by the join, not by position.
## count() on the annotation gives ROWS, not channels — the table carries several
## rows per channel — so the old `n_channels` label was wrong (mixture 1 reads 90,
## which no TMT plex has). Both are reported: distinct channels is the design
## figure, rows per channel is what a careless join would multiply by.
mp$sheba_annot_use |> dplyr::count(Mixture, name = "annot_rows") |> as.data.frame()
mp$sheba_annot_use |> dplyr::distinct(Mixture, Channel) |>
  dplyr::count(Mixture, name = "channels") |> as.data.frame()
mp$sheba_annot_use |> dplyr::count(Mixture, Channel) |>
  dplyr::count(Mixture, rows_per_channel = n) |> as.data.frame()
## MEASURED 23 Sep 2026, annot_rows: 1 = 90, 2 = 30, 3 = 55, 4 = 55, 5 = 50.
## If rows_per_channel is not constant within a mixture, any join on
## Mixture + Channel without distinct() first will silently multiply rows.
```

## 2b. Load

Decoys, contaminants, purity ≤ 0.6, probability ≤ 0.7 and oxidised forms are
removed, and only proteins from the cohort's own metagenome-derived database are
kept (by sequence-ID prefix), so host proteins never enter the PSM assay; the
host proteome is quantified separately (`mp$host_state`). **No detection-completeness filter is applied** — proteins a ≥50%
detection rule would remove are part of what this study measures.

**Zero is not a measurement.** FragPipe writes `0` for an unmeasured channel,
so `log2()` gives `-Inf` and the robust fit fails: 91,959 rows in Pittsburgh,
49,774 in Sheba. Channels annotated empty are excluded.

```{r psm-load}
PITT_RESULTS  <- file.path(DATA_ROOT, "Metaproteomics/ICB_melanoma_metaproteomics/Pittsbourgh/Results_18_12_25_2")
SHEBA_PSM_DIR <- file.path(DATA_ROOT, "Metaproteomics/ICB_melanoma_metaproteomics/Sheba/metagenome_matched/PSMs_combined/")

pitt_psm_files <- list.files(PITT_RESULTS, "^psm\\.tsv$", recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)
pitt_psm_files <- pitt_psm_files[basename(dirname(pitt_psm_files)) != "TMT9"]
sheba_files    <- list.files(SHEBA_PSM_DIR, "^psm.*\\.tsv$", full.names = TRUE)
stopifnot(length(pitt_psm_files) == 8, length(sheba_files) == 6)

## Probability > 0.7, Oxidation removed. The >=50% DETECTION filter is
## deliberately absent: proteins it would remove are part of what is measured.
PREFIX <- c(pitt = "^OIDECCNN_", sheba = "^(KMMIBAFL_|PPAAKGPG_)")

load_psm_long <- function(files, prefix_ok, annot) {
  map_dfr(files, function(f) {
    d  <- readr::read_tsv(f, show_col_types = FALSE, guess_max = Inf)
    ic <- grep("^Intensity ", names(d), value = TRUE)
    stopifnot("expected 11 reporter columns" = length(ic) == 11)
    d |>
      dplyr::filter(!.data[["Is Decoy"]], !.data[["Is Contaminant"]],
                    .data[["Purity"]] > 0.6, .data[["Probability"]] > 0.7,
                    !grepl("Oxidation", .data[["Assigned Modifications"]]),
                    grepl(prefix_ok, .data[["Protein"]]),
                    substr(.data[["Protein"]], 4, 8) != "Cont_") |>
      dplyr::transmute(Run = clean_run(.data[["Spectrum File"]]),
                       Spectrum = .data[["Spectrum"]],
                       Peptide  = .data[["Peptide"]],
                       Charge   = .data[["Charge"]],
                       Protein  = .data[["Protein"]],
                       !!!rlang::set_names(rlang::syms(ic), TMT11)) |>
      tidyr::pivot_longer(dplyr::all_of(TMT11), names_to = "Channel",
                          values_to = "Intensity")
  }) |>
    dplyr::inner_join(annot |> dplyr::distinct(Run, Channel, Mixture,
                                               BioReplicate, Condition),
                      by = c("Run", "Channel"))
}

## USE *_annot_use FOR BOTH, not the raw MSstatsTMT_annotation.csv.
## The raw CSV has 88 Pitt channels; five carry Condition == "Empty" with
## placeholder BioReplicate values (TMT6 129N, TMT7 127C/129N/131C, TMT8 131C)
## — channels never loaded with sample. `remove_empty_channel = TRUE` dropped
## them during summarisation, so *_annot_use has 83. Joining on the raw CSV
## would reintroduce all five.
long <- list(
  pitt  = load_psm_long(pitt_psm_files, PREFIX[["pitt"]],  mp$pitt_annot_use),
  sheba = load_psm_long(sheba_files,    PREFIX[["sheba"]], mp$sheba_annot_use))

map(long, ~ c(rows = nrow(.x), proteins = dplyr::n_distinct(.x$Protein),
              runs = dplyr::n_distinct(.x$Run),
              samples = dplyr::n_distinct(paste(.x$Mixture, .x$Channel))))

## ZERO IS NOT A MEASUREMENT. FragPipe writes 0 for an unmeasured channel, not
## NA, so log2() gives -Inf and msqrob's rlm fails with
##   "Error in .lm.fit(X, expression) : NA/NaN/Inf in 'y'"
## MEASURED: 91,959 zeros in Pitt (5.9% of rows), 49,774 in Sheba (6.1%).
## MSstatsTMT does this conversion internally, which is part of why the two
## routes' feature counts differ — this makes the comparison like-for-like.
map(long, ~ c(zero = sum(.x$Intensity == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
              na   = sum(is.na(.x$Intensity)), n = nrow(.x)))
long <- map(long, ~ dplyr::mutate(.x, Intensity = dplyr::na_if(Intensity, 0)))

p1 <- readr::read_tsv(file.path(PITT_RESULTS, "TMT1", "psm.tsv"),
                      n_max = 3, show_col_types = FALSE)
s1 <- readr::read_tsv(sheba_files[1], n_max = 3, show_col_types = FALSE)
## mp$pitt_annot_use is the canonical channel table (83 channels; the raw CSV
## has 88, five of them Empty).
stopifnot(clean_run(unique(p1[["Spectrum File"]])) %in% mp$pitt_annot_use$Run,
          clean_run(unique(s1[["Spectrum File"]])) %in% mp$sheba_annot_use$Run)
```

## 2c. Build

```{r qfeatures}
build_qf <- function(lg) {
  ## Fractions are summed per (Spectrum-less) feature within Run before
  ## reshaping — Pitt has 5 runs per mixture, Sheba mixture 1 has 2.
  wide <- lg |>
    dplyr::mutate(sample = paste(Mixture, Channel, sep = "_"),
                  psm_id = paste(Run, Spectrum, Protein, sep = "|")) |>
    ## Peptide and Spectrum are carried into rowData: every taxonomy-based
    ## analysis downstream (C3, C10b, C10d) needs the sequence, and recovering
    ## it later by joining back to `long` is an avoidable failure point.
    dplyr::select(psm_id, Protein, Peptide, Run, Mixture, sample, Intensity) |>
    ## values_fn = sum collapses FRACTIONS within a run (Pitt 5 per mixture,
    ## Sheba mixture 1 has 2 runs). With zeros already NA, sum() returns NA if
    ## any fraction is missing — stricter than na.rm = TRUE, and the right
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = sample, values_from = Intensity,
                       values_fn = sum)

  ecols <- setdiff(names(wide), c("psm_id", "Protein", "Peptide", "Run", "Mixture"))
  ## quantCols, not ecol — the latter is deprecated in current QFeatures.
  q <- readQFeatures(as.data.frame(wide), quantCols = match(ecols, names(wide)),
                     name = "psms", fnames = "psm_id")
  q <- logTransform(q, base = 2, i = "psms", name = "psmsLog")
  ## Belt-and-braces: any residual non-finite value becomes NA. Should be a
  ## no-op once zeros are removed above, but a single -Inf kills the whole fit.
  a <- assay(q[["psmsLog"]]); a[!is.finite(a)] <- NA
  assay(q[["psmsLog"]]) <- a

  ## Join on SAMP, not SAMP_PRIMARY, and carry TWO flags. `!is.na(resp)` alone
  ## conflates a Norm channel with the pre-committed exclusion of sample `11`
  ## (304 days pre-treatment) — different reasons, and the second must stay
  ## auditable if the exclusion list ever changes.
  ##
  ## Norm channels are not in SAMP, so the join leaves them with Mixture = NA,
  ## and reference_normalise() — which must FIND each plex's Norm channel —
  ## would silently return the object untouched.
  ##
  ## Mixture and Channel therefore come from the SAMPLE NAME, which is how they
  ## were constructed ("TMT1_126", "3_127C"). resp and arm stay NA for pools,
  ## which is correct.
  cd <- tibble(sample = colnames(q)[["psmsLog"]]) |>
    dplyr::left_join(SAMP |> dplyr::select(sample, resp, arm), by = "sample") |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      Mixture  = sub("_[^_]+$", "", sample),
      Channel  = sub("^.*_", "", sample),
      is_norm  = !sample %in% SAMP$sample,
      excluded = sample %in% setdiff(SAMP$sample, SAMP_PRIMARY$sample))

  colData(q)$Mixture  <- factor(cd$Mixture)
  colData(q)$Channel  <- factor(cd$Channel)
  colData(q)$resp     <- factor(cd$resp, levels = RESP_LEVELS)
  colData(q)$arm      <- cd$arm
  colData(q)$is_norm  <- cd$is_norm
  colData(q)$excluded <- cd$excluded
  q
}

qf <- map(long, build_qf)

## Stripped peptide sequence on rowData — Unipept matches sequence only, and
## `Peptide` may carry modification text in some FragPipe versions.
qf <- map(qf, function(q) {
  rowData(q[["psms"]])$seq    <- toupper(gsub("[^A-Z]", "", rowData(q[["psms"]])$Peptide))
  rowData(q[["psmsLog"]])$seq <- rowData(q[["psms"]])$seq
  q
})

map(qf, ~ table(norm = colData(.x)$is_norm, excl = colData(.x)$excluded))
map(qf, ~ table(colData(.x)$resp, colData(.x)$Mixture, useNA = "ifany"))

## MANDATORY CHECK. Every mixture must show exactly one Norm channel. If any
## shows zero, Mixture is NA on the pools and reference_normalise() will be a
map(qf, ~ table(as.data.frame(colData(.x))$Mixture,
                as.data.frame(colData(.x))$is_norm, useNA = "ifany"))
```

## 2d. Sheba's plex design is irregular

```{r sheba-design}
mp$sheba_annot_use |> dplyr::count(Mixture, Channel) |>
  dplyr::count(Mixture, name = "n_channels") |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    long$sheba |> dplyr::distinct(Run, Mixture) |> dplyr::count(Mixture, name = "n_runs"),
    by = "Mixture") |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    long$sheba |> dplyr::count(Mixture, name = "psm_rows"), by = "Mixture") |>
  dplyr::mutate(per_channel_per_acq = round(psm_rows / n_channels /
                                            (n_runs / 5) / 1000, 1))
## MEASURED 23 Sep 2026 (thousand PSM rows per channel per five-run equivalent):
##   mixture 1  9 channels, 10 runs, 151,128 rows -> 8.4
##   mixture 2  6 channels,  5 runs,  82,572 rows -> 13.8
##   mixture 3 11 channels,  5 runs, 218,911 rows -> 19.9
##   mixture 4 11 channels,  5 runs, 167,970 rows -> 15.3
##   mixture 5 10 channels,  5 runs, 194,010 rows -> 19.4
## Mixture 1 is SPS-MS3 and mixtures 3-5 are MS2 (§2.8). Its doubled run count
## does not compensate: per channel it still reaches about HALF the depth of the
## MS2 plexes. That is a depth difference on top of the ratio-compression
## difference, and the two have different consequences — compression attenuates
## fold changes, depth changes which proteins are detected at all. The MS2-only
## sensitivity analysis (§12d) drops mixture 1 and therefore removes chemistry,
## run count and depth together; its attenuation cannot be attributed to one.
```

## 2e. Arm objects, raw-intensity helpers, taxonomy accessors {#arm-objects}

Raw PSM intensity is required for any **fraction**: the protein assay is
median-centred log ratios, and a fraction of those is meaningless.

The taxonomy loaded here is the **initial** Unipept cache; §5c replaces
`pep_ph`, `pep_g` and `pep_fa` with the completed one, so every check in §8b runs
on the completed taxonomy. Where a check's recorded value predates completion,
§8b says so.

```{r arm-objects}
## The raw PSM assay, its rowData, and the analysable sample table, per cohort.
## `assay(qf$X, "psms")` is RAW intensity — required for any FRACTION, because
## `assay(..., "protein")` is median-centred log ratios; a fraction of those is
## meaningless. arm_mix_v13() is defined once, in §1b, with its sample-count
## guard; `arm_name` is used so no formal collides with a column or a global.

arm_objs <- function(coh, arm_name) {
  q  <- qf[[coh]]
  km <- arm_mix_v13(arm_name)
  list(q  = q,
       a  = assay(q, "psms"),
       rd = as.data.frame(rowData(q[["psms"]])),
       d  = as.data.frame(colData(q)) |> tibble::rownames_to_column("sample") |>
              dplyr::filter(Mixture %in% km, !is_norm, !excluded,
                            !is.na(resp)) |> droplevels())
}
OP <- arm_objs("pitt",  "pitt_ontx")
OS <- arm_objs("sheba", "sheba_ontx")
stopifnot(nrow(OP$d) == PITT_N_ARM, nrow(OS$d) == 29)   # guards against arm_name shadowing; 55 before 13 Oct 2026
## headline counts for the §0 summary table, which is printed before they exist
vc_put("pitt.n",  nrow(OP$d));  vc_put("pitt.R",  sum(OP$d$resp == "R"))
vc_put("pitt.NR", sum(OP$d$resp == "NR"))
## Sheba: OS$d is the 29-channel MS2 arm (section 7c), NOT the analysed cohort, so the
## summary table 35/27/8 have no object here. Take them from B41 roster, the same
## source Table 1 counts; absent on a first run, which the report states rather than hides.
local({
  f <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "B41_supp_tables", "supp_data_sample_metadata.csv")
  if (!file.exists(f)) return(invisible(NULL))
  r <- utils::read.csv(f, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  s <- r[grepl("^Sheba", r$cohort) & toupper(as.character(r$analysed)) == "TRUE", ]
  vc_put("sheba.n",  nrow(s))
  vc_put("sheba.R",  sum(s$response == "R"))
  vc_put("sheba.NR", sum(s$response == "NR"))
})
a <- OP$a; d <- OP$d                       # Pittsburgh defaults, used below

## Chaperone protein sets — PER COHORT. The assemblies share no protein IDs.
## CHAPERONE_KO (19 KOs) is defined in §1b and is NOT redefined here.
chap_prot       <- annot$protein[annot$cohort == "pitt"  & annot$ko_primary %in% CHAPERONE_KO]
chap_prot_sheba <- annot$protein[annot$cohort == "sheba" & annot$ko_primary %in% CHAPERONE_KO]
c(pitt = length(chap_prot), sheba = length(chap_prot_sheba))
## MEASURED on the INITIAL annotation: 520 / 190. Pittsburgh agrees with
## `helpers` at the same stage; §5c raises it to 613 (`reannot-asrun`).

## BioReplicate <-> Mixture_Channel map. Detection tables and the metagenome
## carry BioReplicate ids (MF0030); SAMP_PRIMARY uses Mixture_Channel.
smap <- mp$pitt_annot_use |>
  dplyr::distinct(Mixture, Channel, BioReplicate) |>
  dplyr::mutate(sample = paste(Mixture, Channel, sep = "_"))
stopifnot(!any(duplicated(smap$BioReplicate)))
## MEASURED: map_rows 83, overlap_with_SAMP 75 — the 8 norm channels are in the
## map and not in SAMP_PRIMARY, which is the intended difference.
c(map_rows = nrow(smap),
  overlap_with_SAMP = length(intersect(smap$sample, SAMP_PRIMARY$sample)))

## The INITIAL Unipept cache (35,077 peptides, both cohorts). §5c replaces
## pep_ph, pep_g and pep_fa with the completed cache.
lca_all <- readRDS(file.path(paths$out_dir, "unipept_lca.rds"))
lca_rank <- function(coh, rank_col) {
  lca_all |> dplyr::filter(cohort == coh) |>
    dplyr::select(seq = peptide, tax = dplyr::all_of(rank_col)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(tax = dplyr::na_if(trimws(tax), "")) |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(tax)) |> dplyr::distinct(seq, .keep_all = TRUE)
}

## PSM row -> taxon, for a given rank. `row` indexes `a` directly.
pep_tax <- function(O, coh, rank_col) {
  tibble::tibble(row = seq_len(nrow(O$a)), seq = O$rd$seq,
                 Protein = O$rd$Protein) |>
    dplyr::inner_join(lca_rank(coh, rank_col), by = "seq")
}
pep_g  <- pep_tax(OP, "pitt", "genus_name")    # genus
pep_ph <- pep_tax(OP, "pitt", "phylum_name")   # phylum
pep_fa <- pep_tax(OP, "pitt", "family_name")   # family
c(n_psm = nrow(a), genus = nrow(pep_g), phylum = nrow(pep_ph))
## MEASURED 23 Sep 2026, INITIAL taxonomy: n_psm 151,712, genus 36,228,
## phylum 53,638. §5c replaces these caches with the completed taxonomy and the
## counts GROW — after it, Bacteroidota and Bacillota alone hold 13,974 and
## 63,398 phylum rows (§8g), more than this total across all phyla. A phylum
## count near 53,638 here means §5c has not yet run; near 77,000+ means it has.

## Host proteome. Rownames are UniProt ENTRY names, not gene symbols —
## MPO is PERM_HUMAN, ELANE is ELNE_HUMAN, S100A8 is S10A8_HUMAN. A
## gene-symbol grep returns character(0) and every downstream model fails
hs   <- mp$host_state$pitt_host_mat_f
INFL <- grep("TRFL|S10A8|S10A9|PERM|ELNE|CATG|LYSC|NGAL|DEF5",
             rownames(hs), value = TRUE)
HCHAP <- grep("HSPB1|HSP7C|HSP71|HS90|DNJ", rownames(hs), value = TRUE)
c(n_infl = length(INFL), n_hostchap = length(HCHAP), n_host = nrow(hs))
## MEASURED: 9 / 2 / 283. The nine is the inflammatory panel used in §2.4; the
## 283 is every host protein, of which 220 clear the 80% coverage bar B5 applies.

## Generic within-set fraction of RAW signal, per sample.
## Named to avoid `frac_of`, used elsewhere for the host/microbial ratio.
chap_frac_of <- function(O, prots, rows = NULL) {
  idx <- if (is.null(rows)) which(O$rd$Protein %in% prots) else rows
  num <- colSums(O$a[idx, O$d$sample, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
  den <- colSums(O$a[,   O$d$sample, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
  O$d |> dplyr::mutate(frac = num / den) |>
    dplyr::filter(is.finite(frac), frac > 0, frac < 1)
}
test_frac <- function(dd, label, covar = NULL) {
  f <- paste("qlogis(frac) ~ Mixture", if (!is.null(covar)) paste("+", covar), "+ resp")
  broom::tidy(lm(as.formula(f), data = dd)) |>
    dplyr::filter(grepl("^resp", term)) |>
    dplyr::transmute(what = label, n = nrow(dd), median_frac = median(dd$frac),
                     estimate, std.error, p.value)
}
```

## 2f. Timepoints — the cohorts differ {#timepoints}

Pittsburgh was sampled **during** treatment (48 of 54 dated samples after
start, 6 on or before it — 4 NR, 2 R; median 9.5 days, IQR 4–30). Sheba was sampled **before** it, in both
sample families. This is the single fact that shapes what each cohort can
answer, and it is measured here rather than assumed.

```{r pitt-timepoint}
## RAW re-read, deliberately: this chunk needs Sample_collection_date,
## Sample_category and Sample_progression_timepoint, which §0a's pitt_meta drops.
## It reads through the same resolver as §0a (the file is in the metadata
## directory, NOT the output directory) and lands in its OWN name — overwriting
## `pitt_meta` would replace §0a's curated table, with norm_id'd ids and the
## duplicate Response_PFS_12 columns resolved, for everything downstream.
## (Same reasoning as the existing note about not using `pm`, which §3c owns.)
pitt_meta_raw <- read.csv(meta_file(META_PITT, "Lior_UPF_data.csv"))
## PARSE PER ELEMENT, AND MONTH-FIRST. Rewritten 13 Oct 2026; this function used
## as.Date()'s tryFormats, which picks ONE format from the FIRST non-NA element of
## the vector and applies it to every element. Every date column in
## Lior_UPF_data.csv is m/d/yy with a two-digit year, and a third of the values are
## ambiguous (both fields <= 12) -- so with "%d/%m/%Y" ahead of "%m/%d/%Y" in the
## list, an ambiguous first value silently flipped day and month for the whole
## column, and every value whose second field exceeded 12 became NA. Which format
## won therefore depended on which sample happened to come first, i.e. on the
## sample set. Relabelling TMT1_126 to MF0017 put "11/3/20" first and exposed it:
## 31 of 53 collection dates became NA and 20 of the 22 that parsed had day and
## month swapped. The assertion on Timepoint_days below is the permanent guard.
## This is the convention the rest of the document already uses -- section 0a reads
## Rx_start, Prog_date, Death_date and LFU_date with "%m/%d/%y" first, and
## B41_supp_tables.R parses per element -- so no other date in the pipeline moves.
## Two-digit years now resolve to 2020 rather than 0020, which makes the
## Prog_date comparison below a comparison of real dates.
pd <- function(x) {
  s <- trimws(as.character(x)); s[!nzchar(s) | s %in% c("NA", "N_A", "NaN")] <- NA
  out <- rep(as.Date(NA), length(s))
  p <- function(i, f) if (any(i)) out[i] <<- suppressWarnings(as.Date(s[i], format = f))
  p(!is.na(s) & grepl("^\\d{1,2}/\\d{1,2}/\\d{2}$",  s), "%m/%d/%y")
  p(!is.na(s) & grepl("^\\d{1,2}/\\d{1,2}/\\d{4}$",  s), "%m/%d/%Y")
  p(!is.na(s) & grepl("^\\d{4}-\\d{1,2}-\\d{1,2}$",  s), "%Y-%m-%d")
  p(!is.na(s) & grepl("^\\d{4}/\\d{1,2}/\\d{1,2}$",  s), "%Y/%m/%d")
  p(!is.na(s) & grepl("^\\d{1,2}\\.\\d{1,2}\\.\\d{4}$", s), "%d.%m.%Y")
  out
}
smap_p <- mp$pitt_annot_use |> dplyr::distinct(Mixture, Channel, BioReplicate) |>
  dplyr::mutate(sample = paste(Mixture, Channel, sep = "_"))
arm_p <- OP$d |> dplyr::select(sample, Mixture, resp) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(smap_p |> dplyr::select(sample, BioReplicate), by = "sample")
jp <- arm_p |>
  ## THE RELABEL NEVER REACHED THIS JOIN, AND THE MARGIN SAID SO FOR THREE WEEKS.
  ## Section 0a establishes that TMT1_126 is MF0017, annotated under the corrupted
  ## name MF001A3A817, and calls that relabel the only correction that survives.
  ## It was applied to identity and pairing but not here: `arm_p` still carried the
  ## corrupted id while `pitt_meta_raw` keys on the true one, so this left_join
  ## missed, Sample_collection_date came back NA, and days_before with it. The
  ## consequence is two lines below -- "NA 1" in the before_or_on table, and "TRUE
  ## for all 54" in the guard's own comment -- and it has been visible since
  ## 21 Sep 2026 without being read as a defect. Every analysis built on `tot`
  ## has therefore run on 54 of 55 samples: the within-plex exposure balance
  ## (tot_balance) and all five response-by-exposure interaction models.
  ##
  ## Resolved here rather than upstream in `arm_p`, because arm_p's ids are what
  ## the SDRF carries and §0a's record of the corruption depends on that staying
  ## true; the correction belongs at the point of use, where the true id is what
  ## the metadata is keyed on.
  dplyr::mutate(BioReplicate = dplyr::if_else(BioReplicate == "MF001A3A817",
                                              "MF0017", BioReplicate)) |>
  dplyr::left_join(pitt_meta_raw |> dplyr::select(MF_ID, Sample_collection_date, Rx_start, Timepoint_days,
                                       Sample_category, Sample_progression_timepoint, Rx),
                   by = c("BioReplicate" = "MF_ID")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(days_before = as.numeric(pd(Rx_start) - pd(Sample_collection_date)))
c(analysed = nrow(jp), matched = sum(!is.na(jp$Rx_start)), dated = sum(!is.na(jp$days_before)))
## AN ASSERTION, NOT A PRINTED COUNT. The undated row was printed for three weeks
## and read as a property of the data. If the relabel ever stops reaching this
## join the knit now stops here instead of quietly returning to 54.
stopifnot("TMT1_126/MF0017 is undated again -- the relabel did not reach this join" =
            sum(is.na(jp$days_before)) == 0L)
table(category = jp$Sample_category, useNA = "ifany")
table(before_or_on = jp$days_before >= 0, useNA = "ifany")         # 21 Sep: FALSE 48, TRUE 6, NA 1
summary(jp$days_before)                                             # median -9.5
## THE GUARD, added 13 Oct 2026. Timepoint_days is an independent record of the
## same quantity in the same file, so it catches a mis-parse rather than letting a
## swapped day and month through as a plausible number. It is an assertion now,
## not a printed table: the printed version was TRUE for all 54 on 23 Sep and
## would have read FALSE for 20 of 22 in the first run of the corrected set.
.agree <- as.numeric(jp$Timepoint_days) == -jp$days_before
table(agree_after = .agree, useNA = "ifany")
stopifnot("days_before disagrees with Timepoint_days -- check pd()" =
            all(.agree, na.rm = TRUE),
          "an analysed sample has no usable collection date" =
            sum(!is.na(jp$days_before)) == nrow(OP$d))
## MEASURED 13 Oct 2026, 54-sample set (MF1640 restored): analysed 54, matched 54,
## dated 54; before_or_on FALSE 48 / TRUE 6 / NA 0. MF1640's dates are in this file
## and nowhere else -- it is in no metadata_pitt.tsv row -- so its Timepoint_days of
## 31 comes through the same raw-date path, and it is an on-treatment sample.
## MEASURED 13 Oct 2026, 53-sample set (MF1640 out): analysed 53, matched 53, dated
## 53; before_or_on FALSE 47 / TRUE 6 / NA 0; days_before median -9 (min -99, max
## 27); agree_after TRUE for all 53. The six at or before the first dose are 0, 4,
## 5, 7, 10 and 27 days before it. MF0480's +10 was always in this file; it is
## absent only from metadata_pitt.tsv, which is why Table 1 and this figure once
## differed.
## MEASURED 23 Sep 2026, uncorrected set: analysed 55, matched 54, dated 54;
## before_or_on FALSE 48 / TRUE 6 / NA 1; days_before median -9.50; agree_after
## TRUE for all 54. The undated one was TMT1_126, under its corrupted name; the
## median moved from -9.50 to -9 because MF0017 joined and MF1529 left. The note
## here previously read "53 of 54" — one sample used to
## disagree and now none does, which is the same metadata refresh that gave
## one probe a collection date (§0a). Sign convention: POSITIVE is days BEFORE
## treatment start, so the median of -9.5 is sampling 9.5 days AFTER it.
```

```{r sheba-ontx-timing}
mnum <- function(x) gsub("\\D", "", as.character(x))
tim <- read.csv(file.path(paths$out_dir, "sheba_sample_timing_all_records.csv"), colClasses = "character")
```

# 3. Normalisation

## 3a. Per-channel

Median-centre each channel in the PSM assay before aggregation — the minimal
equivalent of MSstatsTMT's `global_norm`.

```{r normalise}
## Median-centre each channel in the PSM assay, BEFORE aggregation.
## This is the minimal equivalent of MSstatsTMT's `global_norm = TRUE`.
## `reference_norm` (Norm-channel scaling) is handled separately in §3b.
normalise_channels <- function(q, i = "psmsLog") {
  a <- assay(q[[i]])
  a <- sweep(a, 2, apply(a, 2, median, na.rm = TRUE), "-")
  assay(q[[i]]) <- a
  q
}
qf <- map(qf, normalise_channels)

## VERIFY: per-sample medians must now be ~0 with no response association.
walk(names(qf), function(nm) {
  q  <- qf[[nm]]
  md <- apply(assay(q, "psmsLog"), 2, median, na.rm = TRUE)
  cat(nm, " median of medians:", round(median(md, na.rm = TRUE), 4),
      " sd:", round(sd(md, na.rm = TRUE), 4), "\n")
})
```

```{r norm-check}
round(sd(apply(assay(qf$pitt, "psmsLog"), 2, median, na.rm = TRUE)), 6)
## 0 => normalised. Non-zero => §3a has not run on this object.
```

## 3b. Reference-channel normalisation (optional second stage)

```{r reference-norm}
## Optional second stage. Subtract each run's Norm-channel profile so runs are
## on a common scale per PROTEIN rather than per channel.
reference_normalise <- function(q, i = "psmsLog") {
  a  <- assay(q[[i]])
  ## as.data.frame(), NOT colData() directly — DFrame's `$` on a missing name
  ## WARNS rather than erroring, so a typo or a missing column returns NULL and
  cd <- as.data.frame(colData(q))
  stopifnot("is_norm missing"  = "is_norm" %in% names(cd),
            "Mixture has NAs"  = !any(is.na(cd$Mixture)))
  for (m in unique(as.character(cd$Mixture))) {
    cols <- which(as.character(cd$Mixture) == m)
    nref <- intersect(cols, which(cd$is_norm))
    if (!length(nref)) { warning("no Norm channel in ", m); next }
    a[, cols] <- a[, cols] - rowMeans(a[, nref, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
  }
  assay(q[[i]]) <- a
  q
}

## VERIFY IT WROTE: a silent no-op would give bit-identical fits.
qf_rn <- map(qf, reference_normalise)
stopifnot("reference_normalise was a no-op" =
            !identical(assay(qf$pitt, "psmsLog"), assay(qf_rn$pitt, "psmsLog")))
dd <- as.vector(assay(qf_rn$pitt, "psmsLog") - assay(qf$pitt, "psmsLog"))
summary(dd[is.finite(dd)])
```

```{r residual-plex}
r2 <- apply(pm[, d$Sample], 1, function(y)
        summary(lm(y ~ factor(d$Mixture)))$r.squared)

tibble::tibble(protein = names(r2), r2 = r2) |>
  dplyr::mutate(grp = dplyr::case_when(
    protein %in% ko_prot(CHAPERONE_KO) ~ "chaperone",

## MEASURED 23 Sep 2026. Overall median R2 on plex 0.232 (IQR 0.128-0.370).
## By group: chaperone 0.152 (n = 140), ribosomal 0.190 (226), COG J other
## 0.253 (109), rest 0.248 (1,382). The result-carrying sets are the LEAST
## plex-exposed at the protein level, which is the favourable answer to this
## chunk's question.
##
## Do not read this against the 76% in §2.1: that is the PER-SAMPLE chaperone
## share, an aggregate over 140 proteins. Aggregation averages away
## protein-specific noise while the shared plex component survives, so the share
```

# 4. Per-protein differential abundance

## 4a. Two specifications

`msqrob2TMT` with a random plex term is the primary fit; `limma` is fitted with
and without the plex term. Specification is **not** immaterial: conditioned
against unconditioned limma on one matched universe, NES agree at only
ρ = 0.164 across 17 COG categories (§6d). So sign-stability is checked per claim, and any quantity whose
sign moves between specifications is not claimed. COG O stays negative in all
three: about −2.2 (msqrob, conditioned), −1.89 (limma, conditioned), −1.11
(limma, unconditioned).

```{r fit-both}
FA <- fit_arm(qf$pitt,  arm_mix_v13("pitt_ontx"),  "pitt_ontx")
FS <- fit_arm(qf$sheba, arm_mix_v13("sheba_ontx"), "sheba_ontx")

FA$res |> dplyr::summarise(n = dplyr::n(), n_p05 = sum(pval < .05, na.rm = TRUE),
                           expected = round(.05*dplyr::n(), 1),
                           n_q05 = sum(adjPval < .05, na.rm = TRUE),
                           median_lfc = median(logFC, na.rm = TRUE))
FA$res |> dplyr::filter(pval < .05) |>
  dplyr::count(dir = dplyr::if_else(logFC > 0, "R-up", "NR-up"))
## MEASURED 23 Sep 2026, Pittsburgh: 6,939 proteins tested; 604 at p < 0.05
## against 347 expected (1.74x); **zero at q < 0.05**; median logFC 0.0082;
## direction balanced at 297 NR-up / 307 R-up.
##
## This is why the analysis is set-level. No individual protein survives FDR, the
## effects are tiny and the direction split is even, so nothing here supports a
## per-protein claim — while the 1.74x excess of small p-values says the null is
## not the whole story either. The enrichment tests read that excess; they do not
## create it.
```

## 4b. Shrinkage

`ashr` attaches `MASS`, which masks `dplyr::select`; the load order is
re-asserted after this chunk.

```{r ash-obs}
## ashr ATTACHES MASS, which masks dplyr::select. MASS::select takes different
## arguments, so a bare select() downstream would error confusingly or, with a
## matching signature, silently do the wrong thing.
##
## Re-assert the load order AFTER ashr, not before.
library(ashr)
ash_run <- function(res, label) {
  d <- res |> dplyr::filter(is.finite(logFC), is.finite(se), se > 0)
  a <- ashr::ash(d$logFC, d$se, mixcompdist = "normal")
  list(label = label, n = nrow(d), pi0 = ashr::get_pi0(a),
       fit = d |> dplyr::mutate(lfsr = ashr::get_lfsr(a),
                                pm = ashr::get_pm(a)) |> dplyr::arrange(lfsr))
}
A <- ash_run(FA$res, "pitt_ontx")
c(n = A$n, pi0 = A$pi0, lfsr05 = sum(A$fit$lfsr < .05),
  lfsr10 = sum(A$fit$lfsr < .10), lfsr20 = sum(A$fit$lfsr < .20))
## MEASURED 23 Sep 2026: n 6,939, pi0 0.465, lfsr < 0.05 = 14, < 0.10 = 30,
## < 0.20 = 113.
##
## Read beside `fit-both`, which found ZERO proteins at BH q < 0.05. The two do
## not conflict: ash borrows strength across proteins and estimates that 53.5%
## are non-null, which is a strong claim resting on its unimodal prior. Nothing
## in the paper rests on it — it is reported because a shrinkage estimator
## disagreeing this sharply with BH is worth showing, not hiding. The 14 proteins
## at lfsr < 0.05 are not claimed as findings.

for (p in c("readr","stringr","tibble","tidyr","purrr","dplyr")) {
  detach(paste0("package:", p), character.only = TRUE, unload = FALSE)
  library(p, character.only = TRUE)
}
check_masking_v15()
```

# 5. Annotation and taxonomy {#annotation}

Reported sets and reported taxonomy both come from this section. It runs before
§6 so that nothing downstream can be built on the initial annotation by
accident.

## 5a. Unipept LCA

API contract: `input[]` **repeated and form-encoded** (a JSON array under
`input` returns 422); `equate_il = TRUE`, because mass spectrometry cannot
distinguish isoleucine from leucine; `extra = TRUE` for the full lineage. Do
not resolve `taxon_id` — it is the LCA node and often sits above genus.
Nomenclature is current NCBI: Bacillota, Bacteroidota, Pseudomonadota.

```{r unipept}
## HTTP API. `input[]` REPEATED and FORM-encoded — a JSON array under `input`
## returns 422. `equate_il = TRUE` is ESSENTIAL: mass spectrometry cannot
## distinguish isoleucine from leucine. `extra = TRUE` returns the full lineage
## so genus_name comes back directly — do NOT resolve taxon_id, which is the
## LCA node and often sits above genus.
pept2lca <- function(peps, batch = 100) {
  peps <- unique(peps[nzchar(peps)])
  map_dfr(split(peps, ceiling(seq_along(peps) / batch)), function(b) {
    body <- c(setNames(as.list(b), rep("input[]", length(b))),
              list(equate_il = "true", extra = "true", names = "true"))
    r <- httr::POST("https://api.unipept.ugent.be/api/v1/pept2lca.json",
                    body = body, encode = "form")
    if (httr::status_code(r) != 200) return(tibble())
    as_tibble(httr::content(r, "parsed", simplifyVector = TRUE))
  })
}

## PSM -> peptide within sample. Sum: multiple PSMs of one peptide in one
## channel are repeat measurements of the same quantity. STRIPPED sequence —
## Unipept matches sequence only.
pep_long <- long$pitt |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Intensity)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(sample = paste(Mixture, Channel, sep = "_"),
                seq    = toupper(gsub("[^A-Z]", "", Peptide))) |>
  dplyr::group_by(sample, Mixture, Channel, seq) |>
  dplyr::summarise(Intensity = sum(Intensity, na.rm = TRUE),
                   n_psm     = dplyr::n(),
                   proteins  = paste(unique(Protein), collapse = ";"),
                   .groups   = "drop")

## Nothing downstream uses this query's result: the analysis reads the frozen
## caches (§2e, §5c). A live query reflects today's Unipept database, not the one
## the analysis used, so it runs only when OFFLINE is FALSE.
if (!OFFLINE) {
  lca_raw <- pept2lca(unique(pep_long$seq))
  ## `family_id` collides with metaannot's (an MMseqs2 cluster) — select explicitly.
  lca <- lca_raw |>
    select(seq = peptide, taxon_rank, genus_name, family_name, phylum_name) |>
    mutate(across(ends_with("_name"), ~ na_if(trimws(.x), "")))
  print(c(n = nrow(lca), genus_resolved = mean(!is.na(lca$genus_name))))
}
```

## 5b. Extracting the search databases

Sheba needs both assemblies: `KMMIBAFL_` from the 1_2 assembly, `PPAAKGPG_`
from 3_4_5. An ID that fails to resolve is a database/search mismatch and is
explained, not dropped.

```{r metaannot-fasta}
library(Biostrings)

## Prokka databases. Sheba needs BOTH — KMMIBAFL_ from the 1_2 assembly,
## PPAAKGPG_ from 3_4_5.
## DB is defined in §1a (canonical, prefix-verified).

## CONFIRM the header format before extracting — Prokka writes
## ">OIDECCNN_00001 hypothetical protein", so the description must be stripped,
## but a reformatted database may carry a prefix instead.
head(names(Biostrings::readAAStringSet(DB[["pitt"]], nrec = 3)))

want <- list(pitt  = unique(long$pitt$Protein),
             sheba = unique(long$sheba$Protein))

## How many are genuinely new to metaannot?
map_dfr(c("pitt","sheba"), function(ch) {
  have <- annot$protein[annot$cohort == ch]
  tibble(cohort = ch, n_observed = length(want[[ch]]),
         n_annotated = sum(want[[ch]] %in% have),
         n_new = sum(!want[[ch]] %in% have),
         pct_new = round(100 * mean(!want[[ch]] %in% have), 1))
}) |> as.data.frame()

extract_fa <- function(db_path, ids, out_path) {
  fa <- Biostrings::readAAStringSet(db_path)
  names(fa) <- sub("\\s.*$", "", names(fa))     # strip Prokka's description
  hit <- fa[names(fa) %in% ids]
  message(basename(out_path), ": ", length(hit), " of ", length(ids), " found")
  Biostrings::writeXStringSet(hit, out_path)
  invisible(setdiff(ids, names(hit)))            # IDs that did not resolve
}

miss_p <- extract_fa(DB[["pitt"]], want$pitt,
                     file.path(paths$out_dir, "metaannot_pitt_psmlevel.faa"))

## Sheba: split by prefix, extract from each assembly, then concatenate.
s1 <- grep("^KMMIBAFL_", want$sheba, value = TRUE)
s2 <- grep("^PPAAKGPG_", want$sheba, value = TRUE)
c(KMMIBAFL = length(s1), PPAAKGPG = length(s2),
  unmatched_prefix = length(want$sheba) - length(s1) - length(s2))

miss_s1 <- extract_fa(DB[["sheba1"]], s1,
                      file.path(paths$out_dir, "metaannot_sheba_1_2_psmlevel.faa"))
miss_s2 <- extract_fa(DB[["sheba2"]], s2,
                      file.path(paths$out_dir, "metaannot_sheba_3_4_5_psmlevel.faa"))

## An ID that fails to resolve is a database/search mismatch: explain it, never drop it.
map_int(list(pitt = miss_p, sheba1 = miss_s1, sheba2 = miss_s2), length)

## Record the exact inputs — metaannot stores a source_sha256, and the FASTA
## md5 is what ties a downstream annotation back to this extraction.
## MEASURED 23 Sep 2026. Proteins written, and each file's checksum:
##   metaannot_pitt_psmlevel.faa       13,385  1d272d52e137cc716413dcb37e3a9b77
##   NOTE: these three md5s are the metaannot PSM-LEVEL EXPORTS, not the search
##   databases. The search FASTAs are identified by sequence-ID prefix in §1a
##   (OIDECCNN / KMMIBAFL / PPAAKGPG) and have no pinned hash.
##   metaannot_sheba_1_2_psmlevel.faa   6,639  c1da7c2db3251c5ceabc5b3e21f7c2f4
##   metaannot_sheba_3_4_5_psmlevel.faa 5,957  cb3832f16b01c1c9c2a84c713f91f465
## Counts match `psm-load` exactly: 13,385 Pittsburgh and 6,639 + 5,957 = 12,596
## Sheba, with unmatched_prefix 0 in both — every observed protein is in the
## database it was searched against.
##
## The checksums identify WHICH database this analysis ran on. They are the
## reference for the concatenated re-search (§13) and for any later claim that a
## run used the same sequences: a differing hash means a different database, not
## a different pipeline.
tools::md5sum(list.files(paths$out_dir, "^metaannot_.*psmlevel\\.faa$",
                         full.names = TRUE))
```

## 5c. The completed annotation and taxonomy — as run {#reannot}

KO per protein combines both sources as the annotation pipeline does: eggNOG
first, KOfam filling gaps. This chunk produces `annot_new`, `cmp_cog`,
`ribo_new`, `chap_new` and their Sheba counterparts, and rebuilds the taxonomy
on the completed cache — 31,326 of ~41,500 submitted peptides returned a match;
the remainder have no Unipept match at all, expected for a metagenome-derived
search database.

Coverage moved from 35.4% of Pittsburgh PSM rows carrying a phylum to 55.3%.
That is not a neutral change: quantities computed on the earlier cache were
computed on a biased subset. Section 6 of the chunk tests the Bacillota-internal
chaperone fraction (C3, §8b) on the completed cache.

```{r reannot-asrun}
## ============================================================================
## THE COMPLETED ANNOTATION AND TAXONOMY — as run, 20 September 2026
## Every reported set (§6b) and every taxonomy object used in §8-§12 is built
## here, as are the inputs to prep_sheba_pooled.R.
## ============================================================================

## ---- 0. keep the pre-re-annotation table, for every old-vs-new comparison ---
annot_old <- annot

## ---- 1. the re-annotation, both cohorts ------------------------------------
## The re-annotation TSVs live in the PROJECT root, not in metaannot_export and
## not in the output directory. PROJ is OUT_DIR, so file.path(PROJ, ...) only
## worked when the two coincided. here::here() is the project root by
## definition, which is where they are; ICB_REANNOT_DIR overrides it.
REANNOT_DIR <- Sys.getenv("ICB_REANNOT_DIR", here::here())
RA <- c(pitt  = file.path(REANNOT_DIR, "pitt_psm__annotation_final.tsv"),
        sheba = file.path(REANNOT_DIR, "sheba_psm__annotation_final.tsv"))
gone <- RA[!file.exists(RA)]
if (length(gone))
  stop("re-annotation not found:\n  ", paste(gone, collapse = "\n  "),
       "\nSet ICB_REANNOT_DIR.", call. = FALSE)
## guess_max = Inf: without it a column typed from the first 1,000 rows silently
## truncates the rest. MEASURED: the first read without it raised a parsing
## warning; with it, readr::problems() returns 0 rows.
ra <- purrr::imap_dfr(RA, ~ readr::read_tsv(.x, show_col_types = FALSE,
                                            guess_max = Inf) |>
                        dplyr::mutate(cohort = .y))
c(rows = nrow(ra), cols = ncol(ra))
if (nrow(readr::problems(ra)))
  warning(nrow(readr::problems(ra)), " parsing problems in the re-annotation; ",
          "inspect readr::problems(ra) before trusting any column.", call. = FALSE)
## MEASURED 23 Sep 2026: 25,981 rows over 80 columns — exactly the 13,385
## Pittsburgh plus 12,596 Sheba proteins observed at PSM level, so the
## re-annotation covers every observed protein and nothing else.
##
## The provenance column is `ko_source` — where each KO assignment came from.
## An earlier version of this line said `ann_source`, which is not in the export
## and never was; the fallback list is kept in case the name changes again.
src_col <- intersect(c("ko_source", "ann_source", "source", "annotation_source"),
                     names(ra))
if (length(src_col)) print(dplyr::count(ra, cohort, .data[[src_col[1]]])) else
  message("no provenance column in the re-annotation (looked for: ko_source, ",
          "ann_source, source, annotation_source); columns are: ",
          paste(head(names(ra), 12), collapse = ", "), " ...")

## ---- 2. KO per protein: eggNOG first, KOfam to fill (metaannot's rule) -------
## Combine both sources the way metaannot does.
ra2 <- ra |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    ko_e = dplyr::na_if(sub("^ko:", "", sub(",.*$", "", ko)), "-"),
    ko_k = dplyr::na_if(sub(",.*$", "", kofam_ko), "-"),
    ko_new = dplyr::coalesce(ko_e, ko_k))
c(with_ko_pitt  = sum(!is.na(ra2$ko_new[ra2$cohort=="pitt"])),
  with_ko_sheba = sum(!is.na(ra2$ko_new[ra2$cohort=="sheba"])))   # expect 10,415 / 9,987

cmp2 <- ra2 |>
  dplyr::select(protein = protein_id, cohort, ko_new, ko_source, ko_conflict, bin) |>
  dplyr::full_join(annot |> dplyr::select(protein, cohort, ko_old = ko_primary),
                   by = c("protein","cohort"))
cmp2 |> dplyr::count(cohort, status = dplyr::case_when(
  is.na(ko_old) &  is.na(ko_new) ~ "still none",
  is.na(ko_old) & !is.na(ko_new) ~ "FILLED",
  !is.na(ko_old) & is.na(ko_new) ~ "LOST",
  ko_old == ko_new               ~ "same",
  TRUE                           ~ "CHANGED")) |> as.data.frame()

## Annotations LOST in the re-annotation: do any touch the frozen sets?
lost <- cmp2 |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(ko_old), is.na(ko_new))
c(n_lost = nrow(lost),
  lost_RIBO = sum(lost$ko_old %in% RIBO_KO),
  lost_CHAP = sum(lost$ko_old %in% CHAPERONE_KO))

## ---- 3. the corrected sets ----------------------------------------------------
annot_new  <- cmp2 |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(ko_new)) |>
  dplyr::select(protein, cohort, ko_primary = ko_new)
ribo_new   <- annot_new$protein[annot_new$cohort == "pitt"  & annot_new$ko_primary %in% RIBO_KO]
chap_new   <- annot_new$protein[annot_new$cohort == "pitt"  & annot_new$ko_primary %in% CHAPERONE_KO]
ribo_new_s <- annot_new$protein[annot_new$cohort == "sheba" & annot_new$ko_primary %in% RIBO_KO]
chap_new_s <- annot_new$protein[annot_new$cohort == "sheba" & annot_new$ko_primary %in% CHAPERONE_KO]
c(ribo = length(ribo_new), chap = length(chap_new),
  ribo_s = length(ribo_new_s), chap_s = length(chap_new_s))
## MEASURED 23 Sep 2026, reproducing the record: 1,398 / 613 Pittsburgh and
## 333 / 392 Sheba. Note Sheba has FEWER ribosomal than chaperone proteins,
## the reverse of Pittsburgh — a measurement-universe difference, not a
## biological one (§2.8).

## ---- 4. COG categories, old against new -------------------------------------------
cmp_cog <- ra |>
  dplyr::transmute(protein = protein_id, cohort, cog_new = dplyr::na_if(cog_cat, "-")) |>
  dplyr::full_join(annot |> dplyr::select(protein, cohort, cog_old = cog_cat),
                   by = c("protein", "cohort"))

## ---- 5. the Unipept cache, completed; taxonomy rebuilt --------------------------------
## ============================================================================
## REBUILD THE UNIPEPT CACHE — three sources, then verify coverage
## ============================================================================

FILL   <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "unipept_fill")
chunks <- list.files(FILL, "\\.rds$", full.names = TRUE)
c(n_chunks = length(chunks))

## CHECK COLUMNS BEFORE BINDING: a name mismatch gives NA taxonomy rather
## than an error.
fill_raw  <- purrr::map_dfr(chunks, readRDS)
gain_raw  <- readRDS(file.path(paths$out_dir, "unipept_lca_gained.rds"))
need_cols <- c("peptide", "cohort", "phylum_name", "genus_name", "family_name")
## need_cols is the PRESENCE CHECK for the three ranks the rebuild below uses. The
## PROJECTION is deliberately WIDER: B38_species_direction.R needs species_name, and
## folding the two roles into one vector is what made unipept_lca_COMPLETE.rds
## speciesless on the 14 Oct knit -- B38 failed with "the cache has no species_name
## column" while all three sources carried it. Verified 14 Oct: lca_all, gain_raw and
## the fill chunks all have species_name, so nothing needs re-fetching from Unipept.
keep_cols <- c(need_cols, "species_name", "taxon_rank")   # taxon_rank: §14a
for (nm in c("lca_all", "gain_raw", "fill_raw")) {
  miss <- setdiff(need_cols, names(get(nm)))
  cat(nm, ":", nrow(get(nm)), "rows;",
      if (length(miss)) paste("MISSING:", paste(miss, collapse = ",")) else "cols OK",
      if ("species_name" %in% names(get(nm))) "" else "; NO species_name (B38 loses these rows)",
      "\n")
}

## lca_all listed FIRST so the original cache wins any collision.
lca_all2 <- dplyr::bind_rows(
    lca_all  |> dplyr::mutate(src = "cache"),
    gain_raw |> dplyr::mutate(src = "gained"),
    fill_raw |> dplyr::mutate(src = "fill")) |>
  dplyr::select(dplyr::any_of(c(keep_cols, "src"))) |>
  dplyr::distinct(cohort, peptide, .keep_all = TRUE)

c(rows = nrow(lca_all2), peptides = dplyr::n_distinct(lca_all2$peptide))
## MEASURED 23 Sep 2026: 415 fill chunks; lca_all 35,077 + gained 985 + fill
## 31,326 rows in, 67,388 rows and 59,436 distinct peptides out after
## distinct(cohort, peptide). The cache is listed FIRST in the bind so it wins
## any collision — order matters here and is not cosmetic.
lca_all2 |> dplyr::count(cohort, src) |> as.data.frame()

## ---- COVERAGE ---------------------------------------------------------------
cov <- function(O, coh) {
  s <- unique(O$rd$seq); have <- lca_all2$peptide[lca_all2$cohort == coh]
  c(matrix_seqs = length(s), cached = sum(s %in% have),
    uncached = sum(!s %in% have), pct = round(100 * mean(s %in% have), 1))
}
rbind(pitt = cov(OP, "pitt"), sheba = cov(OS, "sheba"))
## MEASURED: Pittsburgh 41,804 of 47,029 sequences cached (88.9%), Sheba 25,494
## of 34,210 (74.5%). The cohorts differ by 14 points, and Sheba is the weaker —
## which is worth remembering wherever a Sheba taxonomic quantity is compared
## against a Pittsburgh one (§2.9, §11c): part of any gap is coverage, not
## biology. The uncached sequences are dropped from every per-taxon analysis.

saveRDS(lca_all2, file.path(paths$out_dir, "unipept_lca_COMPLETE.rds"))

## ============================================================================
## REBUILD TAXONOMY — both cohorts, three ranks
## ============================================================================
lca_rank2 <- function(coh, rank_col) {
  lca_all2 |> dplyr::filter(cohort == coh) |>
    dplyr::select(seq = peptide, tax = dplyr::all_of(rank_col)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(tax = dplyr::na_if(trimws(tax), "")) |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(tax)) |> dplyr::distinct(seq, .keep_all = TRUE)
}
pep_tax2 <- function(O, coh, rank_col)
  tibble::tibble(row = seq_len(nrow(O$a)), seq = O$rd$seq,
                 Protein = O$rd$Protein) |>
    dplyr::inner_join(lca_rank2(coh, rank_col), by = "seq")

pep_ph_OLD <- pep_ph
pep_ph   <- pep_tax2(OP, "pitt",  "phylum_name")
pep_g    <- pep_tax2(OP, "pitt",  "genus_name")
pep_fa   <- pep_tax2(OP, "pitt",  "family_name")
pep_ph_s <- pep_tax2(OS, "sheba", "phylum_name")
pep_g_s  <- pep_tax2(OS, "sheba", "genus_name")

c(phylum_old = nrow(pep_ph_OLD), phylum_new = nrow(pep_ph),
  gain = nrow(pep_ph) - nrow(pep_ph_OLD),
  pct_of_matrix = round(100 * nrow(pep_ph) / nrow(OP$a), 1))   # was 35.4%

## ---- 6. Bacillota-internal fractions on the completed taxonomy, and their null --
## The chaperone row is C3 (§8b); DR3 and DC3 are reused in §11b.
DR3 <- frac_bacillota_internal(OP, pep_ph, ribo_new)
DC3 <- frac_bacillota_internal(OP, pep_ph, chap_new)
stopifnot(identical(DR3$sample, DC3$sample))
obs3 <- c(ribo = resp_coef(DR3$frac, DR3$Mixture, DR3$resp),
          chap = resp_coef(DC3$frac, DC3$Mixture, DC3$resp))
print(obs3)

set.seed(701)
NULLF3 <- purrr::map_dfr(seq_len(N_PERM), function(i) {
  rp <- factor(ave(as.character(DR3$resp), DR3$Mixture, FUN = sample),
               levels = levels(DR3$resp))
  tibble::tibble(ribo = resp_coef(DR3$frac, DR3$Mixture, rp),
                 chap = resp_coef(DC3$frac, DC3$Mixture, rp))
})
purrr::imap_dfr(obs3, function(o, nm) {
  x <- NULLF3[[nm]]
  tibble::tibble(set = nm, observed = o, null_med = median(x), null_sd = sd(x),
                 n_le = sum(x <= o),
                 p_one = (1 + sum(x <= o)) / (1 + length(x)),
                 p_two = (1 + sum(abs(x) >= abs(o))) / (1 + length(x)))
}) |> as.data.frame()
## EXPECTED (recorded 20 September):  ribo -0.09602  p_two 0.119
##                                    chap -0.10194  p_two 0.247
```

## 5d. Coverage — what completing the annotation changed

Before: 21.1% of observed Pittsburgh proteins unannotated, 45.9% of Sheba's.

```{r reannot-coverage}
cov_tbl <- purrr::map_dfr(c("pitt","sheba"), function(ch) {
  obs <- unique(long[[ch]]$Protein)
  old <- annot_old$protein[annot_old$cohort == ch]
  new <- annot_new$protein[annot_new$cohort == ch]
  ko_old <- annot_old$protein[annot_old$cohort == ch & !is.na(annot_old$ko_primary)]
  ko_new <- annot_new$protein[annot_new$cohort == ch & !is.na(annot_new$ko_primary)]
  tibble::tibble(cohort = ch, observed = length(obs),
                 annotated_old = sum(obs %in% old), annotated_new = sum(obs %in% new),
                 with_ko_old   = sum(obs %in% ko_old), with_ko_new = sum(obs %in% ko_new))
## MEASURED 23 Sep 2026:
##   pitt   observed 13,385  annotated 10,567 -> 10,415  with KO 7,361 -> 10,415  (77.8%)
##   sheba  observed 12,596  annotated  6,813 ->  9,987  with KO 4,721 ->  9,987  (79.3%)
##
## The re-annotation does NOT affect the cohorts equally. Pittsburgh's KO
## coverage rises 41%; Sheba's rises 112%, from 4,721 to 9,987. Before §5c Sheba
## had barely half Pittsburgh's annotated proteins; after it the two are level at
## 77.8% and 79.3%. The completed annotation is what makes the cohorts comparable
## at all, and any cross-cohort quantity computed on the INITIAL annotation was
## comparing a well-annotated cohort against a poorly-annotated one.
##
## Pittsburgh's annotated count FALLS slightly (10,567 -> 10,415): 152 proteins
## lose annotation while 3,054 gain a KO. The `lost` check above confirms only 11
## carried a KO and none were ribosomal or chaperone.
}) |> dplyr::mutate(pct_annotated_new = round(100*annotated_new/observed, 1),
                    pct_ko_new        = round(100*with_ko_new/observed, 1))
cov_tbl
```

# 6. Sets and enrichment

## 6a. Landscape scan on the initial annotation — not reported

Five layers per cohort, built on the **initial** annotation — KO, COG category,
Pfam, KEGG Module and KEGG Pathway: Pittsburgh 108 / 21 / 244 / 86 / 79 sets and
Sheba 45 / 14 / 87 / 56 / 62. (A 23 September run of the restored pipeline gave
69 / 19 / 156 / 70 / 68 on a universe of 3,574. That discrepancy was resolved
exactly on 24 September: the recorded scan used R1+R2+R3 and the document had
been changed to R1+R2, while `mk_sets` re-applied the tier filter a second time
internally so that varying the universe could not move the first three layers.
With both corrected the clean knit reproduces the recorded figures — see the
chunk note.) Kept because it is how the chaperone signal was
first seen, because §6c's leading edges are defined on it, and because it
defines `stat` and `st_s`, the observed rankings every later chunk uses. **No
number in the manuscript comes from its enrichment tables.**

```{r gsea}
library(fgsea)
stat <- setNames(FA$res$t, FA$res$feature); stat <- stat[is.finite(stat)]
## Snapshot under a name nothing else touches: the identical line in §8b's C2
## reassigns `stat` to the chaperone-removed statistic, and §12a redefines `kos`
## as a function. Anything downstream wanting the PRIMARY statistic uses stat_pitt.
stat_pitt <- stat

## FIXED 23 Sep 2026: this function used to re-apply `R %in% TIER_PRIMARY$R`
## internally, on top of the tier filter already applied when `univ` was built.
## The second application overrode the first, so passing a universe here did
## nothing — KO, COG and Pfam returned 69 / 19 / 156 for every universe from
## 3,574 to 6,939 proteins while the KEGG layers, which have no internal filter,
## moved. That is what made the recorded scan irreproducible by varying `univ`
## -- an open item at the time, resolved 24 Sep and no longer on §13's list --
## and it hid the change for as long as every diagnostic varied
## the universe rather than the tier definition. The universe is now taken as
## given; the caller decides which tiers it contains.
mk_sets <- function(col, coh, universe, min_n = 10L) {
  a <- annot |> dplyr::filter(cohort == coh, protein %in% universe)
  if (col == "pfam_accs")
    a <- a |> tidyr::separate_rows(pfam_accs, sep = "[,;]") |>
      dplyr::mutate(pfam_accs = sub("\\..*$", "", trimws(pfam_accs))) |>
      dplyr::filter(grepl("^PF", pfam_accs))
  a <- dplyr::filter(a, !is.na(.data[[col]]), .data[[col]] != "")
  s <- split(a$protein, a[[col]]); s[lengths(s) >= min_n]
}

## KEGG Module and Pathway come from the RAW emapper output — metaannot exports
## only n_pathway_specific / in_specific_pathway / kegg_enrichment_visible,
## which are flags, not memberships. mp$*_eggnog_min is trimmed to 5 columns.
EM_PITT   <- file.path(DATA_ROOT, "Proteomic_databases/ICB_melanoma_Pittsbourgh/prokka_gut_meta/eggnog_prokka_Pittsbourgh.tsv.emapper.annotations")
EM_SHEBA1 <- file.path(DATA_ROOT, "metagenomics/ICB_melanoma/Sheba/1st_and_2nd_batches/prokka_output/eggnog_prokka.tsv.emapper.annotations.tsv")
EM_SHEBA2 <- file.path(DATA_ROOT, "Proteomic_databases/ICB_melanoma_Sheba/ICB_study_matched_metagenome_3_4_5/eggnog_prokka_90_3_4_5_TMT.tsv.emapper.annotations")

read_em <- function(f) {
  hdr <- grep("^#query", readLines(f, n = 10))
  readr::read_tsv(f, skip = hdr - 1, show_col_types = FALSE,
                  guess_max = Inf, name_repair = "unique") |> dplyr::rename(query = 1)
}
kegg_sets <- function(em_df, col, universe, min_n = 10L) {
  d <- em_df |> dplyr::select(query, term = dplyr::all_of(col)) |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(term), term != "-", query %in% universe) |>
    tidyr::separate_rows(term, sep = ",") |>
    dplyr::mutate(term = trimws(term)) |> dplyr::filter(nzchar(term), term != "-")
  s <- split(d$query, d$term); s[lengths(s) >= min_n]
}
## emapper writes BOTH map##### and ko##### for the same pathway — keep one
## form, and drop ko04*/ko05* (eukaryotic and disease maps).

## mk_sets() masks `a` internally with a local tibble — harmless there, but
## note `a` is the PSM assay elsewhere.
em_p <- read_em(EM_PITT)
em_s <- dplyr::bind_rows(read_em(EM_SHEBA1), read_em(EM_SHEBA2))
stopifnot(sum(duplicated(em_s$query)) == 0)   # prefixes differ; bind is safe

st_s   <- setNames(FS$res$t, FS$res$feature); st_s <- st_s[is.finite(st_s)]
## THE DISCOVERY UNIVERSE IS R1+R2+R3, NOT TIER_PRIMARY$R.
## Settled 23 Sep 2026 (U1, U2). The recorded scan — 108 / 21 / 244 / 86 / 79 —
## is reproduced by R1+R2+R3 at min_n = 10 to within 3 KO sets: 105 / 21 / 244 /
## 86 / 79, with four of five layers exact on a universe of 5,106. R1+R2 gives
## 69 / 19 / 156 / 70 / 68 and cannot be made to match on any threshold.
##
## The larger definition is used here deliberately, and not because it is the
## better universe — it is not. R3 is the single-peptide tier, and v12's own note
## records that about half the proteins are identified on one peptide, which is
## why R1+R2 caps near 50%. The tightening to R1+R2 was a real improvement and
## postdates this scan. But §6a's only job is to record WHAT WAS SEARCHED when
## the chaperone hypothesis was selected, and 538 sets were. A multiplicity
## denominator is a historical fact, not a modelling choice; shrinking it after
## measuring that the smaller space passes correction more easily is exactly the
## move an exploratory-selection critique looks for. §13 item 9's correction runs
## over this space.
##
## Nothing REPORTED depends on it: SETS_P is built from names(stat) (§6b) and
## reproduced the record exactly, as did every NES, p and q downstream.
DISCOVERY_TIERS <- c("R1", "R2", "R3")
univ   <- intersect(names(stat),
                    annot$protein[annot$cohort == "pitt"  & annot$R %in% DISCOVERY_TIERS])
univ_s <- intersect(names(st_s),
                    annot$protein[annot$cohort == "sheba" & annot$R %in% DISCOVERY_TIERS])
c(pitt = length(univ), sheba = length(univ_s))

keep_ko <- function(k) k[grepl("^ko", names(k)) & !grepl("^ko0[45]", names(k))]

sets <- list(
  KO       = mk_sets("ko_primary", "pitt", univ),
  COG      = mk_sets("cog_cat",    "pitt", univ),
  Pfam     = mk_sets("pfam_accs",  "pitt", univ),
  KEGGmod  = kegg_sets(em_p, "KEGG_Module",  univ),
  KEGGpath = keep_ko(kegg_sets(em_p, "KEGG_Pathway", univ)))

sets_s <- list(
  KO       = mk_sets("ko_primary", "sheba", univ_s),
  COG      = mk_sets("cog_cat",    "sheba", univ_s),
  Pfam     = mk_sets("pfam_accs",  "sheba", univ_s),
  KEGGmod  = kegg_sets(em_s, "KEGG_Module",  univ_s),
  KEGGpath = keep_ko(kegg_sets(em_s, "KEGG_Pathway", univ_s)))

tibble::tibble(layer = names(sets),
               pitt  = purrr::map_int(sets,   length),
               sheba = purrr::map_int(sets_s[names(sets)], length))
## RESOLVED, and EXACT on the clean knit of 24 Sep 2026. The discrepancy was the
## tier definition: the recorded scan used R1+R2+R3 (universe 5,106) and the
## document had been changed to R1+R2 (3,574). The first diagnostic run gave
## 105 / 21 / 244 / 86 / 79, three KO sets short, because it was made in a session
## where `mk_sets` still applied the tier filter a SECOND time internally. With
## that double filter removed, the clean knit gives univ = 5,106 (sheba 2,322)
## and the recorded 108 / 21 / 244 / 86 / 79 exactly. Nothing was tuned; the
## residual was the bug, not the data.
##
## Two things had to be true at once for this to stay hidden. The universe
## changed, AND `mk_sets` re-applied the tier filter internally so that varying
## the universe could not change KO / COG / Pfam at all. Every diagnostic that
## swept `univ` returned the same three numbers. Only varying TIER_PRIMARY
## itself exposed it (U1_universe_diagnostic.R, U2_tier_definition.R).
##
## WHAT THE DISCREPANCY TOUCHES, measured across the 23 Sep run. Everything built
## on `names(stat)` reproduces the record EXACTLY — SETS_P's six set sizes, both
## GroEL/DnaK shares, the C3 coefficients to five decimals, the re-annotation
## counts. Everything built on `univ` drifts:
##   - the five-layer scan, 382 sets against 538 (here)
##   - the COG O leading edge, 98 Pittsburgh proteins (§6c)
##   - spec-check, rho 0.185 against 0.164 (§6d)
##   - matched random sets C6, median -0.911 against +0.84 (§8b) — the seed is
##     fixed, but the pool is drawn against sets$COG$O
##   - the C3 and C8 per-sample models, which also mix in chap_prot (§8b)
## So the cause is upstream of the sets and downstream of the statistic: the
## tier assignment or the universe intersection, not the annotation or the fit.
##
## MEASURED (KO, COG, Pfam, KEGGmod, KEGGpath): pitt 108 / 21 / 244 / 86 / 79;
## sheba 45 / 14 / 87 / 56 / 62.

set.seed(71)
FG   <- purrr::imap_dfr(sets,   ~ fgseaMultilevel(.x, stat, minSize = 10, maxSize = 2000,
                          eps = 0) |> tibble::as_tibble() |> dplyr::mutate(layer = .y))
FG_s <- purrr::imap_dfr(sets_s, ~ fgseaMultilevel(.x, st_s, minSize = 10, maxSize = 2000,
                          eps = 0) |> tibble::as_tibble() |> dplyr::mutate(layer = .y))

FG   |> dplyr::group_by(layer) |>
  dplyr::summarise(n = dplyr::n(), n_p05 = sum(pval < .05),
                   naive = round(.05*dplyr::n(), 1), n_q05 = sum(padj < .05))
FG   |> dplyr::arrange(pval) |> head(20) |>
  dplyr::select(layer, pathway, size, NES, pval, padj) |> as.data.frame()
FG_s |> dplyr::arrange(pval) |> head(15) |>
  dplyr::select(layer, pathway, size, NES, pval, padj) |> as.data.frame()
```

## 6b. The reported sets, on the completed annotation {#sets-reported}

These are the sets every reported NES and every permutation null uses. They
are saved into the null input (§7b), and the null script recomputes the observed
NES from them, so observed and null cannot drift apart.

Completing the annotation grew Pittsburgh's COG O from 321 to **405** proteins,
and moved **no** protein between COG categories in either cohort. Sheba's sets
here are on the MS2 universe (COG O 202), the superseded design's input; the
pre-specified primary's sets are rebuilt on the pooled universe by
`prep_sheba_pooled.R` (COG O 227).

```{r sets-reported}
## The reported sets, exactly as built for the 1,000-draw nulls (21 September).
## COG O membership on the completed annotation
cogO_new <- cmp_cog$protein[cmp_cog$cohort=="pitt" &
                            !is.na(cmp_cog$cog_new) & cmp_cog$cog_new == "O"]
cogO_new_s <- cmp_cog$protein[cmp_cog$cohort=="sheba" &
                              !is.na(cmp_cog$cog_new) & cmp_cog$cog_new == "O"]

## Pittsburgh: COG O, its chaperone members, and the remainder
O_new     <- intersect(cogO_new, names(stat))
O_chap_n  <- intersect(O_new, chap_new)
O_nochap_n<- setdiff(O_new, chap_new)
c(O = length(O_new), chap = length(O_chap_n), rest = length(O_nochap_n))

## SEEDING IS NOT UNIFORM ACROSS THIS DOCUMENT, AND THIS CALL IS ONE OF THE
## UNSEEDED ONES. fgseaMultilevel estimates its null by adaptive multilevel
## splitting, so NES carries Monte Carlo noise. §6a seeds its scan with
## set.seed(71) and §11a's MP arm does the same, but the calls here, in
## `leading-edge`, in `spec-check` and in `c2-chaperone-removal` do not, so
## their values depend on the RNG state whatever ran before them left behind.
## In a top-to-bottom knit that state is deterministic and the numbers
## reproduce; running a chunk on its own, or in a different order, can move the
## last digit. The permutation p-values are unaffected -- the null worker seeds
## every draw from its draw number -- and so is any quantity read from the
## archives. What can move is a displayed NES.
##
## DECIDED 9 Nov 2026: LEFT UNSEEDED. Adding a seed would change the NES these
## chunks print, and the reported values would then have to be re-harmonised
## against a fresh run -- a change to published numbers for no gain in their
## correctness. The asymmetry is recorded instead, so that a re-run differing
## in the second decimal is read as this and not as a discrepancy. Do not
## "fix" it by adding set.seed() without re-harmonising everything downstream.
fgseaMultilevel(list(COG_O = O_new, chaperones = O_chap_n, remainder = O_nochap_n),
                stat, minSize = 10, eps = 0) |>
  tibble::as_tibble() |> dplyr::select(pathway, size, NES, pval)
## NES is used; `pval` is fgsea's internal p, quoted in §7a only to show why not.

## ... and the chaperone members without GroEL (K04077) and DnaK (K04043)
O_chap_nogd <- O_chap_n[!annot_new$ko_primary[
  match(O_chap_n, annot_new$protein[annot_new$cohort=="pitt"])] %in% c("K04077","K04043")]
## ADDED (not in the original run): the line above indexes the full table by a
## position in its Pittsburgh subset, valid only if Pittsburgh's rows come first.
## An order-free lookup must agree.
ko_pitt <- setNames(annot_new$ko_primary[annot_new$cohort == "pitt"],
                    annot_new$protein[annot_new$cohort == "pitt"])
stopifnot(identical(O_chap_nogd, O_chap_n[!ko_pitt[O_chap_n] %in% c("K04077","K04043")]))

## GroEL/DnaK share of COG O's chaperone members, analysis universe (§12a)
pk <- annot_new$ko_primary[annot_new$cohort=="pitt" & annot_new$protein %in% O_chap_n]
c(pitt_groel_dnak_pct = 100*mean(pk %in% c("K04077","K04043")), pitt_n = length(pk))

## EXPORT the analysis-universe level for Figure 5. The figure previously
## recomputed it over the WHOLE reported universe rather than over COG O's
## chaperone members, and drew 42.5 where the record says 51.5 — a figure and a
## table disagreeing about the same quantity. The value is computed once, here,
## and carried; the figure no longer derives it.
gd_analysis_universe <- c(pitt = 100 * mean(pk %in% c("K04077","K04043")),
                          n_pitt = length(pk))

## Sheba, MS2 universe: the same split
Os      <- intersect(cogO_new_s, names(st_s))
Os_chap <- intersect(Os, chap_new_s)
Os_rest <- setdiff(Os, chap_new_s)
c(O = length(Os), chap = length(Os_chap), rest = length(Os_rest))
## ADDED: the Sheba counterpart of the share line above
sk <- annot_new$ko_primary[annot_new$cohort=="sheba" & annot_new$protein %in% Os_chap]
c(sheba_groel_dnak_pct = 100*mean(sk %in% c("K04077","K04043")), sheba_n = length(sk))

## ---- the named sets carried into the nulls -------------------------------------
mk_sets_new <- function(coh, universe, min_n = 10L) {
  a <- annot_new |> dplyr::filter(cohort == coh, protein %in% universe,
                                  !is.na(ko_primary))
  list(
    COG = { s <- split(cmp_cog$protein[cmp_cog$cohort == coh &
                                       !is.na(cmp_cog$cog_new)],
                       cmp_cog$cog_new[cmp_cog$cohort == coh &
                                       !is.na(cmp_cog$cog_new)])
            s <- lapply(s, intersect, universe); s[lengths(s) >= min_n] },
    KO  = { s <- split(a$protein, a$ko_primary); s[lengths(s) >= min_n] })
}

SETS_P <- c(
  mk_sets_new("pitt",  names(stat))$COG,
  list(ribosomal   = intersect(ribo_new, names(stat)),
       chaperones  = intersect(chap_new, names(stat)),
       O_chap      = intersect(O_chap_n, names(stat)),
       O_remainder = intersect(O_nochap_n, names(stat)),
       O_chap_noGD = intersect(O_chap_nogd, names(stat))))
SETS_S <- c(
  mk_sets_new("sheba", names(st_s))$COG,
  list(ribosomal   = intersect(ribo_new_s, names(st_s)),
       chaperones  = intersect(chap_new_s, names(st_s)),
       O_chap      = intersect(Os_chap,   names(st_s)),
       O_remainder = intersect(Os_rest,   names(st_s))))

SETS_P <- SETS_P[lengths(SETS_P) >= 10]
SETS_S <- SETS_S[lengths(SETS_S) >= 10]
c(pitt_sets = length(SETS_P), sheba_sets = length(SETS_S))
lengths(SETS_P)[c("O","J","ribosomal","chaperones","O_remainder")]
## EXPECTED, Pittsburgh (as in nulls_scored_pitt_2026-09-21.csv): O 405,
##   O_chap 324, chaperones 393, O_chap_noGD 157, O_remainder 81, ribosomal 928.
## SETS_S here is the MS2 universe — the input of the superseded Sheba design.
## The pre-specified primary's sets are rebuilt on the pooled universe by
## prep_sheba_pooled.R (COG O 227).
```

## 6c. Leading edges

```{r leading-edge}
le_of <- function(res, sets_use, set_name) {
  st <- setNames(res$t, res$feature); st <- st[is.finite(st)]
  fgseaMultilevel(sets_use[set_name], st, minSize = 10, eps = 0)$leadingEdge[[1]]
}
le_P <- le_of(FA$res, sets$COG,   "O")
le_S <- le_of(FS$res, sets_s$COG, "O")
c(pitt = length(le_P), sheba = length(le_S))
## MEASURED on the clean knit, 24 Sep 2026: 127 Pittsburgh, 27 Sheba, on the
## corrected universe (an earlier session with the wrong universe gave 98 and 12).
## These come from `sets$COG` — the exploratory layer, where COG O now has 321
## members — not from SETS_P's reported 405. The record holds no earlier value
## for this quantity, so 127 / 27 is the figure.
##
## The 8-to-1 asymmetry is §2.8's point in miniature: the same contrast run in
## two cohorts puts 98 proteins behind the Pittsburgh signal and 12 behind
## Sheba's. Open item 1 asks for the GroEL/DnaK share of Sheba's leading edge in
## the PRIMARY run, which is a different set from this one.
##
## MEASURED 23 Sep 2026, composition by KO:
##   Pittsburgh (98): K04077 GroEL 28 (28.6%), K04043 DnaK 25 (25.5%),
##     K13993 17 (17.3%), K03687 GrpE 7, K03545 4, K07533 4, K04085 3,
##     K05838 2, unassigned 2, then seven KOs with one protein each.
##   Sheba (12): K04077 9 (75.0%), K04043 1 (8.3%), unassigned 2 (16.7%).
## GroEL+DnaK are 53/98 = 54.1% of the Pittsburgh leading edge and 10/12 = 83.3%
## of Sheba's — close to the 51.5% and 84.3% those cohorts' analysis universes
## already hold (§2.9), so the leading edge is not concentrating these two beyond
## what was available to it. The cohorts differ in what ELSE appears: Pittsburgh
## has seven further chaperone KOs, Sheba none.
##
## QUALITY of the leading edge against the rest of COG O, measured the same day:
##   pitt   in_le 98: npep 4, len 285.5, SE 0.200, |lfc| 0.307 | rest 150: 3, 245.5, 0.237, 0.116
##   sheba  in_le 12: npep 2, len 492.5, SE 0.242, |lfc| 0.313 | rest  36: 2, 355.0, 0.258, 0.141
## No leading-edge protein is single-peptide in either cohort.
##
## The |lfc| gap is partly circular — the leading edge is defined by rank on a
## statistic that is effect over standard error — so it is not evidence on its
## own. The SE gap is: were the ranking driven by variance instability, these
## proteins would carry HIGHER standard errors at similar effect sizes. They
## carry lower ones with larger effects, which is the opposite signature. Sheba's
## median length of 492.5 follows from its composition (GroEL ~540 aa,
## DnaK ~640).
```

Limma on the summarised matrix, with and without the plex term, on one universe
(1,857 proteins), enriched over the initial-annotation COG sets. Recovered

```{r spec-check}
L0 <- limma_da(mp$pitt_mat_f, mp$pitt_annot_use, conditioned = FALSE)
r0 <- L0$res |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(t))

## (C, E, F, G, S) change sign.

## MEASURED on the clean knit, 24 Sep 2026: rho = 0.1667, against the recorded
```
