# 10. The metagenome {#metagenome}

## 10a. Pittsburgh — inputs

The three input tables sit on **different sample sets**: MetaPhlAn and
pathabundance carry 82 samples, the KO table 81. Composition and pathways
therefore run on 73 labelled samples, KO-based analyses on 72. Asserted, not
assumed.

```{r mg-paths}
MG <- file.path(DATA_ROOT, "metagenomics/ICB_melanoma/Pittsburgh/Stool_samples")

## The HUMAnN outputs are
## under humann_output/, and the merged tables under a subdirectory whose name
## is MISSPELLED ON DISK as "merged_ouptut". Reproduce it exactly.
MG_FILES <- list(
  mpa   = file.path(MG, "merged_metaphlan_profile.txt"),
  meta  = file.path(MG, "metadata_for_metagenomics.tsv.txt"),
  path  = file.path(MG, "humann_output", "merged_ouptut",
                    "merged_pittsburgh_pathabunance.tsv"),
  ko    = file.path(MG, "humann_output", "merged_ouptut",
                    "merged_genefamilies_ko.tsv"),
  match = file.path(MG, "humann_output", "humann_match_table_pittsburgh.txt"),
  klog  = file.path(MG, "kneaddata_output"))
stopifnot(all(vapply(MG_FILES[1:5], file.exists, logical(1))))

## THE THREE INPUT TABLES ARE ON DIFFERENT SAMPLE SETS:
##
##   merged_metaphlan_profile.txt        82 samples   MF0480 present
##   merged_pittsburgh_pathabunance.tsv  82 samples   MF0480 present
##   merged_genefamilies_ko.tsv          81 samples   MF0480 ABSENT
##
## The KO table was regrouped from a genefamilies merge that predates MF0480.
##
## CONSEQUENCE: §10b's composition analysis has 73 labelled samples; §10c's
## functional analysis has 72. They are not the same cohort, and the difference
## is one labelled non-responder.
##
## This is asserted rather than assumed, so a future re-merge is visible.
## mg_clean and mg_bio are defined HERE, above mg_ncol, not further down:
## mg_ncol calls mg_clean, so the chunk could not run top-to-bottom and only
## worked in a session where mg_clean already existed from an earlier run.
mg_clean <- function(x)
  sub("_merged(_Abundance)?$", "", sub("^trimmed_", "", x))
mg_bio   <- function(x) norm_id(sub("(pGTSH.*|_S[0-9]+)$", "", mg_clean(x)))

mg_ncol <- function(f, n = 1)
  dplyr::n_distinct(mg_clean(names(readr::read_tsv(f, n_max = n,
    show_col_types = FALSE, skip = if (grepl("metaphlan", f)) 1 else 0))[-1]))
MG_NCOL <- c(mpa = mg_ncol(MG_FILES$mpa), path = mg_ncol(MG_FILES$path),
             ko = mg_ncol(MG_FILES$ko))
print(MG_NCOL)
if (MG_NCOL[["ko"]] != MG_NCOL[["mpa"]])
  warning("KO table has ", MG_NCOL[["ko"]], " samples against MetaPhlAn's ",
          MG_NCOL[["mpa"]], " — the HUMAnN regroup is STALE. ",
          "§10c runs on the smaller set; do not compare its n to §10b's.")

## TWO STATES EXIST ON DISK, differing by exactly one sample — MF0480, a
## labelled non-responder:
##
##              mpa cols   labelled   match rows
##   backup        82         72          81
##   current       83         73          82
##
## EXPECTED on the current files at the >=5M floor: 68 labelled samples,
## Bacteroidota 25.748 / 38.202, p = 0.04958.
##
## Use the CURRENT top-level files. The backup is kept for provenance only.
MG_BACKUP <- file.path(MG, "merged_backup_pre_MF0480")
c(current_mpa = file.exists(MG_FILES$mpa),
  backup_mpa  = file.exists(file.path(MG_BACKUP, "merged_metaphlan_profile.txt")))

## The four name forms in play. MetaPhlAn and HUMAnN prefix "trimmed_"; HUMAnN
## also suffixes "_merged_Abundance"; sample ids end either in the long
## pGTSH-date form or in _S<n>.

## + MF0017, 13 Oct 2026 (pitt_sample_corrections.R): its metagenome was unlabelled only
## because its proteome label was filed under a corrupted name. The EXPECTED
## counts in this section's comments predate it by one labelled non-responder.
mg_meta <- readr::read_tsv(MG_FILES$meta, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  apply_pitt_mg_corrections() |>
  dplyr::transmute(sample = Sample_name, Condition,
                   resp = factor(ifelse(Condition == "responder", "R", "NR"),
                                 levels = RESP_LEVELS),
                   bio = mg_bio(Sample_name))
c(labelled = nrow(mg_meta), NR = sum(mg_meta$resp == "NR"))   # 74, 39 (73, 38 before MF0017)
```

```{r mg-depth}
## The logs carry the final counts; do not decompress 82 fastq.gz to get them.
## Restrict to kneaddata logs: MF0480 has an incomplete leftover log nested
## inside MF0461's directory, and multiqc writes a .log of its own.
logs <- list.files(MG_FILES$klog, "\\.log$", recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)
c(n_kneaddata_logs = length(logs),
  n_toplevel_dirs  = length(list.dirs(MG_FILES$klog, recursive = FALSE)),
  nested = sum(!dirname(logs) %in% list.dirs(MG_FILES$klog, recursive = FALSE)))
## EXPECTED: 83 logs -> 82 names -> 82 unique; the nested leftover has no
## `final pair1` line and yields no row.
depth <- purrr::map_dfr(logs, function(f) {
  l <- grep("final pair1", readLines(f, warn = FALSE), value = TRUE)
  if (!length(l)) return(NULL)
  tibble::tibble(
    sample = sub(".*/trimmed_([^/]+)_paired_1.*", "\\1", l[1]),
    reads  = as.numeric(sub(".*: ([0-9.]+)\\s*$", "\\1", l[1])))
})
c(n = nrow(depth), median = median(depth$reads),
  min = min(depth$reads), max = max(depth$reads))
## EXPECTED: 82 / 19,118,723 / 21,829 / 47,478,455.
stopifnot(nrow(depth) == 82L, !anyDuplicated(depth$sample))

## 82 samples, 73 labelled (MF1613_S21 carries Condition = NA, and eight
## others are unlabelled). At the >=5M floor: 76 samples, 68 labelled — and
## §10b's composition figures are computed on that set.
c(under_1M = sum(depth$reads < 1e6), under_5M = sum(depth$reads < 5e6),
  under_10M = sum(depth$reads < 1e7))                    # 4, 6, 11

## Which low-depth samples are LABELLED — the ones that entered every analysis.
depth |> dplyr::filter(reads < 5e6) |>
  dplyr::left_join(mg_meta, by = "sample") |>
  dplyr::arrange(reads) |> dplyr::select(sample, reads, Condition)

KEEP_5M <- depth$sample[depth$reads >= 5e6]              # 76 samples
```

## 10b. Composition under depth floors

The ≥5M floor is primary; the floor is set on depth, not on outcome.

```{r mg-composition}
mpa_raw <- readr::read_tsv(MG_FILES$mpa, skip = 1, show_col_types = FALSE)
mpa_samples <- mg_clean(names(mpa_raw)[-1])

phy <- mpa_raw |>
  dplyr::filter(stringr::str_count(clade_name, "\\|") == 1,
                grepl("\\|p__", clade_name)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(phylum = sub(".*\\|p__", "", clade_name)) |>
  dplyr::select(-clade_name) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-phylum, names_to = "raw", values_to = "pct") |>
  dplyr::mutate(sample = mg_clean(raw)) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(mg_meta, by = "sample")

## Three floors. The >=5M version is PRIMARY — the floor is chosen on depth,
## not on outcome.
test_phylum <- function(floor_reads) {
  keep <- depth$sample[depth$reads >= floor_reads]
  phy |> dplyr::filter(sample %in% keep) |>
    dplyr::group_by(phylum) |>
    dplyr::filter(max(pct) >= 0.1) |>
    dplyr::group_modify(~{
      w <- wilcox.test(pct ~ resp, data = .x)
      tibble::tibble(n = nrow(.x),
                     med_NR = median(.x$pct[.x$resp == "NR"]),
                     med_R  = median(.x$pct[.x$resp == "R"]),
                     p = w$p.value)
    }) |> dplyr::ungroup() |> dplyr::mutate(floor = floor_reads)
}
comp_all <- purrr::map_dfr(c(0, 1e6, 5e6), test_phylum)

comp_all |> dplyr::filter(phylum %in% c("Bacteroidota","Firmicutes",
                                        "Actinomycetota","Pseudomonadota")) |>
  dplyr::arrange(phylum, floor) |> as.data.frame()

## Bacteroidota : Firmicutes, same three floors
bf <- phy |> dplyr::filter(phylum %in% c("Bacteroidota","Firmicutes")) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = phylum, values_from = pct) |>
  dplyr::mutate(lr = log2((Bacteroidota + 0.01)/(Firmicutes + 0.01)))
purrr::map_dfr(c(0, 1e6, 5e6), function(fl) {
  d <- bf |> dplyr::filter(sample %in% depth$sample[depth$reads >= fl])
  tibble::tibble(floor = fl, n = nrow(d),
                 med_NR = median(d$lr[d$resp == "NR"]),
                 med_R  = median(d$lr[d$resp == "R"]),
                 p = wilcox.test(lr ~ resp, data = d)$p.value)
})
```

## 10c. Gene content, and the invariance test

Single-copy CPM is **not** invariant to a phylum swap, so the criterion is sign
and significance: chaperone CPM against Firmicutes negative, ribosomal against
Bacteroidota positive, both p < 0.01. Set-level CPM by response is flat —
chaperone 9,481 NR against 9,938 R (Wilcoxon p = 0.238), ribosomal p = 0.955.
Metagenome tables keep MetaPhlAn's phylum names: Firmicutes for Bacillota,
Actinobacteria for Actinomycetota.

```{r mg-genecontent}
ko_raw <- readr::read_tsv(MG_FILES$ko, show_col_types = FALSE)
names(ko_raw)[1] <- "feature"
ko_cpm <- ko_raw |>
  dplyr::filter(!grepl("\\|", feature), !feature %in% c("UNMAPPED","UNGROUPED")) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-feature, names_to = "raw", values_to = "v") |>
  dplyr::mutate(sample = mg_clean(raw)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(sample) |> dplyr::mutate(cpm = 1e6 * v / sum(v)) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |> dplyr::inner_join(mg_meta, by = "sample")

## Ribosomal KOs present in the metagenome, and the chaperone set from §1b
RIBO_MG <- ko_cpm |> dplyr::filter(feature %in% RIBO_KO) |>
  dplyr::group_by(feature) |> dplyr::filter(median(cpm) > 1) |>
  dplyr::pull(feature) |> unique()
c(n_ribo_mg = length(RIBO_MG), n_chap_mg = sum(CHAPERONE_KO %in% ko_cpm$feature))

set_cpm <- function(kos) ko_cpm |> dplyr::filter(feature %in% kos) |>
  dplyr::group_by(sample, resp) |> dplyr::summarise(tot = sum(cpm), .groups = "drop")
purrr::imap_dfr(list(chaperone = CHAPERONE_KO, ribosomal = RIBO_MG),
  function(kos, nm) {
    d <- set_cpm(kos)
    tibble::tibble(set = nm, med_NR = median(d$tot[d$resp == "NR"]),
                   med_R = median(d$tot[d$resp == "R"]),
                   p = wilcox.test(tot ~ resp, data = d)$p.value)
  })

## THE INVARIANCE TEST: is single-copy CPM invariant to a phylum swap?
## It is not.
firm <- phy |> dplyr::filter(phylum == "Firmicutes")   |> dplyr::select(sample, F = pct)
bact <- phy |> dplyr::filter(phylum == "Bacteroidota") |> dplyr::select(sample, B = pct)
purrr::imap_dfr(list(chaperone = CHAPERONE_KO, ribosomal = RIBO_MG),
  function(kos, nm) {
    d <- set_cpm(kos) |> dplyr::inner_join(firm, by = "sample") |>
      dplyr::inner_join(bact, by = "sample")
    tibble::tibble(set = nm,
      r_firmicutes = cor(d$F, d$tot), p_F = cor.test(d$F, d$tot)$p.value,
      r_bacteroidota = cor(d$B, d$tot), p_B = cor.test(d$B, d$tot)$p.value)
  })
## EXPECTED on 72 samples (the KO table's set — see §10a):
##   chaperone vs Firmicutes    r = -0.30934, p = 0.00819
##   ribosomal vs Bacteroidota  r = +0.30732, p = 0.00864
##
## Criterion: sign and significance — negative for chaperone vs Firmicutes,
## positive for ribosomal vs Bacteroidota, both p < 0.01.
##
## Set-level CPM by response, EXPECTED:
##   chaperone  9,481 NR / 9,938 R    p = 0.238
##   ribosomal  108,785 / 112,500     p = 0.955
c(n_labelled_in_ko = dplyr::n_distinct(ko_cpm$sample),
  n_labelled_in_meta = nrow(mg_meta))     # 72 vs 73 — MF0480 is the difference
```

## 10d. HUMAnN pathways

```{r mg-pathways}
hm <- readr::read_tsv(MG_FILES$match, col_names = c("raw","label"),
                      show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  dplyr::mutate(sample = mg_clean(raw),
                resp = factor(ifelse(grepl("^responder", label), "R",
                              ifelse(grepl("^non_responder", label), "NR", NA)),
                              levels = RESP_LEVELS)) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(resp))

pw_cpm <- readr::read_tsv(MG_FILES$path, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  dplyr::rename(feature = 1) |>
  dplyr::filter(!grepl("\\|", feature),
                !feature %in% c("UNMAPPED","UNINTEGRATED")) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-feature, names_to = "raw", values_to = "v") |>
  dplyr::mutate(sample = mg_clean(raw)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(sample) |> dplyr::mutate(cpm = 1e6 * v / sum(v)) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |> dplyr::inner_join(hm |> dplyr::select(sample, resp),
                                        by = "sample")

pw_res <- pw_cpm |> dplyr::group_by(feature) |>
  dplyr::filter(median(cpm) >= 10) |>
  dplyr::group_modify(~{
    w <- wilcox.test(cpm ~ resp, data = .x)
    tibble::tibble(p = w$p.value,
                   med_NR = median(.x$cpm[.x$resp == "NR"]),
                   med_R  = median(.x$cpm[.x$resp == "R"]))
  }) |> dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::mutate(q = p.adjust(p, "BH"), dir = ifelse(med_NR > med_R, "NR", "R"))
c(tested = nrow(pw_res), nominal = sum(pw_res$p < .05),
  expected = round(.05 * nrow(pw_res), 1), min_q = min(pw_res$q))

## Full KO scan
ko_res <- ko_cpm |> dplyr::group_by(feature) |>
  dplyr::filter(median(cpm) >= 5) |>
  dplyr::group_modify(~ tibble::tibble(p = wilcox.test(cpm ~ resp, data = .x)$p.value)) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |> dplyr::mutate(q = p.adjust(p, "BH"))
c(tested = nrow(ko_res), nominal = sum(ko_res$p < .05),
  expected = round(.05 * nrow(ko_res), 1), min_q = min(ko_res$q))
```

## 10e. Sheba — inputs and databases {#mg-sheba}

| tree | content | database |
|---|---|---|
| `metaphlan/` | 46 profiles: 26 S-series (the MS2 proteome's samples), 20 ME-series | `mpa_vJun23_CHOCOPhlAnSGB_202403` |
| `Humann4_output/` | HUMAnN 4.0.0.alpha.1, 50 samples, with its own MetaPhlAn profiles | `mpa_vOct22_CHOCOPhlAnSGB_202403` |

Pittsburgh's standalone profiles use `mpa_vJan25_CHOCOPhlAnSGB_202503`. The two
cohorts' standalone taxonomies are therefore **not comparable**; HUMAnN 4's
internal profiles, which use one database in both, are.

```{r mg-sheba-inputs}
## ============================================================================
## SHEBA — MEASURED 22 Sep 2026 (sheba_mg_inventory.R, sheba_mg_inventory2.R)
##   metaphlan/       46 per-sample profiles + merged_output/merged_abundance_table.txt
##                    (the same 46): 26 S-series (batches 3-5, the MS2 proteome's
##                    samples), 20 ME-series (batches 1-2: mixtures 1-2 plus during/after
##                    tubes). ALL mpa_vJun23_CHOCOPhlAnSGB_202403.
##   Humann4_output/  HUMAnN v4.0.0.alpha.1 (Pittsburgh's version), 50 samples; its own
##                    MetaPhlAn profiles are mpa_vOct22_CHOCOPhlAnSGB_202403.
##   humann/, reaction_tables/  unversioned RPK outputs (HUMAnN 3 style) — NOT used.
##   metadata.tsv     ME-series only; Time_point wrong for 86A (+7 d) — NOT used for timing.
##   The directory's mpa_vOct22_..._202212 tree and species files match no profile here.
## ============================================================================
SH <- file.path(DATA_ROOT, "metagenomics/ICB_melanoma/Sheba/combined_batches")
SH_FILES <- list(
  mpa   = file.path(SH, "metaphlan", "merged_output", "merged_abundance_table.txt"),
  prof  = file.path(SH, "metaphlan"),
  path  = file.path(SH, "Humann4_output", "pathabundance_merged_relab.tsv"),
  h4dir = file.path(SH, "Humann4_output"))
stopifnot(file.exists(SH_FILES$mpa), file.exists(SH_FILES$path))
mg_db <- function(f) sub("^#", "", readLines(f, n = 1, warn = FALSE))
MG_DB <- c(pitt = mg_db(MG_FILES$mpa), sheba = mg_db(SH_FILES$mpa))
print(MG_DB)      # 22 Sep: pitt mpa_vJan25_CHOCOPhlAnSGB_202503 · sheba mpa_vJun23_CHOCOPhlAnSGB_202403

## sample names: "<id>_S<n>_..." (S-series) or "<id>_ME_..." (ME-series); 96 is in both
sh_id <- function(x) tibble::tibble(
  raw = x, id = sub("_.*$", "", x),
  family = dplyr::case_when(grepl("^[^_]+_S[0-9]+_", x) ~ "S", grepl("^[^_]+_ME_", x) ~ "ME"))

## each sample's TUBE, by date, from the collection records (§2f)
tim <- read.csv(file.path(paths$out_dir, "sheba_sample_timing_all_records.csv"), colClasses = "character") |>
  dplyr::mutate(days = as.numeric(days_before_start), collected = as.Date(collected))
tube_of <- function(id, family) {
  probe <- sub("[abc]$", "", tolower(id)); suf <- toupper(sub("^[0-9]+", "", id))
  if (family == "S") {                                     # the arm's own record; 94a / 94b = two episodes
    r <- tim[tim$probe_key == probe & tim$file == "sheba_bar_ilan", ]
    k <- if (suf == "B") 2L else 1L
  } else {                                                 # stool bank: A / B / C = before / during / after
    blk <- unname(c(A = "before", B = "during", C = "after")[suf])
    if (is.na(blk)) blk <- if (probe == "822") "during" else "before"   # this probe's bank tube is the during one
    r <- tim[tim$probe_key == probe & tim$file == "stool_bank" & tim$block == blk, ]
    k <- 1L
  }
  r <- r[order(r$collected), ]
  if (nrow(r) < k) return(data.frame(patient = NA_character_, collected = as.Date(NA), days = NA_real_,
                                     protocol = NA_character_, best_response = NA_character_))
  r[k, c("patient", "collected", "days", "protocol", "best_response")]
}
sh_mpa_raw <- readr::read_tsv(SH_FILES$mpa, skip = 1, show_col_types = FALSE)
sm <- sh_id(names(sh_mpa_raw)[-1])
stopifnot(nrow(sm) == 46L, !anyNA(sm$family), sum(sm$family == "S") == 26L)

  dplyr::mutate(pre  = days >= 0,

                  grepl("complete|partial", best_response, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "R",

stopifnot(!anyNA(sh_mg_meta$patient), !anyNA(sh_mg_meta$resp))
table(family = sh_mg_meta$family, pre = sh_mg_meta$pre)   # expect S: 26 pre · ME: 11 pre, 9 not
```

Nothing reaches p < 0.05 (smallest p = 0.30, Actinobacteria) at 6 labelled

```{r mg-sheba-composition}
sh_phy <- sh_mpa_raw |>
  dplyr::filter(stringr::str_count(clade_name, "\\|") == 1, grepl("\\|p__", clade_name)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(phylum = sub(".*\\|p__", "", clade_name)) |> dplyr::select(-clade_name) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-phylum, names_to = "raw", values_to = "pct") |>
  dplyr::inner_join(dplyr::select(sh_set5, raw, patient, family, resp), by = "raw")
stopifnot(dplyr::n_distinct(sh_phy$raw) == nrow(sh_set5))
table(family = sh_set5$family, resp = sh_set5$resp)
sh_comp <- sh_phy |> dplyr::group_by(phylum) |> dplyr::filter(max(pct) >= 0.1) |>
  dplyr::group_modify(~ {
    obs <- tail(coef(lm(pct ~ family + resp, data = .x)), 1)
    set.seed(8100)
    nl <- replicate(1000, {
      rp <- factor(ave(as.character(.x$resp), .x$family, FUN = sample), levels = RESP_LEVELS)
      tail(coef(lm(.x$pct ~ .x$family + rp)), 1) })
    tibble::tibble(n = nrow(.x), med_NR = median(.x$pct[.x$resp == "NR"]),
                   med_R = median(.x$pct[.x$resp == "R"]),
                   p_wilcox = wilcox.test(pct ~ resp, data = .x)$p.value,
                   p_within_family = (1 + sum(abs(nl) >= abs(obs))) / (1 + length(nl)))
  }) |> dplyr::ungroup() |> dplyr::arrange(p_within_family)
as.data.frame(sh_comp)
```

## 10g. The cross-cohort gate {#mg-gate}

Enforced in code, not by convention: standalone taxonomy **stops**; HUMAnN 4
pathways and HUMAnN 4 taxonomy **pass**.

```{r mg-cross-cohort-gate}
pt_h4 <- list.files(file.path(MG, "humann_output"), "metaphlan.*\\.(tsv|txt)$", recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)
sh_h4 <- list.files(SH_FILES$h4dir, "_1_metaphlan_profile\\.tsv$", recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)
one_db <- function(fs) if (length(fs)) paste(unique(vapply(fs, mg_db, "", USE.NAMES = FALSE)), collapse = " | ") else NA_character_
MG_DB_HUMANN <- c(pitt = one_db(pt_h4), sheba = one_db(sh_h4))
print(MG_DB_HUMANN)       # 22 Sep: BOTH mpa_vOct22_CHOCOPhlAnSGB_202403
c(n_pitt_h4 = length(pt_h4), n_sheba_h4 = length(sh_h4))   # NA above means these are 0
## "taxonomy": the standalone tables (§10a, §10e). "pathways" and "taxonomy_humann4":
## HUMAnN 4's own per-sample MetaPhlAn profiles — one database for both cohorts.
## WET-LAB PROVENANCE — recorded 24 Sep 2026, and NOT checkable in code.
## The two cohorts share NOTHING upstream of the FASTQ files:
##   preservation   Pittsburgh RNAlater      | Sheba frozen
##   extraction     two different labs, two different protocols
##   sequencing     CORRECTED 24 Sep 2026 — read length follows the SAMPLE FAMILY,
##                  not the cohort. All 26 Sheba S-series libraries are 2x151,
##                  the same as Pittsburgh; only the 20 ME-series are 244 bp. The
##                  earlier "Sheba ~2x250" was measured on ME files alone.
## Only the downstream analysis is common. Preservation method and lysis
## efficiency are both established sources of compositional bias in stool, and
## the Firmicutes:Bacteroidota ratio is among the metrics they move most — which
## is precisely the axis separating these cohorts (Sheba 76.6/3.4 = 22; Pitt
## 42-54/26-38 = 1.5). All four variables are confounded with cohort and cannot
## be separated post hoc.
##
## THE FUNCTION BELOW CANNOT SEE ANY OF THIS. It compares database strings and
## passes when they match, which it now does for the HUMAnN route — licensing a
## comparison that is not like-for-like for reasons it never tests. Database
## identity is NECESSARY and NOT SUFFICIENT. Any cross-cohort metagenomic
## composition claim must carry the provenance caveat above, whatever this
## returns. Within-cohort analyses (§2.3, §11c, the Sheba replication) are
## unaffected: each runs on one pipeline throughout.
mg_cross_cohort_ok <- function(level = c("taxonomy", "pathways", "taxonomy_humann4")) {
  level <- match.arg(level)
  message("NOTE: database identity only. Preservation, extraction and platform ",
          "differ between these cohorts and are not tested here — see the note ",
          "above this function before reading any cross-cohort composition.")
  db <- if (level == "taxonomy") MG_DB else MG_DB_HUMANN
  if (anyNA(db))
    stop(sprintf("%s: no profiles found, or the database is unreadable (Pittsburgh %s; Sheba %s). ",
                 level, db[["pitt"]], db[["sheba"]]),
         "This is an INPUT problem, not a database mismatch: check the file listings before reading it as one.")
  if (db[["pitt"]] != db[["sheba"]])
    stop(sprintf("%s: MetaPhlAn databases differ (Pittsburgh %s; Sheba %s). ",
                 level, db[["pitt"]], db[["sheba"]]),
         "Cross-cohort comparison is not like-for-like; re-profile one cohort with the other's database.")
  invisible(TRUE)
}
try(mg_cross_cohort_ok("taxonomy"))
## INTERIM RE-PROFILING, 24 Sep 2026. Sheba re-run against Pittsburgh's own
## database (mpa_vJan25_CHOCOPhlAnSGB_202503), 30 of 46 samples so far — all 20
## ME-series, 10 of 26 S-series. Bacteroidota median:
##   all 30 tubes                                   3.415 %
##   24 tubes with a consistent invocation          3.404 %
##   21 patients, one tube each, consistent         3.374 %
## against 3.358 % on Sheba's native vJun23 and 4.157 % on the shared vOct22.
## Re-profiling with the other cohort's database moves the figure by 0.016
## points. THREE databases now give the same answer, and Pittsburgh is 35-39 %
## throughout: version drift is excluded independently of §10h's HUMAnN route.
##
## FULL 46-SAMPLE TABLE, 24 Sep 2026 (merged_abundance_table_mpa_vJan25_shortIDs.txt,
## mpa_vJan25_CHOCOPhlAnSGB_202503 — Pittsburgh's database). The interim 30-tube
## figure of 3.374% is superseded; the open item on it is closed.
##   46 samples, 26 S-series and 20 ME-series, from 38 distinct patients
##   (7 patients gave 2-3 tubes: 86, 87, 94, 96, 122, 165, 174).
##   Deduplicated to one tube per patient, S-series preferred where available:
##     Bacteroidota median 3.433% (mean 4.533%) over 38 patients
##     restricted to the 25 S-series tubes (2x151 bp, as Pittsburgh): 3.843%
##   Pittsburgh on the same database: ~35%. The gap is ~9-fold and holds with
##   database, profiler version, options and read length all controlled.
##   Firmicutes:Bacteroidota median 20.1, against Pittsburgh's ~1.5.
##
## The six UNCLASSIFIED = 0 samples are all ME (11, 122A, 122B, 141, 165A, 86A),
## and the split by family is clean: median UNCLASSIFIED 16.3% for S against 3.9%
## for ME. That is the read-length explanation the server gave, not two MetaPhlAn
## invocations as first diagnosed.
##
## Four S-series tubes reach Pittsburgh-like levels — 118_S24 25.8%, 152_S15
## 17.3%, 682_S16 13.3%, 97_S17 11.0% — which a uniformly Bacteroidota-depleting
## protocol would not produce. Whatever separates those four from the rest is
## worth knowing and is not established here.
##
## READ LENGTH IS ALSO EXCLUDED, 24 Sep 2026. All 26 S-series libraries are 2x151,
## matching Pittsburgh; only the 20 ME-series are 244 bp. Restricted to the S
## series the comparison is controlled on read length, database, MetaPhlAn version
## and options at once, and the gap holds: median Bacteroidota 2.5 % against
## Pittsburgh's ~35 %. Two S samples reach Pittsburgh-like levels (118_S24 25.8 %,
## 152_S15 17.3 %), which a uniformly Bacteroidota-depleting protocol would not
## produce. What remains: preservation (RNAlater against frozen), extraction
## laboratory and protocol, or a real cohort difference.
##
## TWO ODDITIES in the interim table:
##   1. Six samples (11_ME, 122A_ME, 122B_ME, 141_ME, 165A_ME, 86A_ME) carry
##      UNCLASSIFIED = 0 and phylum sums of exactly 100 %, while the other 24
##      have UNCLASSIFIED at a median of 10 %. Diagnosed here as two MetaPhlAn
##      invocations; the server later showed otherwise. ALL SIX ARE ME-SERIES,
##      and the unclassified fraction splits by family — median 3.9 % for the 20
##      ME samples against 18.5 % for the 16 S samples — which fits the ME

##      invocation is no longer the leading explanation.
##   2. 30 tubes from 24 patients (122, 165, 174, 86, 87 contribute several).

## Neither changes the conclusion (0.04 points across all three subsets), but

mg_cross_cohort_ok("pathways")          # 22 Sep: passes
mg_cross_cohort_ok("taxonomy_humann4")  # 22 Sep: passes
```

## 10h. Metagenome against proteome — an open discrepancy

Bacteroidota is 6–12× lower in the Sheba metagenome than Pittsburgh's (≈4%
against 25–38%), yet the two proteomes are close: by median intensity share
Sheba 17.4% against Pittsburgh 16.3%, by peptide rows 13.2% against 16.6%
(first chunk below). Within either cohort the proteome share does not track the
metagenome share (Spearman −0.20, 48 pairs, Pittsburgh; −0.15, 24 pairs, Sheba
mixtures 3–5; computed by `sheba_mg_by_family.R`). Unexplained; carried as a limitation. The
same-database test below is the next step.

```{r mg-proteome-crosscheck}
## Bacteroidota share of the proteome, both cohorts — no MetaPhlAn anywhere
ph_frac <- function(O, pp, tx = "Bacteroidota") {
  s <- O$d$sample
  colSums(O$a[pp$row[pp$tax == tx], s, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE) /
    colSums(O$a[pp$row, s, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
}
c(pitt_intensity = median(ph_frac(OP, pep_ph)), sheba_intensity = median(ph_frac(OS, pep_ph_s)),
  pitt_rows = mean(pep_ph$tax == "Bacteroidota"), sheba_rows = mean(pep_ph_s$tax == "Bacteroidota"))
## EXPECTED: 0.1629779 0.1735588 0.1664324 0.1319014
```

```{r mg-same-db-test}
mg_cross_cohort_ok("taxonomy_humann4")
c(pitt_profiles = length(pt_h4), sheba_profiles = length(sh_h4)); head(basename(pt_h4), 3)
read_mpa_one <- function(f) {                          # one MetaPhlAn profile -> clade, pct
  L  <- readLines(f, warn = FALSE)
  hl <- grep("^#clade_name", L, value = TRUE)
  k  <- if (length(hl)) match("relative_abundance", strsplit(sub("^#", "", hl[1]), "\t")[[1]]) else NA
  if (is.na(k)) k <- 3L
  d <- strsplit(L[!startsWith(L, "#") & nzchar(L)], "\t")
  tibble::tibble(clade = vapply(d, `[`, "", 1), pct = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(vapply(d, `[`, "", k))))
}
bact_of <- function(fs) purrr::map_dfr(fs, function(f) {
  x <- read_mpa_one(f)
  tibble::tibble(file = basename(f),
                 bact = sum(x$pct[grepl("^k__[^|]+\\|p__(Bacteroidota|Bacteroidetes)$", x$clade)]))
})
## Pittsburgh: HUMAnN 4's profiles -> §10a's sample names -> labelled samples at >= 5 M
bp <- bact_of(pt_h4) |> dplyr::mutate(sample = mg_clean(sub("_(1_)?metaphlan.*$", "", file)))
dup_p <- sum(duplicated(bp$sample)); bp <- bp[!duplicated(bp$sample), ]
bp <- bp |> dplyr::filter(sample %in% KEEP_5M) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(dplyr::select(mg_meta, sample, resp), by = "sample") |>
  dplyr::left_join(phy |> dplyr::filter(phylum == "Bacteroidota") |>
                     dplyr::select(sample, bact_standalone = pct), by = "sample")
## Sheba: HUMAnN 4's profiles -> (id, family) -> the patient set at >= 5 M (§10e)
bs4 <- bact_of(sh_h4) |> dplyr::mutate(raw_h4 = sub("_1_metaphlan_profile\\.tsv$", "", file))
bs4 <- dplyr::bind_cols(bs4, dplyr::select(sh_id(bs4$raw_h4), id, family)) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(dplyr::select(sh_set5, id, family, resp, raw), by = c("id", "family")) |>
  dplyr::left_join(sh_phy |> dplyr::filter(phylum == "Bacteroidota") |>
                     dplyr::select(raw, bact_standalone = pct), by = "raw")
c(pitt_duplicate_profiles = dup_p, pitt_n = nrow(bp), sheba_n = nrow(bs4))   # expect 68 and 32
rbind(Pittsburgh = c(n = nrow(bp), vOct22 = median(bp$bact),
                     standalone = median(bp$bact_standalone, na.rm = TRUE),
                     spearman = cor(bp$bact, bp$bact_standalone, method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs")),
      Sheba      = c(n = nrow(bs4), vOct22 = median(bs4$bact),
                     standalone = median(bs4$bact_standalone, na.rm = TRUE),
                     spearman = cor(bs4$bact, bs4$bact_standalone, method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs")))
wilcox.test(bp$bact, bs4$bact)$p.value     # the two cohorts under one database
```

# 11. Systems — metagenome × metaproteome {#systems}

## 11a. Gene capacity and protein output are weakly coupled

Within a patient, the metagenome predicts the metaproteome across KOs at
ρ = 0.238 — and a randomly chosen **other** patient's metagenome does almost as
well (0.234), so nearly all of that is structure common to gut communities. The
patient-specific part shows only on genes that vary between people: restricted to
the 200 most variable core KOs, a patient's own metagenome beats the mismatched
control in 34 of 47 patients (delta +0.033, p = 0.00028). The coupling is real
and weak, and no response contrast enters the measurement, so attenuation cannot
explain it either way.

Pathway-level R − NR contrasts in the two layers are therefore **not** evidence
of divergence: two noisy contrasts on coupled layers disagree from attenuation
alone. NES only below: `fgsea` internal p-values are not reportable on this
design and are dropped rather than hidden. Every statistic is R − NR.

```{r a1-capacity-coupling}
local({
  ## A1 — does protein output track gene capacity WITHIN patients?
  ##
  ## Why: the pathway-level dissociation (rho = -0.11, sign agreement 46%) is a
  ## correlation between two noisy response contrasts, and attenuation alone drives
  ## such a correlation toward zero. Section 1 below contains no response contrast
  ## at all, so it cannot be explained that way. Sections 2 and 3 are the set-level
  ## tracking coefficient and the genus decomposition that must precede promoting
  ## the paired chaperone model (the ribosomal version of it dissolved into one genus).
  ##
  ## Run in the analysis session, after analysis_v17.Rmd §11 (needs §5c and §10).

  EPS <- 1e-9

  ## =====================================================================
  ## 1. WITHIN-PATIENT COUPLING ACROSS KOs — no response contrast
  ## =====================================================================
  ## For each patient: how well does their own metagenome predict their own
  ## metaproteome across KOs? Compared against the SAME patient's proteome scored
  ## against every OTHER patient's metagenome. If own and mismatched agree, the
  ## metagenome carries no patient-specific information about protein output, and
  ## the dissociation holds without leaning on any response coefficient.

  ko_of <- setNames(annot_new$ko_primary[annot_new$cohort == "pitt"],
                    annot_new$protein[annot_new$cohort == "pitt"])
  rws <- tibble(row = seq_len(nrow(OP$a)), protein = OP$rd$Protein) |>
    mutate(ko = unname(ko_of[protein])) |> filter(!is.na(ko))
  M  <- rowsum(OP$a[rws$row, OP$d$sample, drop = FALSE], group = rws$ko, na.rm = TRUE)
  MP <- sweep(M, 2, colSums(M, na.rm = TRUE), "/")            # KO share per sample

  pat <- OP$d |> select(sample, Mixture, resp) |>
    inner_join(smap |> select(sample, BioReplicate), by = "sample") |>
    mutate(bio = norm_id(BioReplicate))
  MG <- ko_cpm |> filter(sample %in% KEEP_5M) |>
    group_by(bio, feature) |> summarise(cpm = sum(cpm), .groups = "drop") |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = bio, values_from = cpm, values_fill = 0)
  G  <- as.matrix(MG[, -1]); rownames(G) <- MG$feature

  pat <- pat |> filter(bio %in% colnames(G), sample %in% colnames(MP))
  kos <- intersect(rownames(MP), rownames(G))
  cat(sprintf("paired patients %d; KOs in both layers %d\n", nrow(pat), length(kos)))
  stopifnot(nrow(pat) >= 20, length(kos) >= 100)

  coup <- function(s, b) {                       # one proteome against one metagenome
    x <- MP[kos, s]; y <- G[kos, b]
    keep <- x > 0                                # KOs this patient's proteome detects
    if (sum(keep) < 100) return(NA_real_)
    suppressWarnings(cor(log(x[keep] + EPS), log(y[keep] + EPS), method = "spearman"))
  }
  ## every proteome against every metagenome, once: rows = proteome, cols = metagenome
  K <- outer(seq_len(nrow(pat)), seq_len(nrow(pat)),
             Vectorize(function(i, j) coup(pat$sample[i], pat$bio[j])))
  own <- diag(K)
  mis <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(pat)), function(i) median(K[i, -i], na.rm = TRUE), 0)
  rk  <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(pat)), function(i)
    mean(K[i, -i] >= own[i], na.rm = TRUE), 0)     # per-patient one-sided p

  cpl <- tibble(sample = pat$sample, bio = pat$bio, resp = pat$resp,
                own = own, mismatched = mis, delta = own - mis, p_own = rk)
  w <- suppressWarnings(wilcox.test(cpl$own, cpl$mismatched, paired = TRUE))
  cat(sprintf(
  "\n[1] within-patient coupling\n    own            median rho %.3f  (IQR %.3f-%.3f)\n    mismatched     median rho %.3f\n    delta          median %+.4f;  own > mismatched in %d of %d patients\n    paired Wilcoxon p = %.3g;  patients with own-p < 0.05: %d\n",
    median(cpl$own), quantile(cpl$own, .25), quantile(cpl$own, .75), median(cpl$mismatched),
    median(cpl$delta), sum(cpl$delta > 0), nrow(cpl), w$p.value, sum(cpl$p_own < 0.05)))
  cat("    READING: delta near zero = capacity does not predict output patient-specifically;\n",
      "            a clearly positive delta means the layers DO track and pillar 1 weakens.\n")

  ## =====================================================================
  ## 2. SET-LEVEL TRACKING — the log(mg) coefficient, per set
  ## =====================================================================
  paired_set <- function(prots, kos_set) {
    mpd <- chap_frac_of(OP, prots) |> select(sample, Mixture, resp, mp = frac) |>
      inner_join(smap |> select(sample, BioReplicate), by = "sample") |>
      mutate(bio = norm_id(BioReplicate))
    mgd <- ko_cpm |> filter(feature %in% kos_set, sample %in% KEEP_5M) |>
      group_by(bio) |> summarise(mg = sum(cpm) / 1e6, .groups = "drop")
    inner_join(mpd, mgd, by = "bio") |> filter(is.finite(mp), mp > 0, mp < 1, mg > 0)
  }
  pr <- paired_set(ribo_new, RIBO_KO)
  pc <- paired_set(chap_new, CHAPERONE_KO)

  track <- function(d, lab) {
    m  <- lm(qlogis(mp) ~ Mixture + log(mg) + resp, data = d)
    m0 <- lm(qlogis(mp) ~ Mixture + resp,           data = d)
    cf <- coef(summary(m))
    tibble(set = lab, n = nrow(d),
           beta_log_mg = cf["log(mg)", 1], se = cf["log(mg)", 2], p_log_mg = cf["log(mg)", 4],
           beta_std = cf["log(mg)", 1] * sd(log(d$mg)) / sd(qlogis(d$mp)),
           partial_R2 = 1 - sum(residuals(m)^2) / sum(residuals(m0)^2),
           resp = cf["respR", 1], resp_p_param = cf["respR", 4])
  }
  perm_resp <- function(d, B = 1000, seed = 4801) {
    f <- function(r) { cf <- coef(summary(lm(qlogis(d$mp) ~ d$Mixture + log(d$mg) + r)))
                       cf[grep("^r", rownames(cf)), 1] }
    o <- f(d$resp); set.seed(seed)
    nl <- replicate(B, f(factor(ave(as.character(d$resp), d$Mixture, FUN = sample),
                                levels = levels(d$resp))))
    c(obs = o, null_sd = sd(nl), p_two = (1 + sum(abs(nl) >= abs(o))) / (1 + B))
  }
  tt <- bind_rows(track(pr, "ribosomal"), track(pc, "chaperone"))
  print(as.data.frame(tt), row.names = FALSE, digits = 3)
  cat("\n    within-plex permutation on resp:\n")
  print(round(rbind(ribosomal = perm_resp(pr), chaperone = perm_resp(pc)), 4))

  ## =====================================================================
  ## 3. GENUS DECOMPOSITION OF THE CHAPERONE COMPANION
  ## =====================================================================
  ## (a) within-genus chaperone fraction by response, genus by genus
  g_frac <- function(prots, g) {
    x <- pep_g |> filter(tax == g)
    den <- colSums(OP$a[x$row, OP$d$sample, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
    num <- colSums(OP$a[x$row[x$Protein %in% prots], OP$d$sample, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
    OP$d |> mutate(f = num / den) |> filter(f > 0, f < 1)
  }
  gen <- count(pep_g, tax, sort = TRUE) |> filter(n >= 200) |> pull(tax)
  scan_c <- map_dfr(gen, function(g) {
    d <- g_frac(chap_new, g)
    if (nrow(d) < 20 || n_distinct(d$Mixture) < 2) return(NULL)
    cf <- coef(summary(lm(qlogis(f) ~ Mixture + resp, d)))
    if (!"respR" %in% rownames(cf)) return(NULL)
    tibble(genus = g, n = nrow(d), psm = sum(pep_g$tax == g),
           est = cf["respR", 1], p = cf["respR", 4])
  }) |> mutate(q = p.adjust(p, "BH")) |> arrange(p)
  cat("\n[3a] within-genus chaperone fraction, by response\n")
  print(as.data.frame(head(scan_c, 12)), row.names = FALSE, digits = 3)
  sc <- scan_c |> mutate(se = abs(est / qt(p / 2, df = n - 7, lower.tail = FALSE)), w = 1 / se^2)
  cat(sprintf("    genera %d; NR-up %d; BH q<0.10 %d; precision-weighted mean %+.4f; excluding the top genus %+.4f\n",
    nrow(sc), sum(sc$est < 0), sum(sc$q < 0.10), weighted.mean(sc$est, sc$w),
    weighted.mean(sc$est[-1], sc$w[-1])))

  ## (b) leave-one-genus-out on the paired model: does any one genus carry it?
  frac_excl <- function(prots, g_excl) {
    drop <- pep_g$row[pep_g$tax %in% g_excl]
    keep <- setdiff(seq_len(nrow(OP$a)), drop)
    num  <- colSums(OP$a[intersect(keep, which(OP$rd$Protein %in% prots)), OP$d$sample, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
    den  <- colSums(OP$a[keep, OP$d$sample, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
    OP$d |> select(sample, Mixture, resp) |> mutate(mp = num / den)
  }
  logo <- map_dfr(c("(none)", head(sc$genus, 8)), function(g) {
    d <- frac_excl(chap_new, if (g == "(none)") character(0) else g) |>
      inner_join(pc |> select(sample, mg), by = "sample") |>
      filter(is.finite(mp), mp > 0, mp < 1)
    cf <- coef(summary(lm(qlogis(mp) ~ Mixture + log(mg) + resp, data = d)))
    tibble(excluded = g, n = nrow(d), resp = cf["respR", 1], p = cf["respR", 4],
           beta_log_mg = cf["log(mg)", 1])
  })
  cat("\n[3b] paired chaperone model, leaving one genus out\n")
  print(as.data.frame(logo), row.names = FALSE, digits = 3)
  cat("    READING: if one exclusion moves `resp` toward zero the way Blautia did for\n",
      "            the ribosomal set, the chaperone companion is that genus and must not\n",
      "            be promoted to a main figure as a community-level result.\n")
  MP <<- MP
  G <<- G
  kos <<- kos
  pat <<- pat
  ## and again under names nothing later in the document reuses: §12a's
  ## sheba-db-composition defines `kos` as a function, which would otherwise
  ## leave this chunk's KO vector unreachable by the end of a full run.
  cpl_MP <<- MP
  cpl_G <<- G
  cpl_kos <<- kos
  cpl_pat <<- pat
  ## `pat` carries sample/bio/resp only. The per-patient statistics — own,
  ## mismatched, delta and the within-row rank p_own — live in `cpl` and were
  ## never exported, so anything downstream asking for cpl_pat$own got NULL and
  ## silently produced NA. Export both.
  cpl_stats <<- cpl
})
  ## EXPECTED: 47 paired patients, 1,320 KOs. own rho 0.238 vs mismatched 0.234,
  ##   delta +0.006, 27/47, p 0.166. log(mg): ribosomal 0.378 (p 0.011, partial R2
  ##   0.153), chaperone 0.722 (p 0.026, 0.121); resp with capacity in the model
  ##   ribosomal -0.192 (perm 0.010), chaperone -0.193 (0.043). Within-genus scan:
  ##   22 genera, none at BH q<0.10, precision-weighted -0.0396. Leave-one-genus-out
  ##   keeps resp between -0.19 and -0.20; excluding Blautia -0.199.
```

```{r systems-mg-vs-mp}
## ============================================================================
## SYSTEMS VIEW — metagenome (MG) vs metaproteome (MP), KEGG pathway level
## Genetic information processing vs energy (and other) metabolism, R vs NR
##
## Runs in the current Pittsburgh session. Needs: stat, em_p, ko_cpm,
## KEEP_5M; optionally st0 / st1 for the MP specification check.
##
## CONVENTION: every statistic is R - NR. NES < 0 = NR-up, NES > 0 = R-up.
## NES ONLY. fgsea internal p-values are not reportable on this design
## (null SD 0.98-1.41 across sets, displaced location); dropped, not hidden.
## ============================================================================

need <- c("stat", "em_p", "ko_cpm", "KEEP_5M")
miss <- need[!vapply(need, exists, logical(1))]
if (length(miss)) stop("missing from session: ", paste(miss, collapse = ", "))
suppressPackageStartupMessages({ library(fgsea); library(ggplot2) })

## ---- 1. KEGG pathway categories (from map number) -------------------------
## Umbrella maps (01100 "metabolic pathways" etc.) overlap everything and are
## dropped. 00970 aminoacyl-tRNA biosynthesis is TRANSLATION in KEGG BRITE
## despite its 00xxx number, so it is special-cased into information.
GLOBAL <- c(1100,1110,1120,1200,1210,1212,1220,1230,1232,1240,1250,1310,1320)
kegg_cat <- function(mapid) {
  n <- as.integer(sub("^map", "", mapid))
  dplyr::case_when(
    n %in% GLOBAL                                               ~ NA_character_,
    n == 970 | (n >= 3000 & n < 4000)                           ~ "Genetic information processing",
    n %in% c(190, 195, 196, 680, 710, 720, 910, 920)            ~ "Energy metabolism",
    n %in% c(10,20,30,40,51,52,53,500,520,562,620,630,640,650,660) ~ "Carbohydrate metabolism",
    n %in% c(220,250,260,270,280,290,300,310,330,340,350,360,380,400,410,430,450,460,470,480)
                                                                ~ "Amino acid metabolism",
    n %in% c(230, 240)                                          ~ "Nucleotide metabolism",
    n %in% c(130,670,730,740,750,760,770,780,785,790,830,860)   ~ "Cofactors & vitamins",
    n %in% c(61,62,71,72,73,100,120,121,140,561,564,565,590,591,592,600,1040)
                                                                ~ "Lipid metabolism",
    n >= 2000 & n < 3000                                        ~ "Environmental information processing",
    n >= 4000                                                   ~ NA_character_,
    TRUE                                                        ~ "Other metabolism")
}
CAT_ORDER <- c("Genetic information processing", "Environmental information processing",
               "Energy metabolism", "Carbohydrate metabolism", "Amino acid metabolism",
               "Nucleotide metabolism", "Cofactors & vitamins", "Lipid metabolism",
               "Other metabolism")

## Names for labelling. KEGGREST if online; a fixed dictionary otherwise.
KEY <- c(map03010 = "Ribosome", map03018 = "RNA degradation", map03020 = "RNA polymerase",
         map03030 = "DNA replication", map03060 = "Protein export",
         map00970 = "Aminoacyl-tRNA", map00190 = "Oxidative phosphorylation",
         map00680 = "Methane", map00910 = "Nitrogen", map00920 = "Sulfur",
         map00720 = "C fixation (prok.)", map00010 = "Glycolysis",
         map00020 = "TCA cycle", map00220 = "Arginine biosynth.",
         map02010 = "ABC transporters", map02060 = "PTS")
pw_names <- if (OFFLINE) KEY else tryCatch({
  x <- KEGGREST::keggList("pathway")
  setNames(unname(x), sub("^path:", "", names(x)))
}, error = function(e) KEY)

## ---- 2. MP — protein-level sets, the established unit ----------------------
mp_pairs <- em_p |>
  dplyr::select(query, KEGG_Pathway) |>
  dplyr::filter(query %in% names(stat), !is.na(KEGG_Pathway), KEGG_Pathway != "-") |>
  tidyr::separate_rows(KEGG_Pathway, sep = ",") |>
  dplyr::mutate(p = trimws(KEGG_Pathway)) |>
  dplyr::filter(grepl("^map\\d{5}$", p)) |>
  dplyr::distinct(query, p)
MP_SETS <- split(mp_pairs$query, mp_pairs$p)
MP_SETS <- MP_SETS[lengths(MP_SETS) >= 10 & !is.na(kegg_cat(names(MP_SETS)))]

set.seed(71)
fg_mp <- fgseaMultilevel(MP_SETS, stat, minSize = 10, maxSize = 2000, eps = 0) |>
  tibble::as_tibble() |> dplyr::transmute(pathway, size_mp = size, NES_mp = NES)

## ---- 3. MG — KO-level statistic on the depth-floored, labelled samples -----
## KO -> pathway built from SINGLE-KO genes only: a multi-KO gene would pass
## every one of its pathways to every one of its KOs.
ko2map <- em_p |>
  dplyr::select(KEGG_ko, KEGG_Pathway) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(KEGG_ko), KEGG_ko != "-", !grepl(",", KEGG_ko),
                !is.na(KEGG_Pathway), KEGG_Pathway != "-") |>
  dplyr::mutate(ko = sub("^ko:", "", KEGG_ko)) |>
  tidyr::separate_rows(KEGG_Pathway, sep = ",") |>
  dplyr::mutate(p = trimws(KEGG_Pathway)) |>
  dplyr::filter(grepl("^map\\d{5}$", p)) |>
  dplyr::distinct(ko, p)

mg <- ko_cpm |> dplyr::filter(sample %in% KEEP_5M, !is.na(resp))
c(mg_samples = dplyr::n_distinct(mg$sample),
  R  = dplyr::n_distinct(mg$sample[mg$resp == "R"]),
  NR = dplyr::n_distinct(mg$sample[mg$resp == "NR"]))
## ~68 labelled at the 5M floor; the KO table is 81 samples (MF0480 lost in
## regrouping), so this is a subset of §10b's 73.

tt <- function(x, g) {
  r <- x[g == "R"]; n <- x[g == "NR"]
  if (length(r) < 3 || length(n) < 3 || sd(x) == 0) return(NA_real_)
  tryCatch(unname(t.test(r, n)$statistic), error = function(e) NA_real_)   # R - NR
}
mg_stat <- mg |>
  dplyr::group_by(feature) |>
  dplyr::filter(mean(cpm > 0) >= 0.2) |>                 # prevalence floor
  dplyr::summarise(t = tt(log2(cpm + 1), resp), .groups = "drop")
st_mg <- setNames(mg_stat$t, mg_stat$feature); st_mg <- st_mg[is.finite(st_mg)]
c(mg_KOs_ranked = length(st_mg))

MG_SETS <- split(ko2map$ko, ko2map$p)
MG_SETS <- lapply(MG_SETS, intersect, names(st_mg))
MG_SETS <- MG_SETS[lengths(MG_SETS) >= 10 & !is.na(kegg_cat(names(MG_SETS)))]

set.seed(72)
fg_mg <- fgseaMultilevel(MG_SETS, st_mg, minSize = 10, maxSize = 2000, eps = 0) |>
  tibble::as_tibble() |> dplyr::transmute(pathway, size_mg = size, NES_mg = NES)

## ---- 4. Join and summarise --------------------------------------------------
sysv <- dplyr::full_join(fg_mp, fg_mg, by = "pathway") |>
  dplyr::mutate(category = factor(kegg_cat(pathway), levels = CAT_ORDER),
                name = dplyr::coalesce(unname(pw_names[pathway]), pathway),
                name = sub(" - .*$", "", name)) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(category))

c(pathways = nrow(sysv), in_both = sum(!is.na(sysv$NES_mp) & !is.na(sysv$NES_mg)))

## Per-category medians — the systems-level summary
cat_tab <- sysv |>
  dplyr::group_by(category) |>
  dplyr::summarise(n_mp = sum(!is.na(NES_mp)), med_MP = median(NES_mp, na.rm = TRUE),
                   n_mg = sum(!is.na(NES_mg)), med_MG = median(NES_mg, na.rm = TRUE),
                   frac_MP_NRup = mean(NES_mp < 0, na.rm = TRUE),
                   frac_MG_NRup = mean(NES_mg < 0, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
print(as.data.frame(cat_tab), digits = 3)

## Cross-layer concordance on shared pathways
both <- sysv |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(NES_mp), !is.na(NES_mg))
c(rho_all = cor(both$NES_mp, both$NES_mg, method = "spearman"),
  sign_agree = mean(sign(both$NES_mp) == sign(both$NES_mg)), n = nrow(both))
both |> dplyr::group_by(category) |>
  dplyr::summarise(n = dplyr::n(),
                   rho = if (dplyr::n() >= 5) cor(NES_mp, NES_mg, method = "spearman") else NA_real_,
                   sign_agree = mean(sign(NES_mp) == sign(NES_mg)), .groups = "drop") |>
  as.data.frame()

## The two focal categories, pathway by pathway
sysv |> dplyr::filter(category %in% c("Genetic information processing", "Energy metabolism")) |>
  dplyr::arrange(category, NES_mp) |>
  dplyr::select(category, pathway, name, size_mp, NES_mp, size_mg, NES_mg) |>
  as.data.frame()

## ---- 5. MP specification check (optional) -----------------------------------
## Specification check: MP information processing is sign-stable, MP
## metabolism is NOT. Same universe both ways (limma, 1,857 proteins).
if (exists("st0") && exists("st1")) {
  spec <- lapply(list(cond = st1, uncond = st0), function(s) {
    ss <- lapply(MP_SETS, intersect, names(s)); ss <- ss[lengths(ss) >= 10]
    fgseaMultilevel(ss, s, minSize = 10, maxSize = 2000, eps = 0) |>
      tibble::as_tibble() |> dplyr::select(pathway, NES)
  })
  spec_tab <- dplyr::inner_join(spec$cond, spec$uncond, by = "pathway",
                                suffix = c("_cond", "_uncond")) |>
    dplyr::mutate(category = kegg_cat(pathway)) |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(category)) |>
    dplyr::group_by(category) |>
    dplyr::summarise(n = dplyr::n(),
                     sign_stable = mean(sign(NES_cond) == sign(NES_uncond)),
                     med_cond = median(NES_cond), med_uncond = median(NES_uncond),
                     .groups = "drop")
  print(as.data.frame(spec_tab), digits = 3)
}

## ---- 6. Figure --------------------------------------------------------------
long <- sysv |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(NES_mp, NES_mg), names_to = "layer", values_to = "NES") |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(NES)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(layer = factor(ifelse(layer == "NES_mp", "Metaproteome", "Metagenome"),
                               levels = c("Metaproteome", "Metagenome")),
                category = forcats::fct_rev(category))
meds <- long |> dplyr::group_by(category, layer) |>
  dplyr::summarise(NES = median(NES), .groups = "drop")

pA <- ggplot(long, aes(NES, category, colour = layer)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.height = 0.15, dodge.width = 0.6,
                                             seed = 1), alpha = 0.45, size = 1.4) +
  geom_point(data = meds, position = position_dodge(width = 0.6),
             shape = 124, size = 7, stroke = 1.2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Metaproteome = "#B23A48", Metagenome = "#2E6F95")) +
  labs(x = "NES  (\u2190 NR-up        R-up \u2192)", y = NULL, colour = NULL,
       title = "A. Pathway enrichment by KEGG category",
       subtitle = "each point a pathway; bar = category median") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) + theme(legend.position = "top",
                                        panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

focal <- c("Genetic information processing", "Energy metabolism")
pB <- ggplot(both |> dplyr::mutate(focal = ifelse(category %in% focal,
                                                  as.character(category), "Other")),
             aes(NES_mp, NES_mg)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = 3, colour = "grey60") +
  geom_point(aes(colour = focal, size = focal), alpha = 0.7) +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = ~ dplyr::filter(.x, pathway %in% names(KEY)),
                           aes(label = unname(KEY[pathway])), size = 3,
                           max.overlaps = 30, seed = 1) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Genetic information processing" = "#B23A48",
                                 "Energy metabolism" = "#E09F3E", Other = "grey70")) +
  scale_size_manual(values = c("Genetic information processing" = 2.4,
                               "Energy metabolism" = 2.4, Other = 1.2), guide = "none") +
  annotate("text", x = -Inf, y = -Inf, hjust = -0.1, vjust = -0.6, size = 3,
           label = "both NR-up", colour = "grey40") +
  annotate("text", x = Inf, y = Inf, hjust = 1.1, vjust = 1.6, size = 3,
           label = "both R-up", colour = "grey40") +
  labs(x = "Metaproteome NES", y = "Metagenome NES", colour = NULL,
       title = "B. Same pathway, two layers") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) + theme(legend.position = "top",
                                        panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

fig <- tryCatch(patchwork::wrap_plots(pA, pB, ncol = 2, widths = c(1.1, 1)),
                error = function(e) NULL)
out <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "systems_MG_vs_MP")
if (!is.null(fig)) {
  ggsave(paste0(out, ".pdf"), fig, width = 14, height = 6.5)
} else {
  ggsave(paste0(out, "_A.pdf"), pA, width = 7.5, height = 6.5)
  ggsave(paste0(out, "_B.pdf"), pB, width = 7, height = 6.5)
}
readr::write_csv(sysv, paste0(out, "_pathways.csv"))
readr::write_csv(cat_tab, paste0(out, "_categories.csv"))
message("written: ", out, "*")
```

```{r a1b-leverage}
local({
  ## A1b — does the own-vs-mismatched test have any leverage?
  ##
  ## A1 §1 found own rho 0.238 against mismatched 0.234. That is evidence for a
  ## dissociation ONLY if the paired metagenomes differ from each other in the first
  ## place. If they are near-identical, a mismatched metagenome is almost the same
  ## input and delta ~ 0 measures the design, not the biology.
  ##
  ## Scale matters here: with a 1e-9 pseudocount an absent KO sits at log = -20.7,
  ## so both "similarity" and "variability" are otherwise dominated by presence and
  ## absence rather than by quantity. Everything below uses log1p(CPM), and the
  ## variable-KO ranking is computed on the CORE set (present in nearly every
  ## patient) so that it reflects quantitative variation.
  ##
  ## Run after A1 in the same session (reuses MP, G, kos, pat).

  EPS <- 1e-9

  ## ---- inputs: verify, and rebuild if the session has moved on -----------------
  ## MP, G, kos and pat are left behind by A1. `G` is a one-letter name and the
  ## session also uses "G" as a COG set label, so it is easily overwritten; this
  ## rebuilds from source rather than trusting what is in the workspace.
  ok_mat <- function(nm) exists(nm) && is.matrix(get(nm)) &&
    !is.null(rownames(get(nm))) && !is.null(colnames(get(nm)))
  ## CONTENT FOR THESE TWO AS WELL, and for the reason §0a records. §12a
  ## redefines `kos` as a FUNCTION, and `pat` is a short name several chunks
  ## reuse, so a bare exists() returns TRUE for the wrong object, this guard
  ## passes, and the rebuild below is skipped -- leaving the chunk to fail
  ## later on `pat$bio` or on a function where a KO vector belongs.
  ok_kos <- function() exists("kos") && is.character(kos) && length(kos) > 0
  ok_pat <- function() exists("pat") && is.data.frame(pat) &&
    all(c("sample", "bio") %in% names(pat))
  if (!ok_mat("MP") || !ok_mat("G") || !ok_kos() || !ok_pat()) {
    for (nm in c("MP", "G")) if (exists(nm) && !ok_mat(nm))
      message("NOTE: `", nm, "` in the session is ", paste(class(get(nm)), collapse = "/"),
              " of length ", length(get(nm)), " — not the matrix A1 built. Rebuilding.")
    need2 <- c("OP", "smap", "norm_id", "ko_cpm", "KEEP_5M", "annot_new")
    m2 <- need2[!vapply(need2, exists, logical(1))]
    if (length(m2)) stop("cannot rebuild; missing: ", paste(m2, collapse = ", "))
    ko_of <- setNames(annot_new$ko_primary[annot_new$cohort == "pitt"],
                      annot_new$protein[annot_new$cohort == "pitt"])
    rws <- tibble::tibble(row = seq_len(nrow(OP$a)), protein = OP$rd$Protein) |>
      dplyr::mutate(ko = unname(ko_of[protein])) |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(ko))
    Msum <- rowsum(OP$a[rws$row, OP$d$sample, drop = FALSE], group = rws$ko, na.rm = TRUE)
    MP <- sweep(Msum, 2, colSums(Msum, na.rm = TRUE), "/")
    pat <- OP$d |> dplyr::select(sample, Mixture, resp) |>
      dplyr::inner_join(smap |> dplyr::select(sample, BioReplicate), by = "sample") |>
      dplyr::mutate(bio = norm_id(BioReplicate))
    MGw <- ko_cpm |> dplyr::filter(sample %in% KEEP_5M) |>
      dplyr::group_by(bio, feature) |> dplyr::summarise(cpm = sum(cpm), .groups = "drop") |>
      tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = bio, values_from = cpm, values_fill = 0)
    G <- as.matrix(MGw[, -1]); rownames(G) <- MGw$feature
    pat <- pat |> dplyr::filter(bio %in% colnames(G), sample %in% colnames(MP))
    kos <- intersect(rownames(MP), rownames(G))
    message(sprintf("rebuilt: %d patients, %d KOs in both layers", nrow(pat), length(kos)))
  }
  stopifnot(ok_mat("MP"), ok_mat("G"), length(kos) >= 100, nrow(pat) >= 20)

  Gp <- G[kos, pat$bio, drop = FALSE]                 # metagenome, KOs x patients
  Mp <- MP[kos, pat$sample, drop = FALSE]             # proteome,  KOs x samples
  pres <- rowMeans(Gp > 0)
  core <- names(pres)[pres >= 0.9]                    # present in >= 90% of patients

  ## ---- 1. between-patient similarity, on a sane scale -------------------------
  off_diag <- function(M) { x <- cor(M, method = "spearman"); x[lower.tri(x)] }
  cg_all  <- off_diag(log1p(Gp))
  cg_core <- off_diag(log1p(Gp[core, , drop = FALSE]))
  cm_all  <- off_diag(log1p(Mp * 1e6))
  cat(sprintf(
  "[1] between-patient similarity (log1p scale)\n    metagenome, all %4d KOs : median rho %.3f (IQR %.3f-%.3f)\n    metagenome, %4d core KOs: median rho %.3f (IQR %.3f-%.3f)\n    proteome,   all %4d KOs : median rho %.3f (IQR %.3f-%.3f)\n",
    length(kos), median(cg_all),  quantile(cg_all, .25),  quantile(cg_all, .75),
    length(core), median(cg_core), quantile(cg_core, .25), quantile(cg_core, .75),
    length(kos), median(cm_all),  quantile(cm_all, .25),  quantile(cm_all, .75)))
  cat("    Metagenome similarity near 1.0 on the CORE set would mean the mismatched\n",
      "    control is nearly the same input, and A1 §1 has little leverage.\n")

  sd_core <- apply(log1p(Gp[core, , drop = FALSE]), 1, sd)
  cat(sprintf("    core-KO between-patient SD of log1p(CPM): median %.3f, IQR %.3f-%.3f, top decile > %.3f\n",
    median(sd_core), quantile(sd_core, .25), quantile(sd_core, .75), quantile(sd_core, .90)))

  ## ---- 2. the same test, restricted to KOs that actually vary -----------------
  coup_on <- function(k, s, b) {
    x <- MP[k, s]; y <- G[k, b]; keep <- is.finite(x) & x > 0
    if (sum(keep) < 30) return(NA_real_)
    suppressWarnings(cor(log(x[keep] + EPS), log(y[keep] + EPS), method = "spearman"))
  }
  pair_matrix <- function(k) {
    n <- nrow(pat)
    vapply(seq_len(n), function(j)                      # columns = metagenome
      vapply(seq_len(n), function(i) coup_on(k, pat$sample[i], pat$bio[j]), 0),
      numeric(n))
  }
  ranked <- names(sort(sd_core, decreasing = TRUE))
  sets <- list(`core, top 100 by SD`  = head(ranked, 100),
               `core, top 200 by SD`  = head(ranked, 200),
               `core, top 500 by SD`  = head(ranked, 500),
               `core, all`            = ranked,
               `all KOs (as in A1)`   = kos)

  res <- bind_rows(lapply(names(sets), function(nm) {
    k <- sets[[nm]]
    if (length(k) < 30) return(NULL)
    K   <- pair_matrix(k)
    stopifnot(identical(dim(K), c(nrow(pat), nrow(pat))))
    own <- diag(K)
    mis <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(pat)), function(i) median(K[i, -i], na.rm = TRUE), 0)
    rk  <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(pat)), function(i) mean(K[i, -i] >= own[i], na.rm = TRUE), 0)
    ## summarise into plain values FIRST — inside tibble(), a later argument would
    ## see the new `own` column instead of this vector.
    v_own <- median(own, na.rm = TRUE); v_mis <- median(mis, na.rm = TRUE)
    v_del <- median(own - mis, na.rm = TRUE); v_hi <- sum(own > mis, na.rm = TRUE)
    v_p   <- suppressWarnings(wilcox.test(own, mis, paired = TRUE))$p.value
    tibble(restriction = nm, kos_used = length(k),
           min_sd = if (nm == "all KOs (as in A1)") NA_real_ else round(min(sd_core[k]), 3),
           own = v_own, mismatched = v_mis, delta = v_del,
           own_higher = v_hi, n = nrow(pat), p_paired = v_p,
           patients_p05 = sum(rk < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE))
  }))
  cat("\n[2] own vs mismatched, by restriction\n")
  print(as.data.frame(res), row.names = FALSE, digits = 3)
  cat("\n    READING: if delta stays ~0 as the restriction tightens onto variable core\n",
      "            KOs, capacity genuinely does not predict output patient-specifically\n",
      "            and A1 §1 stands. If delta grows, the full-profile test was diluted\n",
      "            and the claim must be stated on this subset.\n")
})
  ## EXPECTED: metagenome similarity, all KOs rho 0.847; 856 core KOs rho 0.780;
  ##   proteome 0.691. Core-KO SD median 0.785. delta by restriction: top 100
  ##   +0.0380 (p 0.026), top 200 +0.0333 (p 0.00028, 34/47), top 500 +0.0104,
  ##   core all +0.0110, all KOs +0.0062. The full profile dilutes.
```

```{r b2-paired-formal}
local({
  ## B2 — turn the own-vs-stranger observation into a formal result.
  ## Three things the current version lacks: a per-patient delta against the FULL
  ## mismatched distribution rather than its median; the coupling as a continuous
  ## function of between-patient gene variability rather than a top-200 threshold;
  ## and a variance partition saying how much protein output is common structure,
  ## how much is the patient's own capacity, and how much is patient state.
  ## Run after A1 (reuses MP, G, kos, pat; rebuilds nothing).

  EPS <- 1e-9

  ## ---- inputs: verify, and rebuild if the session has moved on -----------------
  ## MP, G, kos and pat are left behind by A1. `G` is a one-letter name and the
  ## session also uses "G" as a COG set label, so it is easily overwritten; this
  ## rebuilds from source rather than trusting what is in the workspace.
  ok_mat <- function(nm) exists(nm) && is.matrix(get(nm)) &&
    !is.null(rownames(get(nm))) && !is.null(colnames(get(nm)))
  ## CONTENT FOR THESE TWO AS WELL, and for the reason §0a records. §12a
  ## redefines `kos` as a FUNCTION, and `pat` is a short name several chunks
  ## reuse, so a bare exists() returns TRUE for the wrong object, this guard
  ## passes, and the rebuild below is skipped -- leaving the chunk to fail
  ## later on `pat$bio` or on a function where a KO vector belongs.
  ok_kos <- function() exists("kos") && is.character(kos) && length(kos) > 0
  ok_pat <- function() exists("pat") && is.data.frame(pat) &&
    all(c("sample", "bio") %in% names(pat))
  if (!ok_mat("MP") || !ok_mat("G") || !ok_kos() || !ok_pat()) {
    for (nm in c("MP", "G")) if (exists(nm) && !ok_mat(nm))
      message("NOTE: `", nm, "` in the session is ", paste(class(get(nm)), collapse = "/"),
              " of length ", length(get(nm)), " — not the matrix A1 built. Rebuilding.")
    need2 <- c("OP", "smap", "norm_id", "ko_cpm", "KEEP_5M", "annot_new")
    m2 <- need2[!vapply(need2, exists, logical(1))]
    if (length(m2)) stop("cannot rebuild; missing: ", paste(m2, collapse = ", "))
    ko_of <- setNames(annot_new$ko_primary[annot_new$cohort == "pitt"],
                      annot_new$protein[annot_new$cohort == "pitt"])
    rws <- tibble::tibble(row = seq_len(nrow(OP$a)), protein = OP$rd$Protein) |>
      dplyr::mutate(ko = unname(ko_of[protein])) |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(ko))
    Msum <- rowsum(OP$a[rws$row, OP$d$sample, drop = FALSE], group = rws$ko, na.rm = TRUE)
    MP <- sweep(Msum, 2, colSums(Msum, na.rm = TRUE), "/")
    pat <- OP$d |> dplyr::select(sample, Mixture, resp) |>
      dplyr::inner_join(smap |> dplyr::select(sample, BioReplicate), by = "sample") |>
      dplyr::mutate(bio = norm_id(BioReplicate))
    MGw <- ko_cpm |> dplyr::filter(sample %in% KEEP_5M) |>
      dplyr::group_by(bio, feature) |> dplyr::summarise(cpm = sum(cpm), .groups = "drop") |>
      tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = bio, values_from = cpm, values_fill = 0)
    G <- as.matrix(MGw[, -1]); rownames(G) <- MGw$feature
    pat <- pat |> dplyr::filter(bio %in% colnames(G), sample %in% colnames(MP))
    kos <- intersect(rownames(MP), rownames(G))
    message(sprintf("rebuilt: %d patients, %d KOs in both layers", nrow(pat), length(kos)))
  }
  stopifnot(ok_mat("MP"), ok_mat("G"), length(kos) >= 100, nrow(pat) >= 20)

  Gp <- G[kos, pat$bio, drop = FALSE]; Mp <- MP[kos, pat$sample, drop = FALSE]

  coup <- function(k, i, j) {
    x <- MP[k, pat$sample[i]]; y <- G[k, pat$bio[j]]; keep <- is.finite(x) & x > 0
    if (sum(keep) < 30) return(NA_real_)
    suppressWarnings(cor(log(x[keep] + EPS), log(y[keep] + EPS), method = "spearman"))
  }
  Kmat <- function(k) vapply(seq_len(nrow(pat)), function(j)
    vapply(seq_len(nrow(pat)), function(i) coup(k, i, j), 0), numeric(nrow(pat)))

  ## ---- 1. per patient, against the whole mismatched distribution --------------
  K <- Kmat(kos); own <- diag(K)
  per <- tibble(sample = pat$sample, resp = pat$resp, own = own,
                mis_mean = vapply(seq_len(nrow(pat)), function(i) mean(K[i, -i], na.rm = TRUE), 0),
                mis_sd   = vapply(seq_len(nrow(pat)), function(i) sd(K[i, -i], na.rm = TRUE), 0)) |>
    mutate(delta = own - mis_mean, z = delta / mis_sd,
           pctile = vapply(seq_len(nrow(pat)), function(i) mean(K[i, -i] < own[i], na.rm = TRUE), 0))
  cat(sprintf("[1] per-patient delta: median %+.4f (IQR %+.4f to %+.4f); median z %+.2f; own above its own mismatched mean in %d of %d\n",
      median(per$delta), quantile(per$delta,.25), quantile(per$delta,.75), median(per$z),
      sum(per$delta > 0), nrow(per)))
  cat(sprintf("    one-sample Wilcoxon on delta: p = %.3g\n",
              suppressWarnings(wilcox.test(per$delta))$p.value))

  ## ---- 2. coupling as a continuous function of gene variability ---------------
  pres <- rowMeans(Gp > 0); core <- names(pres)[pres >= 0.9]
  sd_core <- apply(log1p(Gp[core, , drop = FALSE]), 1, sd)
  r <- rank(-sd_core); n <- length(core); bins <- cut(r, breaks = quantile(r, seq(0, 1, .2)),
                                                      include.lowest = TRUE, labels = paste0("Q", 1:5))
  prof <- bind_rows(lapply(levels(bins), function(b) {
    k <- core[bins == b]; Kb <- Kmat(k); ow <- diag(Kb)
    ms <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(pat)), function(i) mean(Kb[i, -i], na.rm = TRUE), 0)
    tibble(bin = b, n_ko = length(k), median_sd = median(sd_core[k]),
           own = median(ow, na.rm = TRUE), mismatched = median(ms, na.rm = TRUE),
           delta = median(ow - ms, na.rm = TRUE),
           p = suppressWarnings(wilcox.test(ow, ms, paired = TRUE))$p.value)
  }))
  cat("\n[2] coupling by gene variability (Q1 = most variable core KOs)\n")
  print(as.data.frame(prof), row.names = FALSE, digits = 3)
  cat(sprintf("    Spearman(delta, median between-patient SD of the bin) = %.3f\n",
              cor(prof$delta, prof$median_sd, method = "spearman")))

  ## ---- 3. variance partition of protein output --------------------------------
  ## Sequential R^2, each term added to the last: KO identity (structure common to
  ## all guts) -> that patient's own gene abundance -> patient identity (state).
  long <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(pat)), function(i) {
    x <- Mp[, i]; y <- Gp[, i]; k <- is.finite(x) & x > 0
    data.frame(y = log(x[k] + EPS), ko = kos[k], patient = pat$sample[i], cap = log(y[k] + EPS))
  }))
  r2 <- function(f) summary(lm(as.formula(f), data = long))$r.squared
  a <- r2("y ~ ko"); b <- r2("y ~ ko + cap"); d <- r2("y ~ ko + cap + patient")
  cat(sprintf("\n[3] variance in log protein share (%d patient-KO observations)\n    KO identity %.5f | + own gene abundance %.5f (+%.5f) | + patient %.5f (+%.5f)\n",
              nrow(long), a, b, b - a, d, d - b))
  cat("    READING: the middle increment is what a patient's own metagenome adds\n",
      "            beyond structure common to every gut.\n")
})
  ## EXPECTED: per-patient delta median +0.0081 (z +0.39), 29/47, Wilcoxon 0.0875.
  ##   By variability quintile (Q1 most variable): +0.0243 (p 0.00125), +0.0174,
  ##   -0.0147, -0.0049, +0.0163 — only Q1 carries it. Variance in log protein
  ##   share over 32,912 patient-KO rows, five decimals: KO identity 0.75092,
  ##   + own gene abundance 0.75103 (+0.00010), + patient 0.75778 (+0.00675).
```

```{r b10-per-ko-slopes}
local({
  ## B10 — does the pooled +0.000 hide real per-KO coupling?
  ##
  ## B2's variance partition put KO identity at 75.1% and a patient's own gene
  ## abundance at +0.000 on top of it. That is ONE pooled slope across every KO and
  ## patient. If per-KO slopes are sign-heterogeneous, real couplings average to
  ## zero and the partition understates them. §2.3 currently rests on that number.
  ##
  ## Per KO, across patients, regress log protein share on log gene CPM. Then judge
  ## the distribution of slopes against a null built by SHUFFLING THE PAIRING —
  ## each patient's proteome scored against another patient's metagenome — which
  ## preserves every marginal and destroys only the correspondence.
  ##
  ## Run after A1 (MP, G, kos, pat) or in a session where §11a has run.

  ok_mat <- function(nm) exists(nm) && is.matrix(get(nm)) &&
    !is.null(rownames(get(nm))) && !is.null(colnames(get(nm)))
  ## CONTENT, NOT PRESENCE -- §12a redefines `kos` as a function and `pat` is a
  ## reused short name, so a bare exists() lets the wrong object through and
  ## this stop() never fires. Same rule as §0a's guards.
  ok_kos <- function() exists("kos") && is.character(kos) && length(kos) > 0
  ok_pat <- function() exists("pat") && is.data.frame(pat) &&
    all(c("sample", "bio") %in% names(pat))
  if (!ok_mat("MP") || !ok_mat("G") || !ok_kos() || !ok_pat())
    stop("run A1_capacity_output_coupling.R (or §11a) first: MP, G, kos, pat needed")
  set.seed(1001); NPERM <- 200L; MIN_PAT <- 20L; EPS <- 1e-9

  X <- log(MP[kos, pat$sample, drop = FALSE] + EPS)     # protein, KO x patient
  Y <- log(G[kos, pat$bio, drop = FALSE] + EPS)         # genes, same order
  stopifnot(identical(dim(X), dim(Y)))
  detected <- MP[kos, pat$sample, drop = FALSE] > 0
  use <- rowSums(detected) >= MIN_PAT
  cat(sprintf("%d KOs detected in >= %d of %d patients\n", sum(use), MIN_PAT, ncol(X)))

  slopes <- function(perm) {                      # perm: column order for the gene layer
    vapply(which(use), function(i) {
      k <- detected[i, ]
      x <- Y[i, perm][k]; y <- X[i, ][k]
      if (sd(x) == 0 || sd(y) == 0) return(NA_real_)
      unname(coef(lm(y ~ x))[2])
    }, 0)
  }
  obs <- slopes(seq_len(ncol(Y)))
  nl  <- replicate(NPERM, {
    p <- sample(ncol(Y)); while (any(p == seq_len(ncol(Y)))) p <- sample(ncol(Y))
    s <- slopes(p); c(median(s, na.rm = TRUE), mean(s > 0, na.rm = TRUE))
  })
  summ <- c(median = median(obs, na.rm = TRUE), frac_pos = mean(obs > 0, na.rm = TRUE))
  cat(sprintf("\n[1] per-KO slopes (%d estimable)\n    observed  median %+.4f, positive in %.1f%%\n    shuffled  median %+.4f (95%% %.4f to %.4f), positive in %.1f%% (95%% %.1f to %.1f)\n",
    sum(!is.na(obs)), summ[["median"]], 100 * summ[["frac_pos"]],
    median(nl[1, ]), quantile(nl[1, ], .025), quantile(nl[1, ], .975),
    100 * median(nl[2, ]), 100 * quantile(nl[2, ], .025), 100 * quantile(nl[2, ], .975)))
  p_med <- (1 + sum(abs(nl[1, ] - median(nl[1, ])) >= abs(summ[["median"]] - median(nl[1, ])))) / (1 + NPERM)
  p_pos <- (1 + sum(abs(nl[2, ] - median(nl[2, ])) >= abs(summ[["frac_pos"]] - median(nl[2, ])))) / (1 + NPERM)
  cat(sprintf("    permutation p: median %.3f, fraction positive %.3f\n", p_med, p_pos))

  res <- tibble(ko = rownames(X)[use], slope = obs,
                n_pat = rowSums(detected)[use],
                sd_genes = apply(Y[use, , drop = FALSE], 1, sd)) |> arrange(desc(slope))
  cat("\n[2] strongest per-KO couplings\n")
  print(as.data.frame(head(res, 10)), row.names = FALSE, digits = 3)
  cat(sprintf("    Spearman(slope, between-patient SD of the gene) = %.3f — B2 found the\n    coupling concentrated in variable KOs; this says whether that holds per KO\n",
              cor(res$slope, res$sd_genes, method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs")))

  real <- p_pos < 0.05 || p_med < 0.05
  cat("\n---- verdict ----\n", if (real)
  "MASKED COUPLING. The per-KO slope distribution is displaced from the shuffled
  null, so real patient-specific coupling exists at the level of individual
  functions and the pooled +0.000 understates it. Read the MAGNITUDE before acting
  on the p-value: a median slope near 0.007 means doubling a gene's abundance moves
  its protein by well under one percent, which is detectable and negligible at the
  same time. §2.3 should say both." else
  "POOLED RESULT STANDS. The per-KO slopes are indistinguishable from what
  shuffling the pairing produces, so the +0.000 increment is not hiding
  sign-heterogeneous couplings. §2.3's wording holds, and this is the control that
  justifies it.", "\n")
})
  ## EXPECTED: 679 KOs in >=20 of 47 patients, 675 estimable. Observed median slope
  ##   +0.0074, positive in 55.1%; shuffled-pairing null median -0.0004 (95% -0.0060
  ##   to +0.0064), positive in 49.7%. Permutation p: median 0.015, fraction positive
  ##   0.060. Displaced but negligible. Spearman(slope, gene SD) -0.092.
```

## 11b. Response conditioned on gene capacity, and one genus that does not replicate {#paired}

In the 47 patients carrying both layers, gene capacity predicts protein share
(`log(mg)` 0.378 ribosomal, 0.722 chaperone; partial R² 0.15 and 0.12), and the
response difference **survives with capacity in the model**: ribosomal −0.192
(within-plex permutation p = 0.010), chaperone −0.193 (p = 0.043). That is the
evidence that the response signal sits in output rather than capacity, patient by
patient, and it is stronger than the unpaired comparison of gene content (§10c,
p = 0.238), which sets 72 metagenomes against 55 proteomes.

No single genus carries the chaperone version: leaving any one genus out moves
the coefficient between −0.19 and −0.20, and excluding *Blautia* strengthens it
to −0.199. Within genera the effect is about a fifth of the community-level one
(precision-weighted −0.040; nothing at BH q < 0.10 across 22 genera), a third
line of evidence that composition carries much of the difference (§8f).

The ribosomal set behaves differently. Do non-responders carry more ribosomal
protein than their gene capacity predicts? In *Blautia*, yes; across 25 testable
genera the precision-weighted effect is **−0.002 (p = 0.93)**, and a KO-matched
test in Sheba fails. Reported as a negative.

```{r paired-mg-mp}
## RENAMED 24 Sep 2026: these residual vectors were called `r2`, which is the

## before the export, so the exported `r2` was this chunk's residuals and S1C

  dplyr::inner_join(smap |> dplyr::select(sample, BioReplicate), by = "sample") |>
  dplyr::mutate(bio = norm_id(BioReplicate))

## protein beyond capacity — the resp term is the claim
summary(lm(qlogis(mp) ~ Mixture + log(mg) + resp, data = pr))
## and the ratio form
summary(lm(log2(mp / mg) ~ Mixture + resp, data = pr))

rc <- function(y, d, r) { cf <- coef(summary(lm(y ~ d$Mixture + log(d$mg) + r)))
                          cf[grep("^r", rownames(cf)), 1] }
obs <- rc(qlogis(pr$mp), pr, pr$resp)
set.seed(4701)
nl <- replicate(1000, rc(qlogis(pr$mp), pr,
        factor(ave(as.character(pr$resp), pr$Mixture, FUN = sample),
               levels = levels(pr$resp))))
c(obs = obs, null_med = median(nl), null_sd = sd(nl),
  p_two = (1 + sum(abs(nl) >= abs(obs))) / (1 + length(nl)))

## and whether the 8 unpaired patients were lost at random
lost <- setdiff(OP$d$sample, pr$sample)
table(OP$d$resp[OP$d$sample %in% lost])

## ---- 2. The chaperone companion --------------------------------------------------

mp_c <- chap_frac_of(OP, chap_new) |> dplyr::select(sample, Mixture, resp, mp = frac) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(smap |> dplyr::select(sample, BioReplicate), by = "sample") |>
  dplyr::mutate(bio = norm_id(BioReplicate))
mg_c <- ko_cpm |> dplyr::filter(feature %in% CHAPERONE_KO, sample %in% KEEP_5M) |>
  dplyr::group_by(bio) |> dplyr::summarise(mg = sum(cpm) / 1e6, .groups = "drop")

c(paired = nrow(pc))

## the growth-law test: do the two "beyond capacity" residuals co-vary within patient?
rr <- residuals(lm(qlogis(mp) ~ Mixture + log(mg), data = pr))
rc <- residuals(lm(qlogis(mp) ~ Mixture + log(mg), data = pc))
cor.test(rr[match(pc$bio, pr$bio)], rc, method = "spearman")

## ---- 3. Co-variation, and its controls (shared denominator, composition) ----------

num_of <- function(O, prots) {
  rows <- which(O$rd$Protein %in% prots)
  tibble::tibble(sample = O$d$sample,
                 num = colSums(O$a[rows, O$d$sample, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE),
                 tot = colSums(O$a[, O$d$sample, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE))
}
dd <- num_of(OP, ribo_new) |> dplyr::rename(rib = num) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(num_of(OP, chap_new) |> dplyr::select(sample, chp = num), by = "sample") |>
  dplyr::inner_join(pr |> dplyr::select(sample, Mixture, resp, mg_r = mg), by = "sample") |>
  dplyr::inner_join(pc |> dplyr::select(sample, mg_c = mg), by = "sample")

## does co-variation survive with the denominator partialled out?
r1 <- residuals(lm(log(rib) ~ Mixture + log(tot) + log(mg_r), dd))
resid_chp <- residuals(lm(log(chp) ~ Mixture + log(tot) + log(mg_c), dd))
cor.test(r1, resid_chp, method = "spearman")

## and the resp effects with tot free rather than fixed at 1
for (f in c("log(rib) ~ Mixture + log(tot) + log(mg_r) + resp",
            "log(chp) ~ Mixture + log(tot) + log(mg_c) + resp"))
  print(round(coef(summary(lm(as.formula(f), dd)))[c("log(tot)","respR"), ], 4))

names(phy); unique(phy$phylum)[1:8]

ph <- if ("bio" %in% names(phy)) phy else
  phy |> dplyr::inner_join(mg_meta |> dplyr::select(sample, bio), by = "sample")

comp <- ph |>
```
