```{r paired-mg-mp}
  dplyr::group_by(bio, phylum) |> dplyr::summarise(pct = sum(pct), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = phylum, values_from = pct, values_fill = 0)
c(patients = nrow(comp), cols = paste(names(comp), collapse = ","))

dd2 <- dd |> dplyr::inner_join(pr |> dplyr::select(sample, bio), by = "sample") |>
  dplyr::inner_join(comp, by = "bio") |>
  dplyr::mutate(FB = log((Firmicutes + 0.1) / (Bacteroidota + 0.1)))
c(n = nrow(dd2))                         ## expect 47

r1 <- residuals(lm(log(rib) ~ Mixture + log(tot) + log(mg_r) + FB, dd2))
resid_chp <- residuals(lm(log(chp) ~ Mixture + log(tot) + log(mg_c) + FB, dd2))
cor.test(r1, resid_chp, method = "spearman")
for (f in c("log(rib) ~ Mixture + log(tot) + log(mg_r) + FB + resp",
            "log(chp) ~ Mixture + log(tot) + log(mg_c) + FB + resp"))
  print(round(coef(summary(lm(as.formula(f), dd2)))[c("FB","respR"), ], 4))

## ---- 4. Within Bacillota -------------------------------------------------------

stopifnot(identical(DR3$sample, DC3$sample))
cor.test(residuals(lm(qlogis(DR3$frac) ~ DR3$Mixture)),
         residuals(lm(qlogis(DC3$frac) ~ DC3$Mixture)), method = "spearman")

## ---- 5. Within Blautia, its permutation null, and every genus ---------------------

g_frac <- function(prots, g) { x <- pep_g |> dplyr::filter(tax == g)
  den <- colSums(OP$a[x$row, OP$d$sample, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
  num <- colSums(OP$a[x$row[x$Protein %in% prots], OP$d$sample, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
  OP$d |> dplyr::mutate(f = num / den) |> dplyr::filter(f > 0, f < 1) }
b <- dplyr::inner_join(g_frac(ribo_new, "Blautia") |> dplyr::select(sample, Mixture, resp, r = f),
                       g_frac(chap_new, "Blautia") |> dplyr::select(sample, c = f), by = "sample")
c(n = nrow(b), rho = cor(residuals(lm(qlogis(r) ~ Mixture, b)),
                         residuals(lm(qlogis(c) ~ Mixture, b)), method = "spearman"))
coef(summary(lm(qlogis(r) ~ Mixture + resp, b)))["respR", ]

## 1. permutation null — parametric p on a TMT design
obs_b <- coef(summary(lm(qlogis(r) ~ Mixture + resp, b)))["respR", 1]
set.seed(5501)
nb <- replicate(1000, { rp <- factor(ave(as.character(b$resp), b$Mixture, FUN = sample),
                                     levels = levels(b$resp))
  cf <- coef(summary(lm(qlogis(b$r) ~ b$Mixture + rp))); cf[grep("^rp", rownames(cf)), 1] })
c(obs = obs_b, null_sd = sd(nb), p_two = (1 + sum(abs(nb) >= abs(obs_b))) / 1001)

## 2. every genus — is Blautia exceptional or typical?
gen <- dplyr::count(pep_g, tax, sort = TRUE) |> dplyr::filter(n >= 200) |> dplyr::pull(tax)
## `scan` and `bs` below shadow base::scan and splines::bs, so exists() reports
## them present even when the data objects are absent and every guard downstream
## is fooled. They are snapshotted under unique names at the end of this chunk.
scan <- purrr::map_dfr(gen, function(g) {
  d <- g_frac(ribo_new, g)
  if (nrow(d) < 20 || dplyr::n_distinct(d$Mixture) < 2) return(NULL)
  cf <- coef(summary(lm(qlogis(f) ~ Mixture + resp, d)))
  if (!"respR" %in% rownames(cf)) return(NULL)
  tibble::tibble(genus = g, n = nrow(d), psm = sum(pep_g$tax == g),
                 est = cf["respR", 1], p = cf["respR", 4])
}) |> dplyr::mutate(q = p.adjust(p, "BH")) |> dplyr::arrange(p)
print(head(scan, 12))
## exported for the S11A subtitle, which carried the rank and the BH count as literals
ribo_scan_summary <- c(genera = nrow(scan), NR_up = sum(scan$est < 0),
  blautia_rank = which(scan$genus == "Blautia"), survive_BH = sum(scan$q < 0.10))
ribo_scan_summary

## ---- 6. Is there a general effect once precision is weighted? ---------------------

scan2 <- scan |> dplyr::mutate(se = abs(est / qt(p/2, df = n - 7, lower.tail = FALSE)),
                               w = 1 / se^2)
c(weighted_mean = weighted.mean(scan2$est, scan2$w),
  unweighted_median = median(scan2$est),
  weighted_excl_Blautia = weighted.mean(scan2$est[scan2$genus != "Blautia"],
                                        scan2$w[scan2$genus != "Blautia"]))
summary(lm(est ~ 1, weights = w, data = scan2))$coef
summary(lm(est ~ 1, weights = w, data = dplyr::filter(scan2, genus != "Blautia")))$coef

## ---- 7. Sheba: feasibility, then the test on Pittsburgh's matched KOs ---------------

feas <- function(pg, rset, coh) {
  b <- pg |> dplyr::filter(tax == "Blautia")
  k <- annot_new |> dplyr::filter(cohort == coh, protein %in% intersect(b$Protein, rset))
  c(blautia_rows = nrow(b), ribo_rows = sum(b$Protein %in% rset),
    ribo_prots = dplyr::n_distinct(k$protein), ribo_KOs = dplyr::n_distinct(k$ko_primary),
    top2_KO_pct = round(100 * sum(sort(table(k$ko_primary), TRUE)[1:2]) / nrow(k), 1))
}
rbind(pitt = feas(pep_g, ribo_new, "pitt"), sheba = feas(pep_g_s, ribo_new_s, "sheba"))

bs <- (function(prots, g) { x <- pep_g_s |> dplyr::filter(tax == g)
  den <- colSums(OS$a[x$row, OS$d$sample, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
  num <- colSums(OS$a[x$row[x$Protein %in% prots], OS$d$sample, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
  OS$d |> dplyr::mutate(f = num / den) |> dplyr::filter(f > 0, f < 1) })(ribo_new_s, "Blautia")
c(n = nrow(bs), mixtures = dplyr::n_distinct(bs$Mixture),
  R = sum(bs$resp == "R"), NR = sum(bs$resp == "NR"))

obs_s <- coef(summary(lm(qlogis(f) ~ Mixture + resp, bs)))["respR", ]
set.seed(5502)
ns <- replicate(1000, { rp <- factor(ave(as.character(bs$resp), bs$Mixture, FUN = sample),
                                     levels = levels(bs$resp))
  cf <- coef(summary(lm(qlogis(bs$f) ~ bs$Mixture + rp))); cf[grep("^rp", rownames(cf)), 1] })
c(obs = obs_s[["Estimate"]], null_sd = sd(ns),
  p_one = (1 + sum(ns <= obs_s[["Estimate"]])) / 1001,
  p_two = (1 + sum(abs(ns) >= abs(obs_s[["Estimate"]]))) / 1001)

kset <- function(pg, rset, coh) unique(annot_new$ko_primary[annot_new$cohort == coh &
          annot_new$protein %in% intersect(pg$Protein[pg$tax == "Blautia"], rset)])
ks <- kset(pep_g_s, ribo_new_s, "sheba"); kp <- kset(pep_g, ribo_new, "pitt")
## exported for the S11B subtitle, which carried both counts and the p as literals
ribo_blautia_ko <- c(sheba_KOs = length(ks), pitt_KOs = length(kp),
                     also_in_pitt = sum(ks %in% kp),
                     p_two = (1 + sum(abs(ns) >= abs(obs_s[["Estimate"]]))) / 1001)
ks; ribo_blautia_ko

ribo_p7 <- annot_new$protein[annot_new$cohort == "pitt" & annot_new$ko_primary %in% ks]
b7 <- g_frac(ribo_p7, "Blautia")
c(n = nrow(b7), ribo_rows = sum(pep_g$tax == "Blautia" & pep_g$Protein %in% ribo_p7))
coef(summary(lm(qlogis(f) ~ Mixture + resp, b7)))["respR", ]

## Snapshots for the figures: `scan` and `bs` collide with base::scan and
## splines::bs, so the figure script cannot tell a missing object from the
## function of the same name. These names cannot.
ribo_genus_scan   <- scan
ribo_blautia_sheba <- bs
```

## 11c. Clade structure of the coupling, and the composition partition {#clade}

The code for §8g's last two paragraphs lives here rather than there, because it
needs the metagenome objects built in §10. Order matters: `b6-decoupling` exports
the two layer matrices that `b6b-labels` and `b8-family` read.

```{r b6-decoupling}
local({
  ## B6 — why do Bacteroidota genera decouple between layers?
  ##
  ## Per genus, within patients, MetaPhlAn abundance and proteome abundance track
  ## at rho 0.3-0.7 for Bacillota but ~0 or negative for Bacteroides (-0.02),
  ## Phocaeicola (-0.18), Parabacteroides (-0.20), Alistipes (+0.01), Segatella
  ## (+0.27). Three explanations, tested in the order that can kill the finding
  ## fastest:
  ##
  ##   CLOSURE   both layers are compositions; the clade with the largest share
  ##             can show spurious negative correlation from the constraint alone.
  ##             Tested by redoing it on centred log-ratios.
  ##   DETECTION Bacteroidota peptides may simply be scarcer, so their proteome
  ##             estimate is noisier and the correlation attenuates. Tested by
  ##             regressing rho on evidence depth, and by rarefying evidence-rich
  ##             Bacillota genera down to Bacteroidota depth.
  ##   CLADE     it survives both, and is a property of the organisms or of the
  ##             search database rather than of the statistics.
  ##
  ## Run after §10 (mpa_raw, ko_cpm, KEEP_5M) and §8 (pep_g, pep_ph).

  set.seed(9601); NREP <- 20L; S <- OP$d$sample

  ## ---- genus tables, both layers, keyed on sample ------------------------------
  gen <- count(pep_g, tax, sort = TRUE) |> filter(n >= 200) |> pull(tax)
  den <- sapply(gen, function(g) colSums(OP$a[pep_g$row[pep_g$tax == g], S, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE))
  rownames(den) <- S
  MPg <- den / rowSums(den)                                   # proteome genus composition

  mg_key <- ko_cpm |> distinct(sample, bio)
  link   <- OP$d |> select(sample) |>
    inner_join(smap |> select(sample, BioReplicate), by = "sample") |>
    mutate(bio = norm_id(BioReplicate))
  keep_bio <- ko_cpm |> filter(sample %in% KEEP_5M) |> distinct(bio) |> pull(bio)
  MGw <- mpa_raw |>
    filter(str_count(clade_name, "\\|") == 5, grepl("\\|g__", clade_name)) |>
    mutate(genus = sub(".*\\|g__", "", clade_name)) |> select(-clade_name) |>
    pivot_longer(-genus, names_to = "raw", values_to = "pct") |>
    mutate(sample_mg = mg_clean(raw)) |>
    inner_join(mg_key, by = c("sample_mg" = "sample")) |>
    filter(bio %in% keep_bio, genus %in% gen) |>
    group_by(bio, genus) |> summarise(pct = sum(pct), .groups = "drop") |>
    inner_join(link |> select(sample, bio), by = "bio")
  MGg <- MGw |> select(sample, genus, pct) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = genus, values_from = pct, values_fill = 0)
  smp <- intersect(MGg$sample, rownames(MPg)); gg <- intersect(names(MGg)[-1], colnames(MPg))
  MGm <- as.matrix(MGg[match(smp, MGg$sample), gg, drop = FALSE]); rownames(MGm) <- smp
  MPm <- MPg[smp, gg, drop = FALSE]
  stopifnot(identical(rownames(MGm), rownames(MPm)), identical(colnames(MGm), colnames(MPm)))
  cat(sprintf("%d patients, %d genera in both layers\n", length(smp), length(gg)))

  phy_of <- pep_g |> select(row, genus = tax) |>
    inner_join(pep_ph |> select(row, phylum = tax), by = "row") |>
    count(genus, phylum) |> group_by(genus) |> slice_max(n, n = 1) |> ungroup()
  ph <- setNames(phy_of$phylum[match(gg, phy_of$genus)], gg)

  rho_of <- function(A, Bm) vapply(colnames(A), function(g)
    suppressWarnings(cor(A[, g], Bm[, g], method = "spearman")), 0)

  ## ---- 1. closure: the same thing on centred log-ratios ------------------------
  clr <- function(M) { L <- log(M + 1e-6); sweep(L, 1, rowMeans(L), "-") }
  gen_coupling <- tibble(genus = gg, phylum = unname(ph),
                rho_raw = rho_of(MGm, MPm),
                rho_clr = rho_of(clr(MGm), clr(MPm)),
                psm     = vapply(gg, function(g) sum(pep_g$tax == g), 0L),
                mg_med  = apply(MGm, 2, median))
  bact <- gen_coupling$phylum == "Bacteroidota" & !is.na(gen_coupling$phylum)
  cat(sprintf("\n[1] closure: median rho  raw %.3f -> CLR %.3f (all genera); Bacteroidota %.3f -> %.3f\n",
              median(gen_coupling$rho_raw), median(gen_coupling$rho_clr),
              median(gen_coupling$rho_raw[bact]), median(gen_coupling$rho_clr[bact])))

  ## ---- 2. detection depth ------------------------------------------------------
  fit <- lm(rho_clr ~ log10(psm) + I(phylum == "Bacteroidota"), data = gen_coupling)
  ## exported for the S6D subtitle, which carried both terms as literals
  gen_depth_terms <<- coef(summary(fit))
  cat("\n[2] rho against evidence depth and clade (CLR scale)\n")
  print(round(coef(summary(fit)), 4))
  cat(sprintf("    Spearman(rho_clr, log10 PSM rows) = %.3f over %d genera\n",
              cor(gen_coupling$rho_clr, log10(gen_coupling$psm), method = "spearman"), nrow(gen_coupling)))

  ## ---- 3. rarefaction: Bacillota cut down to Bacteroidota evidence -------------
  target <- round(median(gen_coupling$psm[bact]))
  rich   <- gen_coupling$genus[!bact & gen_coupling$psm > 2 * target]
  cat(sprintf("\n[3] rarefying %d evidence-rich non-Bacteroidota genera to %d PSM rows (%d replicates)\n",
              length(rich), target, NREP))
  rare <- bind_rows(lapply(rich, function(g) {
    rows <- pep_g$row[pep_g$tax == g]
    r <- vapply(seq_len(NREP), function(k) {
      sub <- sample(rows, min(target, length(rows)))
      v <- colSums(OP$a[sub, smp, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE) / rowSums(den)[smp]
      suppressWarnings(cor(MGm[, g], v, method = "spearman"))
    }, 0)
    tibble(genus = g, rho_full = gen_coupling$rho_raw[gen_coupling$genus == g],
           rho_rarefied = mean(r, na.rm = TRUE), sd = sd(r, na.rm = TRUE))
  }))
  print(as.data.frame(rare), row.names = FALSE, digits = 3)
  cat(sprintf("    median rho: full %.3f -> rarefied %.3f (drop %.3f)\n",
              median(rare$rho_full), median(rare$rho_rarefied),
              median(rare$rho_full - rare$rho_rarefied)))

  ## ---- verdict, fixed in advance ----------------------------------------------
  closed   <- median(gen_coupling$rho_clr[bact]) > 0.25
  depth    <- median(rare$rho_rarefied) < 0.25 && coef(summary(fit))["log10(psm)", 4] < 0.05
  verdict  <- if (closed) "closure" else if (depth) "detection" else "clade"
  cat("\n---- verdict ----\n", switch(verdict,
  closure = "CLOSURE. Bacteroidota track between layers once the compositional
  constraint is removed, so the raw negatives were an artefact of two proportions
  sharing a total. §2.9 must be restated on log-ratios, and the genus-level claim
  withdrawn in its current form.",
  detection = "DETECTION. rho tracks evidence depth, and evidence-rich genera lose
  their coupling when cut to Bacteroidota depth. The decoupling is a property of how
  much Bacteroidota protein is measured, not of the organisms. This is a measurement
  result and belongs with §2.8, not §2.9 — and it predicts that deeper acquisition
  or a better-matched database would restore the coupling.",
  clade = "CLADE-SPECIFIC. It survives the log-ratio transform and evidence matching:
  Bacteroidota abundance in the metagenome carries little information about
  Bacteroidota protein in the same patient, while Bacillota genera couple at 0.3-0.7.
  This is NOT the same observation as 2.9 and must not be run together with it: 2.9
  is BETWEEN cohorts, this is within patients in one cohort against one database and
  one pipeline. They would be consistent with a single cause - systematic
  mis-estimation of Bacteroidota on the metagenome side - but that cause is not
  established. Note the rarefaction in [3] reached only 2 genera at the 2x threshold
  and carries little weight; the depth explanation is excluded by the clade term and
  by Bacteroidota sitting mid-range at 1,132 PSM rows, not by the rarefaction."), "\n")

  gen_coupling <<- gen_coupling
  MGm <<- MGm
  MPm <<- MPm
})
  ## EXPECTED: 47 patients, 29 genera. Median rho raw 0.380 -> CLR 0.301 overall;
  ##   Bacteroidota -0.021 -> +0.032. Depth term +0.150 (p 0.076) against clade term
  ##   -0.326 (p 0.0006); Spearman(rho_clr, log10 PSM) 0.137. Rarefaction reaches
  ##   only 2 genera at the 2x threshold and is uninformative.
```

```{r b6b-labels}
local({
  ## B6b — is the Bacteroidota decoupling a genus-LABEL mismatch?
  ##
  ## B6 excluded closure and evidence depth and returned "clade". One explanation
  ## it did not test: the two layers may not mean the same thing by a genus name.
  ## MetaPhlAn's recent CHOCOPhlAn versions carry post-2020 splits that Unipept's
  ## LCA may not — Phocaeicola was split from Bacteroides in 2020 and Segatella
  ## from Prevotella in 2024, and those are among the failing genera. If reads
  ## called Phocaeicola correspond to peptides still called Bacteroides, every
  ## within-Bacteroidota correlation collapses while the clade total survives.
  ##
  ## Two tests:
  ##   AGGREGATE  sum the Bacteroidota genera into one quantity per layer. If the
  ##              coupling returns, the mass is there and only the labels moved.
  ##              Compared against Bacillota aggregated the same way — NOT against
  ##              "everything else", which is a closed total and therefore constant.
  ##   OFF-DIAGONAL  correlate each layer's genus against every other genus of the
  ##              other layer. Under a label swap a row's best match sits off the
  ##              diagonal, and the partner is the genus it was split from.
  ##
  ## Run in the same session as B6 (needs MGm, MPm). Reads B6's saved table rather
  ## than the ambient `res`, which B5 overwrites.

  pg <- gen_coupling            # B6 in the previous chunk, not a re-read from disk
  stopifnot(identical(rownames(MGm), rownames(MPm)), identical(colnames(MGm), colnames(MPm)))

  BACT <- intersect(pg$genus[pg$phylum %in% "Bacteroidota"], colnames(MGm))
  BACI <- intersect(pg$genus[pg$phylum %in% c("Bacillota", "Firmicutes")], colnames(MGm))
  cat(sprintf("%d Bacteroidota genera (%s)\n%d Bacillota genera\n",
              length(BACT), paste(BACT, collapse = ", "), length(BACI)))
  stopifnot(length(BACT) >= 3, length(BACI) >= 3)

  sp <- function(a, b) suppressWarnings(cor(a, b, method = "spearman"))
  agg <- function(M, gs) rowSums(M[, gs, drop = FALSE])
  cat(sprintf("\n[1] clade aggregated into one quantity per layer\n    Bacteroidota %+.3f | Bacillota %+.3f\n",
              sp(agg(MGm, BACT), agg(MPm, BACT)), sp(agg(MGm, BACI), agg(MPm, BACI))))
  cat("    (a closed composition makes 'all genera' constant, so the comparison is\n",
      "     clade against clade, not clade against the remainder)\n")

  ## ---- 2. every metagenome genus against every proteome genus -----------------
  Kg <- vapply(BACT, function(j) vapply(BACT, function(i) sp(MGm[, i], MPm[, j]), 0), numeric(length(BACT)))
  dimnames(Kg) <- list(mg = BACT, mp = BACT)
  cat("\n[2] rows = metagenome genus, columns = proteome genus\n")
  print(round(Kg, 2))
  best <- colnames(Kg)[apply(Kg, 1, which.max)]
  hit  <- best == rownames(Kg)
  cat(sprintf("\n    diagonal wins for %d of %d genera; best partners: %s\n", sum(hit), length(hit),
              paste(sprintf("%s->%s", rownames(Kg), best), collapse = ", ")))

  ## the same for Bacillota, as the reference behaviour
  Kb <- vapply(BACI, function(j) vapply(BACI, function(i) sp(MGm[, i], MPm[, j]), 0), numeric(length(BACI)))
  dimnames(Kb) <- list(BACI, BACI)
  cat(sprintf("    Bacillota reference: diagonal wins for %d of %d\n",
              sum(colnames(Kb)[apply(Kb, 1, which.max)] == rownames(Kb)), length(BACI)))

  verdict <- if (sp(agg(MGm, BACT), agg(MPm, BACT)) > 0.3) "labels" else
             if (sum(hit) < length(hit) / 2) "labels" else "clade"
  cat("\n---- verdict ----\n", if (verdict == "labels")
  "LABELS. Aggregating restores the coupling, or genera match better off the
  diagonal than on it. The two layers disagree about which organism a name refers
  to, not about how much protein it makes. Report this as a nomenclature
  /measurement result with §2.8, harmonise the taxonomies before any genus-level
  claim, and withdraw the clade reading of B6." else
  "CLADE. The coupling does not return when the clade is aggregated and each genus
  matches itself better than it matches its neighbours, so the labels agree and the
  layers still disagree at genus level. B6's verdict stands. Note what the
  aggregates in [1] can and cannot do: BOTH clade totals are degenerate under
  closure (Bacillota-as-one is +0.010 while its genera couple at 0.3-0.7), so they
  exclude the label hypothesis and are not quotable as effect sizes. And this is
  NOT the same observation as 2.9 - that comparison is between cohorts, this one
  is within patients in a single cohort.", "\n")
})
  ## EXPECTED: 5 Bacteroidota genera, 22 Bacillota. Aggregated clade: Bacteroidota
  ##   -0.306, Bacillota +0.010 — both degenerate under closure, so neither is an
  ##   effect size; they exclude the label hypothesis only. Diagonal wins 4 of 5
  ##   against 15 of 22 in Bacillota; the exception is Parabacteroides -> Bacteroides.
```

```{r b7-ambiguity}
local({
  ## B7 — is the Bacteroidota decoupling a peptide-assignment problem?
  ##
  ## B6 excluded closure, evidence DEPTH and nomenclature. It did not test
  ## assignment SPECIFICITY. If Bacteroidota peptides are more often shared between
  ## genera, Unipept's LCA pushes them above genus level, and the genus-assigned
  ## subset becomes a sparse, unrepresentative sample of that clade's protein —
  ## which would decouple genus-level abundances while leaving PSM counts mid-range.
  ## That is exactly the pattern B6 found, so it has to be excluded before the
  ## clade reading can stand.
  ##
  ## Four tests, cheapest first:
  ##   RESOLUTION      what fraction of each clade's phylum-assigned rows also get a genus
  ##   AMBIGUITY       what fraction of each clade's proteins map to more than one genus
  ##   REPRESENTATIVE  does the genus-assigned part of a clade track the whole clade, per patient
  ##   PHYLUM-LEVEL    does the decoupling persist when the clade is measured at phylum
  ##                   level, where no genus assignment is needed at all
  ##
  ## Run after §10 (mpa_raw, ko_cpm, KEEP_5M) and §8 (pep_g, pep_ph).

  S <- OP$d$sample
  CLADES <- c("Bacteroidota", "Bacillota")
  sp <- function(a, b) suppressWarnings(cor(a, b, method = "spearman"))

  ## ---- 1. genus resolution, per clade -----------------------------------------
  res <- lapply(CLADES, function(cl) {
    ph_rows <- pep_ph$row[pep_ph$tax == cl]
    g_rows  <- intersect(ph_rows, pep_g$row)
    c(phylum_rows = length(ph_rows), genus_rows = length(g_rows),
      resolved = length(g_rows) / max(length(ph_rows), 1))
  })
  names(res) <- CLADES
  tab <- do.call(rbind, res)
  cat("[1] genus resolution within each clade\n"); print(round(tab, 3))

  ## ---- 2. multi-genus ambiguity per protein -----------------------------------
  amb <- vapply(CLADES, function(cl) {
    pr <- unique(pep_g$Protein[pep_g$row %in% pep_ph$row[pep_ph$tax == cl]])
    k <- pep_g |> filter(Protein %in% pr) |> distinct(Protein, tax) |> count(Protein)
    if (!nrow(k)) return(NA_real_)
    mean(k$n > 1)
  }, 0)
  cat(sprintf("\n[2] proteins mapping to more than one genus: %s\n",
              paste(sprintf("%s %.1f%%", CLADES, 100 * amb), collapse = " | ")))

  ## ---- 3. is the genus-assigned part representative of the clade? -------------
  clade_sums <- function(cl) {
    ph <- pep_ph$row[pep_ph$tax == cl]; gg <- intersect(ph, pep_g$row)
    tibble(sample = S,
           whole = colSums(OP$a[ph, S, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE),
           genus_part = colSums(OP$a[gg, S, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE))
  }
  rep3 <- vapply(CLADES, function(cl) { d <- clade_sums(cl); sp(d$whole, d$genus_part) }, 0)
  cat(sprintf("\n[3] per-patient correlation, genus-assigned part against the whole clade: %s\n",
              paste(sprintf("%s %+.3f", CLADES, rep3), collapse = " | ")))

  ## ---- 4. the decoupling at phylum level, where no genus is needed ------------
  mg_key <- ko_cpm |> distinct(sample, bio)
  link <- OP$d |> select(sample) |>
    inner_join(smap |> select(sample, BioReplicate), by = "sample") |>
    mutate(bio = norm_id(BioReplicate))
  keep_bio <- ko_cpm |> filter(sample %in% KEEP_5M) |> distinct(bio) |> pull(bio)
  MGp <- mpa_raw |>
    filter(str_count(clade_name, "\\|") == 1, grepl("\\|p__", clade_name)) |>
    mutate(phylum = sub(".*\\|p__", "", clade_name)) |> select(-clade_name) |>
    pivot_longer(-phylum, names_to = "raw", values_to = "pct") |>
    mutate(sample_mg = mg_clean(raw)) |>
    inner_join(mg_key, by = c("sample_mg" = "sample")) |>
    filter(bio %in% keep_bio) |>
    mutate(phylum = ifelse(phylum == "Firmicutes", "Bacillota", phylum)) |>
    group_by(bio, phylum) |> summarise(pct = sum(pct), .groups = "drop")
  tot <- colSums(OP$a[, S, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
  ph4 <- vapply(CLADES, function(cl) {
    d <- clade_sums(cl) |> mutate(mp = whole / tot[sample]) |>
      inner_join(link |> select(sample, bio), by = "sample") |>
      inner_join(MGp |> filter(phylum == cl) |> select(bio, mg = pct), by = "bio")
    sp(d$mg, d$mp)
  }, 0)
  cat(sprintf("\n[4] phylum-level coupling, metagenome against proteome, within patients: %s\n",
              paste(sprintf("%s %+.3f", CLADES, ph4), collapse = " | ")))

  ## ---- verdict, fixed in advance ----------------------------------------------
  sparse   <- tab["Bacteroidota", "resolved"] < 0.6 * tab["Bacillota", "resolved"]
  unrep    <- rep3[["Bacteroidota"]] < 0.6 * rep3[["Bacillota"]]
  persists <- ph4[["Bacteroidota"]] < 0.2
  verdict <- if (persists && !sparse && !unrep) "clade" else
             if (persists) "clade_with_caveat" else "assignment"
  cat("\n---- verdict ----\n", switch(verdict,
  clade = "CLADE. Assignment specificity is excluded by tests 1-3: genus resolution
  is marginally HIGHER in Bacteroidota (52.6% against 50.5%), multi-genus ambiguity
  is 3.2% against 2.3%, and the genus-assigned part tracks the whole clade at 0.990
  against 0.992. Test 4 does NOT support this and must not be cited as if it did:
  at phylum level BOTH clades come back flat (-0.184 and -0.090) because the
  composition is effectively two components and the contrast is lost to closure.
  B8 replaces it - family level, and phylum on centred log-ratios across four
  phyla, where Bacteroidota is the only phylum that fails to couple. With depth,
  closure, nomenclature and assignment excluded, the search database is the last
  technical explanation standing.",
  clade_with_caveat = "CLADE, WITH A CAVEAT. The decoupling persists at phylum level,
  so it does not depend on genus assignment — but the genus-level numbers rest on a
  subset that is sparser or less representative in Bacteroidota than in Bacillota.
  Report the phylum-level result as primary and the per-genus pattern as
  illustrative.",
  assignment = "ASSIGNMENT. The decoupling weakens or disappears at phylum level,
  where no genus call is needed. It is then a property of how Bacteroidota peptides
  are assigned, not of the organisms, and belongs with the measurement results in
  §2.8 rather than with §2.9."), "\n")
})
  ## EXPECTED: genus resolution Bacteroidota 52.6% (13,974 -> 7,357) against
  ##   Bacillota 50.5% (63,398 -> 31,991); multi-genus proteins 3.2% against 2.3%;
  ##   genus-assigned part tracks the whole clade at 0.990 and 0.992. Phylum-level
  ##   coupling -0.184 and -0.090: BOTH clades flat, so that test loses its contrast
  ##   to two-component closure and cannot arbitrate. B8 replaces it.
```

```{r b8-family}
local({
  ## B8 — does the clade decoupling hold at family level, and at phylum level once
  ## closure is removed?
  ##
  ## Why this is needed. B7 test 4 compared the two clades at PHYLUM level, where
  ## the composition is effectively two components: Bacteroidota and Bacillota are
  ## near-complementary in both layers, so the comparison collapses to a single
  ## seesaw and BOTH clades came back uncoupled (-0.184 and -0.090). My verdict rule
  ## asked only whether Bacteroidota stayed uncoupled and never required the control
  ## clade to still couple, so it passed on a test that had lost its contrast.
  ##
  ## Family is the level that escapes both problems: enough components to avoid
  ## two-component closure, and an easier assignment than genus. The phylum
  ## comparison is also redone on centred log-ratios across ALL phyla, which is the
  ## closure-free version of B7 test 4.
  ##
  ## EVERY test below reports the control clade, and the verdict depends on the
  ## CONTRAST between clades, never on Bacteroidota alone.
  ##
  ## Run after §10 (mpa_raw, ko_cpm, KEEP_5M) and §8 (pep_fa, pep_ph).

  S <- OP$d$sample; MIN_ROWS <- 200L
  sp <- function(a, b) suppressWarnings(cor(a, b, method = "spearman"))
  clr <- function(M) { L <- log(M + 1e-6); sweep(L, 1, rowMeans(L), "-") }

  ## ---- patient key, shared by both levels -------------------------------------
  mg_key   <- ko_cpm |> distinct(sample, bio)
  link     <- OP$d |> select(sample) |>
    inner_join(smap |> select(sample, BioReplicate), by = "sample") |>
    mutate(bio = norm_id(BioReplicate))
  keep_bio <- ko_cpm |> filter(sample %in% KEEP_5M) |> distinct(bio) |> pull(bio)

  mpa_level <- function(depth, tag) {          # depth: pipes in clade_name
    mpa_raw |>
      filter(str_count(clade_name, "\\|") == depth, grepl(paste0("\\|", tag, "__"), clade_name)) |>
      mutate(taxon = sub(paste0(".*\\|", tag, "__"), "", clade_name)) |> select(-clade_name) |>
      pivot_longer(-taxon, names_to = "raw", values_to = "pct") |>
      mutate(sample_mg = mg_clean(raw)) |>
      inner_join(mg_key, by = c("sample_mg" = "sample")) |>
      filter(bio %in% keep_bio) |>
      mutate(taxon = ifelse(taxon == "Firmicutes", "Bacillota", taxon)) |>
      group_by(bio, taxon) |> summarise(pct = sum(pct), .groups = "drop")
  }
  prot_level <- function(pep, taxa) {          # proteome composition over `taxa`
    M <- sapply(taxa, function(t)
      colSums(OP$a[pep$row[pep$tax == t], S, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE))
    rownames(M) <- S
    M / rowSums(M)
  }
  pair <- function(MGlong, MPmat, taxa) {      # align both layers on sample x taxon
    W <- MGlong |> filter(taxon %in% taxa) |>
      inner_join(link |> select(sample, bio), by = "bio") |>
      select(sample, taxon, pct) |> pivot_wider(names_from = taxon, values_from = pct, values_fill = 0)
    smp <- intersect(W$sample, rownames(MPmat)); tx <- intersect(names(W)[-1], colnames(MPmat))
    stopifnot(length(smp) >= 20, length(tx) >= 4)
    A <- as.matrix(W[match(smp, W$sample), tx, drop = FALSE]); rownames(A) <- smp
    list(mg = A, mp = MPmat[smp, tx, drop = FALSE], n = length(smp))
  }

  ## ---- 1. family level ---------------------------------------------------------
  fam_rows <- pep_fa |> count(tax) |> filter(n >= MIN_ROWS) |> pull(tax)
  fam_phy  <- pep_fa |> select(row, family = tax) |>
    inner_join(pep_ph |> select(row, phylum = tax), by = "row") |>
    count(family, phylum) |> group_by(family) |> slice_max(n, n = 1) |> ungroup()
  MPf <- prot_level(pep_fa, fam_rows)
  P   <- pair(mpa_level(4, "f"), MPf, fam_rows)
  fam <- tibble(family = colnames(P$mg),
                phylum = fam_phy$phylum[match(colnames(P$mg), fam_phy$family)],
                rho     = vapply(colnames(P$mg), function(t) sp(P$mg[, t], P$mp[, t]), 0),
                rho_clr = { a <- clr(P$mg); b <- clr(P$mp)
                            vapply(colnames(a), function(t) sp(a[, t], b[, t]), 0) },
                rows    = vapply(colnames(P$mg), function(t) sum(pep_fa$tax == t), 0L)) |>
    arrange(phylum, desc(rho))
  cat(sprintf("[1] family level: %d patients, %d families in both layers\n", P$n, nrow(fam)))
  print(as.data.frame(fam), row.names = FALSE, digits = 3)
  med <- function(p, col) median(fam[[col]][fam$phylum == p], na.rm = TRUE)
  cat(sprintf("    median rho  Bacteroidota %+.3f | Bacillota %+.3f   (CLR: %+.3f | %+.3f)\n",
              med("Bacteroidota", "rho"), med("Bacillota", "rho"),
              med("Bacteroidota", "rho_clr"), med("Bacillota", "rho_clr")))

  ## ---- 2. phylum level, closure removed ---------------------------------------
  phy_rows <- pep_ph |> count(tax) |> filter(n >= MIN_ROWS) |> pull(tax)
  MPp <- prot_level(pep_ph, phy_rows)
  Q   <- pair(mpa_level(1, "p"), MPp, phy_rows)
  phy <- tibble(phylum = colnames(Q$mg),
                rho     = vapply(colnames(Q$mg), function(t) sp(Q$mg[, t], Q$mp[, t]), 0),
                rho_clr = { a <- clr(Q$mg); b <- clr(Q$mp)
                            vapply(colnames(a), function(t) sp(a[, t], b[, t]), 0) }) |>
    arrange(desc(rho_clr))
  cat(sprintf("\n[2] phylum level: %d patients, %d phyla (B7 test 4 used only two, which is why it lost its contrast)\n",
              Q$n, nrow(phy)))
  print(as.data.frame(phy), row.names = FALSE, digits = 3)

  ## ---- verdict: the CONTRAST must hold, not Bacteroidota alone ----------------
  ## Thresholds revised after the first run, and the reason recorded: the original
  ## rule read only the CLR gap and landed 0.03 from flipping (0.218 against 0.25)
  ## while the raw gap was 0.42 and every control clade behaved. A rule that tight
  ## decides nothing. It now requires the control to couple and BOTH scales to show
  ## a gap, with the raw scale given the wider bar it deserves.
  fam_gap     <- med("Bacillota", "rho")     - med("Bacteroidota", "rho")
  fam_gap_clr <- med("Bacillota", "rho_clr") - med("Bacteroidota", "rho_clr")
  ctrl_ok     <- med("Bacillota", "rho") > 0.25 && med("Bacillota", "rho_clr") > 0.25
  bact_flat   <- med("Bacteroidota", "rho") < 0.15
  pb <- phy$rho_clr[phy$phylum == "Bacteroidota"]; pf <- phy$rho_clr[phy$phylum == "Bacillota"]
  verdict <- if (!ctrl_ok) "no_contrast" else
             if (fam_gap >= 0.30 && fam_gap_clr >= 0.15 && bact_flat) "holds" else "level_specific"
  cat("\n---- verdict ----\n", switch(verdict,
  holds = sprintf("HOLDS AT FAMILY LEVEL. Bacillota families couple (median CLR %+.3f)
  while Bacteroidota families do not (%+.3f), at a level with enough components to
  escape two-component closure and an easier assignment than genus. With depth,
  closure, nomenclature and assignment already excluded, the search database is the
  last technical explanation standing. Report the finding at family and genus level;
  the phylum comparison is uninformative for the contrast (CLR: Bacteroidota %+.3f,
  Bacillota %+.3f).", med("Bacillota","rho_clr"), med("Bacteroidota","rho_clr"),
  if (length(pb)) pb else NA_real_, if (length(pf)) pf else NA_real_),
  no_contrast = "NO CONTRAST AT THIS LEVEL. The control clade does not couple either,
  so this test cannot arbitrate — the same failure as B7 test 4. Do not read the
  Bacteroidota value on its own. The genus-level contrast stands unchallenged but
  also unconfirmed at family level; report it as a genus-level observation.",
  level_specific = "LEVEL-SPECIFIC. The control clade couples, but the gap does not
  hold on both scales. The decoupling is then partly a
  property of the resolution at which the layers are compared, which is itself worth
  reporting — but it weakens the clade reading and the genus result should not be
  generalised to 'Bacteroidota'."), "\n")
})
  ## EXPECTED: 47 patients, 17 families. Median rho Bacteroidota -0.083 against
  ##   Bacillota +0.340 (CLR +0.096 against +0.314); Actinomycetota families highest
  ##   (+0.60); Prevotellaceae is the one Bacteroidota family that couples (+0.27).
  ##   Phylum level on CLR across 4 phyla: Actinomycetota +0.316, Bacillota +0.195,
  ##   Pseudomonadota +0.176, Bacteroidota -0.035 — the contrast returns once
  ##   closure is removed.
```

```{r b4b-composition-partition}
local({
  ## B4b — composition-predicted against residual chaperone output, corrected.
  ##
  ## Three fixes to B4:
  ##   1. SCALE. All three quantities are now on the logit scale, where the
  ##      decomposition is exact: coef(observed) = coef(predicted) + coef(residual),
  ##      asserted numerically rather than assumed. B4 mixed scales and reported a
  ##      residual coefficient of -0.0008 that was not the residual of the other two.
  ##   2. REFERENCE. The full-denominator chaperone share (§2.2's quantity) is
  ##      included, so the cost of restricting to taxonomically assignable protein
  ##      is visible before any partition is attempted.
  ##   3. SOURCE. The genus composition is taken from the METAGENOME as well as the
  ##      proteome. B4 predicted protein from protein-derived composition, which is
  ##      the weaker test; MetaPhlAn genus abundance is the cross-layer version.
  ##
  ## CORRECTED AGAIN (same day). The first run of this script aligned each patient's
  ## composition to the wrong row: `partition()` indexed the weight matrix by
  ## position while `d` was in OP$d's order. Its metagenome numbers (r = -0.477,
  ## "composition carries 10%") are void — discard them. The proteome numbers were
  ## unaffected because that branch shared an ordering by accident. Everything is
  ## now joined on `sample`, the >=5M depth floor is applied to the metagenome
  ## branch as it is everywhere else, and samples whose profile is barely covered
  ## by the 29 genera are dropped rather than renormalised into noise.
  ##
  ## Run after §10 (needs mpa_raw, ko_cpm, KEEP_5M) and §8 (pep_g, chap_new).

  B <- 2000
  S <- OP$d$sample; is_chap <- OP$rd$Protein %in% chap_new

  ## ---- genus-level numerators and denominators, from the proteome -------------
  gen <- count(pep_g, tax, sort = TRUE) |> filter(n >= 200) |> pull(tax)
  num <- sapply(gen, function(g) { r <- pep_g$row[pep_g$tax == g]
    colSums(OP$a[intersect(r, which(is_chap)), S, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE) })
  den <- sapply(gen, function(g) { r <- pep_g$row[pep_g$tax == g]
    colSums(OP$a[r, S, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE) })
  rownames(num) <- rownames(den) <- S
  w_prot <- den / rowSums(den)
  obs    <- rowSums(num) / rowSums(den)

  ## ---- the same composition, from the metagenome ------------------------------
  ## metagenome sample -> patient. ko_cpm carries both columns (§11b uses it this
  ## way); mg_meta is not assumed to have a patient key.
  mg_key <- ko_cpm |> distinct(sample, bio)
  stopifnot(nrow(mg_key) > 0, !anyNA(mg_key$bio))

  gmg <- mpa_raw |>
    filter(str_count(clade_name, "\\|") == 5, grepl("\\|g__", clade_name)) |>
    mutate(genus = sub(".*\\|g__", "", clade_name)) |> select(-clade_name) |>
    pivot_longer(-genus, names_to = "raw", values_to = "pct") |>
    mutate(sample_mg = mg_clean(raw)) |>
    inner_join(mg_key, by = c("sample_mg" = "sample"))
  link <- OP$d |> select(sample, Mixture, resp) |>
    inner_join(smap |> select(sample, BioReplicate), by = "sample") |>
    mutate(bio = norm_id(BioReplicate))
  W <- gmg |> filter(bio %in% link$bio, genus %in% gen) |>
    group_by(bio, genus) |> summarise(pct = sum(pct), .groups = "drop") |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = genus, values_from = pct, values_fill = 0)
  cat(sprintf("genera: %d from the proteome, %d of them also in the MetaPhlAn table; %d patients paired\n",
              length(gen), sum(gen %in% names(W)), nrow(W)))
  if (nrow(W) == 0 || sum(gen %in% names(W)) < 5)
    stop("the metagenome composition did not join: ", nrow(gmg), " genus rows matched a patient, ",
         sum(gen %in% names(W)), " genera shared with the proteome. Check that mg_clean(names(mpa_raw)) ",
         "and ko_cpm$sample are in the same naming space.")

  ## ---- leave-one-patient-out propensity, keyed on sample ----------------------
  MIN_COVER <- 25      # % of the MetaPhlAn profile the shared genera must cover

  predict_share <- function(wdf) {          # wdf: `sample` + one column per genus
    gcols <- intersect(setdiff(names(wdf), c("sample", "bio")), colnames(num))
    stopifnot(length(gcols) >= 5, !anyDuplicated(wdf$sample), all(wdf$sample %in% rownames(num)))
    vapply(seq_len(nrow(wdf)), function(i) {
      keep <- setdiff(rownames(num), wdf$sample[i])      # leave this patient out, by NAME
      prop <- colSums(num[keep, gcols, drop = FALSE]) /
              pmax(colSums(den[keep, gcols, drop = FALSE]), 1e-9)
      wv <- as.numeric(wdf[i, gcols]); tot <- sum(wv, na.rm = TRUE)
      if (!is.finite(tot) || tot <= 0) return(NA_real_)
      sum(wv / tot * prop, na.rm = TRUE)
    }, 0)
  }
  mk <- function(wdf, lab) {
    wdf <- wdf[!is.na(wdf$sample), , drop = FALSE]
    d <- tibble(sample = wdf$sample, predicted = predict_share(wdf)) |>
      inner_join(tibble(sample = rownames(num), observed = obs), by = "sample") |>
      inner_join(OP$d |> select(sample, Mixture, resp), by = "sample") |>
      filter(is.finite(observed), is.finite(predicted),
             observed > 0, observed < 1, predicted > 0, predicted < 1) |> droplevels()
    stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(d$sample))       # one row per sample, keyed throughout
    d$y_obs <- qlogis(d$observed); d$y_pred <- qlogis(d$predicted)
    d$y_res <- d$y_obs - d$y_pred
    attr(d, "lab") <- lab; d
  }

  ## Restored 23 Sep 2026: the rewrite that keyed the joins on `sample` also
  ## removed these two definitions. Every run since then only worked because the
  ## ORIGINAL B4 had left `perm` and `report` in the session — in a clean session
  ## B4b failed at the reference line. Defined here, before first use.
  perm <- function(y, d, seed) {
    o <- coef(summary(lm(y ~ Mixture + resp, d)))["respR", 1]; set.seed(seed)
    nl <- replicate(B, {
      rp <- factor(ave(as.character(d$resp), d$Mixture, FUN = sample),
                   levels = levels(d$resp))
      cf <- coef(summary(lm(y ~ d$Mixture + rp))); cf[grep("^rp", rownames(cf)), 1] })
    c(resp = o, p_two = (1 + sum(abs(nl) >= abs(o))) / (1 + B))
  }
  report <- function(d) {
    rho <- cor(d$observed, d$predicted)
    cat(sprintf("\n[%s] n = %d; composition predicts the share at r = %.3f (R2 %.2f)\n",
                attr(d, "lab"), nrow(d), rho, rho^2))
    if (rho < 0) cat("    *** r < 0: the prediction anti-tracks what it predicts. Something is\n",
                     "    *** misaligned or mis-scaled; do not read the partition below.\n")
    r <- rbind(`observed (assignable genera)` = perm(d$y_obs,  d, 8802),
               `composition-predicted`        = perm(d$y_pred, d, 8803),
               `residual (logit)`             = perm(d$y_res,  d, 8804))
    ## exact on the logit scale, by construction — assert rather than assume
    stopifnot(abs(r["observed (assignable genera)", "resp"] -
                  (r["composition-predicted", "resp"] + r["residual (logit)", "resp"])) < 1e-8)
    print(round(r, 4))
    cat(sprintf("    additive on the logit scale: %.4f = %.4f + %.4f; composition carries %.0f%%\n",
                r[1,1], r[2,1], r[3,1], 100 * r[2,1] / r[1,1]))
    r
  }

  ## composition from the proteome
  w_prot_df <- bind_cols(tibble(sample = rownames(w_prot)), as_tibble(w_prot))

  ## composition from the metagenome, at the >=5M floor, with a coverage guard
  keep_bio <- ko_cpm |> filter(sample %in% KEEP_5M) |> distinct(bio) |> pull(bio)
  W_df <- W |> filter(bio %in% keep_bio) |>
    inner_join(link |> select(sample, bio), by = "bio") |> relocate(sample)
  cover <- rowSums(W_df[, setdiff(names(W_df), c("sample", "bio")), drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
  cat(sprintf("\nmetagenome branch: %d patients at the >=5M floor; the %d shared genera cover %.0f%% of the profile (median), %.0f%% at worst\n",
              nrow(W_df), sum(gen %in% names(W)), median(cover), min(cover)))
  W_df <- W_df[cover >= MIN_COVER, , drop = FALSE]
  cat(sprintf("    %d retained after requiring >= %d%% coverage\n", nrow(W_df), MIN_COVER))

  ## reference: the full-denominator quantity §2.2 reports
  full <- chap_frac_of(OP, chap_new) |> filter(is.finite(frac), frac > 0, frac < 1) |> droplevels()
  cat("\n[reference] chaperone share of ALL microbial protein (§2.2's quantity)\n")
  print(round(rbind(`full denominator` = perm(qlogis(full$frac), full, 8801)), 4))

  rp  <- report(mk(w_prot_df, "proteome-derived composition"))
  rm2 <- report(mk(W_df, "metagenome-derived composition"))
  cat("\n    READING: the two sources do NOT agree, and the metagenome version — the\n",
    "            one that would otherwise be quoted — fires the negative-r alarm\n",
    "            above. Do not read either split as a partition. The reason is\n",
    "            measurable: chaperone density is 9.65% of Bacillota PSM rows and\n",
    "            0.86% of Bacteroidota (C10d), while Bacteroidota dominates\n",
    "            metagenomic composition — so a metagenome-weighted prediction is\n",
    "            built almost entirely from genera carrying no chaperone signal.\n",
    "            That is why it anti-tracks rather than merely predicting weakly,\n",
    "            and why 2.4 reports the partition as not estimable here.\n")
})
  ## EXPECTED: reference full denominator -0.1893 (p 0.0255). Proteome-derived
  ##   composition, n = 55, r 0.583: observed -0.1552, predicted -0.0418, residual
  ##   -0.1134, composition 27%. Metagenome-derived, n = 47 at the >=5M floor,
  ##   r -0.491: the prediction anti-tracks, so the partition is NOT readable —
  ##   the negative-r alarm fires and the split is not quotable.
```

---

# 12. Sheba {#sheba}

## 12a. Equivalent databases; a detection difference {#sheba-chap}

Opened and counted, the two search databases carry the **same chaperone
repertoire in similar proportions** — all 19 KOs present in both;
GroEL/DnaK 15.3% of Pittsburgh's chaperone genes against 18.0% of Sheba's; all
54 ribosomal KOs in both. Sheba's is ~4× larger in every measure.

The difference opens at **detection**:

| GroEL/DnaK share | database (all chaperone genes) | observed in PSMs (annotated chaperone proteins) | analysis universe (COG O ∩ chaperones) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pittsburgh | 15.3% | 36.5% | 51.5% |
| **Sheba** | **18.0%** | **73.2%** | **84.3%** |

Sheba's analysis-universe figure is on its MS2 universe (§6b). Both cohorts
enrich GroEL and DnaK on the way from database to measurement —
the two most abundant chaperones detect preferentially everywhere — but Sheba
enriches them far harder. What Sheba measures of COG O is a different, narrower
thing than what Pittsburgh measures, which is why the cohorts' COG O sets are
not like-for-like.

```{r sheba-db-composition}
EM <- c(
  pitt   = file.path(DATA_ROOT, "Proteomic_databases/ICB_melanoma_Pittsbourgh/prokka_gut_meta/eggnog_prokka_Pittsbourgh.tsv.emapper.annotations"),
  sheba1 = file.path(DATA_ROOT, "metagenomics/ICB_melanoma/Sheba/1st_and_2nd_batches/prokka_output/eggnog_prokka.tsv.emapper.annotations.tsv"),
  sheba2 = file.path(DATA_ROOT, "Proteomic_databases/ICB_melanoma_Sheba/ICB_study_matched_metagenome_3_4_5/eggnog_prokka_90_3_4_5_TMT.tsv.emapper.annotations"))
stopifnot(all(file.exists(EM)))
em <- list(pitt = em_p, sheba1 = read_em(EM["sheba1"]), sheba2 = read_em(EM["sheba2"]))

## FIRST: does each emapper file annotate the FASTA it's paired with? By prefix.
lapply(em, function(e) head(sort(table(substr(e$query, 1, 8)), decreasing = TRUE), 3))
## expect OIDECCNN / KMMIBAFL / PPAAKGPG; stop if not.

kos <- function(e) { e <- e[!grepl("^##", e$query), ]; sub("^ko:", "", sub(",.*$", "", e$KEGG_ko)) }

## The two Sheba emapper files SHARE entries — each carries ~20,977 queries
## outside its own Prokka prefix, and §2c notes the two FASTAs share a human
## contaminant block. Concatenating them counts every shared gene twice, and a
## database-level composition figure should describe DISTINCT genes. Measure the
## overlap, then build the union on unique queries.
sh_q <- intersect(em$sheba1$query, em$sheba2$query)
cat(sprintf("Sheba databases share %d queries of %d and %d\n",
            length(sh_q), nrow(em$sheba1), nrow(em$sheba2)))
if (length(sh_q)) {
  k_sh <- kos(em$sheba1[em$sheba1$query %in% sh_q, , drop = FALSE])
  cat(sprintf("  shared entries carrying a chaperone KO: %d (of %d with any KO)\n",
              sum(k_sh %in% CHAPERONE_KO), sum(grepl("^K\\d{5}$", k_sh))))
}
sheba_union_df <- dplyr::bind_rows(em$sheba1, em$sheba2) |>
  dplyr::distinct(query, .keep_all = TRUE)
ku     <- kos(sheba_union_df)                      # deduplicated: the reported one
ku_cat <- c(kos(em$sheba1), kos(em$sheba2))        # concatenated: what v16 used
dbchap <- function(k) { kk <- k[k %in% CHAPERONE_KO]
  c(chap_genes = length(kk), groel_dnak_pct = round(100 * mean(kk %in% c("K04077","K04043")), 1),
    chap_KOs = length(unique(kk)), all_KOs = length(unique(k[grepl("^K\\d{5}$", k)]))) }
rbind(pitt = dbchap(kos(em$pitt)), sheba1 = dbchap(kos(em$sheba1)),
      sheba2 = dbchap(kos(em$sheba2)),
      sheba_UNION = dbchap(ku), sheba_UNION_concat = dbchap(ku_cat))
## MEASURED 23 Sep 2026: the two Sheba databases share ZERO queries, so the union
## is a true union and sheba_UNION equals sheba_UNION_concat exactly — the
## deduplication added here is a no-op and the recorded 18.0 does not
## double-count. Scale differs markedly between cohorts: pitt 5,262 chaperone
## genes across 6,158 KOs; sheba_UNION 24,319 across 8,750. All 19 chaperone KOs
## are present in every database.
## EXPECTED groel_dnak_pct: pitt 15.3, sheba_UNION 18.0 (database level). The
## 18.0 on record was computed on the CONCATENATED union, so compare it against
## `sheba_UNION_concat`; `sheba_UNION` is the deduplicated figure and is the one
## to report. If the two differ materially, the shared block carries chaperone
## genes and the recorded number double-weights them.

sapply(c("K04080","K04081","K03775","K03771"), `%in%`, ku)
```

```{r observed-composition}
## The "observed in PSMs" column: GroEL/DnaK share among annotated chaperone
## proteins. annot_new annotates the PSM-level extraction (§5b-§5c), so
## `n_chap_genes` counts chaperone PROTEINS observed in PSMs, not database genes.
## Recovered verbatim from the 20 September session.
gd <- c("K04077","K04043")
dbcomp <- purrr::map_dfr(c("pitt","sheba"), function(coh) {
  k <- annot_new$ko_primary[annot_new$cohort == coh &
                            annot_new$ko_primary %in% CHAPERONE_KO]
  tibble::tibble(cohort = coh, n_chap_genes = length(k),
                 groel_dnak = sum(k %in% gd),
                 pct_gd = 100*mean(k %in% gd),
                 n_other_KOs = dplyr::n_distinct(k[!k %in% gd]))
})
dbcomp
## EXPECTED:  pitt   613  224  36.5  17
##            sheba  392  287  73.2  13

## and which chaperone KOs Sheba's observed set lacks relative to Pittsburgh
setdiff(unique(annot_new$ko_primary[annot_new$cohort=="pitt" &
                                    annot_new$ko_primary %in% CHAPERONE_KO]),
        unique(annot_new$ko_primary[annot_new$cohort=="sheba" &
                                    annot_new$ko_primary %in% CHAPERONE_KO]))
## EXPECTED: "K03775" "K04080" "K04081" "K03771"
```

## 12b. Response labels

RECIST best overall response, from the arm's dated clinical records. Sample 83
is a responder on that record (collected one day before the first nivolumab dose).

## 12c. The pre-specified design {#sheba-design-prespec}

**Primary.** COG O; pooled pre-treatment samples from mixtures 1, 3, 4 and 5;
one sample per patient (earliest pre-treatment episode); n = 35 (27 R / 8 NR);
within-plex permutation, 1,000 draws, **two-sided**, with the direction
(NES < 0) also required. Mixture 2 carries no within-plex contrast and is
excluded.

**Secondary.** COG O ∩ chaperones and the chaperone set, BH across the two.

**Exploratory, reported unadjusted.** COG O remainder; COG O ∩ chaperones
without GroEL/DnaK; COG G; ribosomal.

**Monte Carlo precision.** If a reported p's binomial 95% interval includes
0.05, the run extends to 10,000 draws.

**Reading, fixed in advance.** A p above threshold reads as **not detected
before treatment** — consistent with a treatment-emergent difference *or* with
insufficient power, and not separable between them. Not a trend. It neither
confirms nor refutes Pittsburgh's on-treatment association.

The plan, every dated amendment, and one post-opening deviation are in
`PRESPEC_sheba_replication.md`. Scoring used `score_sheba_prespec.R` (checksum
recorded), run unedited; verbatim output in
`SHEBA_scoring_record_2026-09-22.txt`.

## 12d. Result — opened 22 September 2026 {#nulls-sheba}

| | set | size | NES | p | Monte Carlo 95% |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **primary** | COG O | 227 | **−1.48** | **0.155** | 0.132 – 0.178 |
| secondary | COG O ∩ chaperones | 179 | −1.39 | 0.279 | 0.250 – 0.307 |
| secondary | chaperones | 183 | −1.38 | 0.268 | 0.240 – 0.296 |
| exploratory | COG O remainder | 48 | −1.43 | 0.083 | 0.066 – 0.101 |
| exploratory | COG O ∩ chaperones, without GroEL/DnaK | 25 | **+0.68** | 0.912 | 0.893 – 0.929 |
| exploratory | COG G | 1,209 | −0.92 | 0.869 | 0.847 – 0.890 |
| exploratory | ribosomal | 132 | +1.13 | 0.689 | 0.659 – 0.718 |

No NA draws for the primary (COG G lost 13 of 1,000). The primary's interval
excludes 0.05, so no extension was triggered. Secondary q = 0.279 for both.

**Not detected before treatment.**

Two further points belong with it.

**Sheba's COG O lean is not concentrated in its chaperones.** The chaperone
intersection (−1.39) and the non-chaperone remainder (−1.43, p = 0.083) lean
toward non-responders about equally, and without GroEL and DnaK the chaperones
point the other way (+0.68). In Pittsburgh the remainder is flat (+0.79) and the
chaperones carry the set.

**Fragility, reported rather than resolved.** Restricting to the MS2 plexes
(3–5), which drops mixture 1's seven patients and rebuilds the universe at COG O
202 rather than 227, moves the set: at patient level, n = 28, NES −1.75,
p = 0.036 (Monte Carlo 0.025–0.048, excluding 0.05); at the level of sampling
episode, n = 29, which counts one patient twice under opposite labels, NES −1.76,
p = 0.040 (0.028–0.053). The episode-level version was the superseded design; the
patient-level one is the **post hoc** sensitivity specified in §13, run on the
same 1,000-draw machinery. Neither substitutes for the primary, nothing in that
run survives BH (q = 0.63 over 29 sets), and all three are reported.

## 12e. What Sheba can and cannot do {#sheba-role}

Three roles, and no others: a **pre-specified test** of whether the difference
is present before treatment, which bounds the discovery; a **measurement
result** in its own right (§12a); and a **fragility account** (§12d).

It is **not** a replication cohort — the timepoints differ. It is **not** a
pre-versus-on comparison: a between-cohort contrast would alias timepoint with
every other difference between the cohorts. And there is **no paired design** —
7 of 35 Sheba patients have an on-treatment tube, at a median of 422 days after
start, none within 30 days; Pittsburgh's later samples are not accessible.

## 12f. Post hoc power at Sheba's design {#power}

If Sheba **had** carried Pittsburgh's COG O effect, how often would a design like
Sheba's detect it? Two hundred draws: four of Pittsburgh's six analysed plexes,
exactly 2 NR per plex and all available R, fitted and scored, with two within-plex
shuffles of each subsample forming the design's null. Detection is NES < 0 with
|NES| beyond the null's 95th percentile.

| set | null q95 \|NES\| | median subsample NES | power | 95% CI | Sheba's percentile |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| COG O | 1.99 | −1.83 | **0.325** | 0.261–0.395 | 0.815 |
| COG O ∩ chaperones | 2.16 | −2.03 | 0.350 | 0.284–0.420 | 0.915 |
| chaperones | 2.13 | −2.02 | 0.395 | 0.327–0.466 | 0.915 |

Three readings. Carrying Pittsburgh's effect, a Sheba-shaped design detects it
**about one time in three**. Every one of the 200 subsamples gives NES < 0, so
the direction is never in question. And Sheba's opened values sit at the 81st to
92nd percentile of the subsample distribution — weaker than most, but inside the
range, with 8–19% of subsamples weaker still. Sheba does not contradict
Pittsburgh; it is underpowered and on the weak side.

**These are lower bounds, and the reason matters.** Pittsburgh is NR-rich and
Sheba is R-rich, so Sheba's design is not constructible from Pittsburgh at all:
the realized draws are n 21–28 against Sheba's 35, and even all six Pittsburgh
plexes supply only 25 R. Pittsburgh's effect is also *assumed* for Sheba, across
a different protein universe and a different timepoint. The analysis is post hoc
and does not modify the pre-specified reading.

```{r power-score}
## Scores the 200 per-draw files from power_s9_2026-09-22.zip. The analysis
## itself is power_s9.R; this only re-derives the table.
POWER_DIR <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "power_out")
f <- list.files(POWER_DIR, full.names = TRUE)
## Without the archive this used to fail inside quantile() on a NULL column,
## which says nothing about the cause. Name it.
if (!length(f))
  stop("no per-draw files in ", POWER_DIR, ".\n",
       "Extract power_s9_2026-09-22.zip into ", paths$out_dir,
       " — the chunk expects them under power_out/.", call. = FALSE)
d <- do.call(rbind, lapply(f, function(x) as.data.frame(readRDS(x))))
stopifnot("power files lack NES/pathway/kind" =
            all(c("NES", "pathway", "kind") %in% names(d)))
cat(sprintf("power archive: %d files, %d rows, %d draws\n",
            length(f), nrow(d), dplyr::n_distinct(d$draw)))
SHEBA <- c(O = -1.482318, O_chap = -1.393893, chaperones = -1.379892)
do.call(rbind, lapply(names(SHEBA), function(s) {
  ob <- d$NES[d$pathway == s & d$kind == "observed"]
  nu <- d$NES[d$pathway == s & d$kind == "null"]
  q95 <- quantile(abs(nu), 0.95, na.rm = TRUE)
  hit <- ob < 0 & abs(ob) > q95
  ci  <- binom.test(sum(hit), sum(!is.na(ob)))$conf.int
  data.frame(set = s, null_q95 = q95, median_NES = median(ob, na.rm = TRUE),
             frac_negative = mean(ob < 0, na.rm = TRUE), power = mean(hit, na.rm = TRUE),
             lo = ci[1], hi = ci[2], sheba_pctile = mean(ob < SHEBA[s], na.rm = TRUE))
}))
## EXPECTED: O 1.990 / -1.83 / 1.00 / 0.325 (0.261-0.395) / 0.815;
##   O_chap 2.160 / -2.03 / 1.00 / 0.350 (0.284-0.420) / 0.915;
##   chaperones 2.125 / -2.02 / 1.00 / 0.395 (0.327-0.466) / 0.915.
##   Realized design: n 21-28 (median 25), NR always 8, R 13-20; 15 of 15 plex
##   combinations sampled. Scoring instead by one-sided p < 0.05 against the
##   pooled null gives 0.360 / 0.465 / 0.470.
```

```{r protein-phylum-export}
##   Record the DEDUPLICATED file's md5 in the methods — the re-search is only
```
