```{r protein-phylum-export}
##   `sheba1|tr|ACCESSION|NAME_HUMAN`, which holds three pipes. Anything
##   recovering the source database must split on the FIRST pipe only.
##
## VERIFIED 24 Sep 2026 (C1c_verify_db.sh on db_dedup.faa):
##   7,399,630 records, 1.5 GB, md5 761ade04f524f382236f3721d951a27a
##   by source: pitt 1,543,197 (none lost, written first), sheba1 2,694,137,
##              sheba2 3,162,296 — all 460,225 duplicates came off the Sheba files
##   no decoy records; 20,528 human contaminant records; no empty sequences
##
## HOST SEQUENCES, resolved 24 Sep 2026. The same human proteome and contaminant
## set was concatenated to all three databases before their original searches, so
## the concatenated database is complete as built: the 20,528 human records
## survive deduplication once and host proteins remain identifiable. They will be
## reported under a `sheba1` prefix rather than `pitt`, which is cosmetic.
##
## It follows that the file section 1a names for Pittsburgh — which contains no
## human sequences — is not literally the file FragPipe searched; the searched
## one carried human, contaminants and probably decoys. That does not affect this
## re-search or any count above, since the emapper annotations are keyed to
## Prokka locus tags either way, but the methods should describe the search
## database as the Prokka file PLUS the human and contaminant block.
##
## DECOYS, resolved 24 Sep 2026: all three searched databases were decoyed with
## DecoyPYrat, so the re-search must use the same generator. DecoyPYrat shuffles
## peptides while preserving cleavage sites; a search engine's internal generator
## reverses whole proteins, which gives a different null and would be a second
## difference between the runs. Run DecoyPYrat on db_dedup.faa with the original
## parameters and leave FragPipe's own decoy generation OFF.
##
## Target+decoy will be about 14.8M sequences, roughly 3 GB. Check FragPipe's
## memory allocation before starting — the original searches ran against
## databases a fifth this size.
##
## The prefix used here is DECOY_ (e.g. >DECOY_OIDECCNN_00001), which
## C1c_verify_db.sh tests for along with XXX_, rev_ and the rest. Set DecoyPYrat
## to the same prefix on the re-search.
##
## DecoyPYrat prepends to the whole identifier, so decoys of the concatenated
## database will read DECOY_pitt|OIDECCNN_00001. C2_rescore_clade.R recovers the
## source by splitting on the first pipe, so any decoy surviving into the PSM
## table shows up as a source named DECOY_pitt rather than hiding among the
## targets; C2 reports and drops them, and a non-zero count means the FDR filter
## did not do its job.
##
## SUPERSEDED for the re-search pre-flight by C1b_clade_map.sh, 24 Sep 2026.
## This chunk lifts pep_ph to the protein level, which covers only proteins that
## were IDENTIFIED — about 10-20k against Pittsburgh's 1,543,197 database
## records. The pre-flight asks about DATABASE content, and identified proteins
## are a biased sample of exactly that. C1b reads the emapper annotations
## instead and covers roughly two thirds of every database:
##   pitt   1,020,456 of 1,543,197 records annotated
##   sheba1 1,713,330 of 2,827,552
##   sheba2 2,224,829 of 3,489,106
##   pooled 3,720,649 Bacillota, 583,042 Bacteroidota, 380,239 Actinomycetota,
##          274,685 Pseudomonadota — 75% Bacillota against 11.8% Bacteroidota
##
## That skew is worth noting on its own: Pittsburgh's METAGENOME is ~35%
## Bacteroidota, so if its database is ~12%, the database under-represents the
## clade relative to the community it was assembled from. That is the direction
## the database explanation for R3 predicts, and C1_preflight reports it per
## database.
##
## This chunk is retained because the file it writes is still useful for
## identified-protein work, but it must not be used for the pre-flight.
## PROTEIN -> PHYLUM, as a flat file, for C1_preflight.sh.
##
## The concatenated re-search turns on one question: does adding the Sheba
## databases supply Bacteroidota sequence Pittsburgh's lacks? Answering it needs
## a clade label per protein, and the script cannot get that from a FASTA header.
##
## `annot_new` carries protein, cohort and ko_primary only — no taxonomy. The
## taxonomy is in `pep_ph`, which is keyed by PSM ROW, so it has to be lifted to
## the protein level first. A protein can carry rows assigned to different
## phyla; the majority wins, and how often that is contested is reported, since
## a heavily contested mapping would weaken the pre-flight's answer.
local({
  lift <- function(O, pp, tag) {
    if (is.null(O) || is.null(pp)) return(NULL)
    tibble(protein = O$rd$Protein[pp$row], phylum = pp$tax, cohort = tag) |>
      filter(!is.na(protein), !is.na(phylum), nzchar(phylum))
  }
  d <- bind_rows(lift(OP, pep_ph, "pitt"),
                 if (exists("OS") && exists("pep_ph_s")) lift(OS, pep_ph_s, "sheba"))
  if (is.null(d) || !nrow(d)) { cat("protein-phylum export skipped: no taxonomy in scope\n")
                                return(invisible()) }
  votes <- d |> count(protein, phylum, name = "n")
  top   <- votes |> group_by(protein) |> arrange(desc(n), .by_group = TRUE) |>
    summarise(phylum = first(phylum), n_top = first(n), n_all = sum(n), .groups = "drop")
  cat(sprintf("protein-phylum map: %d proteins from %d assigned PSM rows\n",
              nrow(top), nrow(d)))
  cat(sprintf("  contested (more than one phylum for a protein): %d (%.1f%%)\n",
              sum(top$n_top < top$n_all), 100 * mean(top$n_top < top$n_all)))
  cat("  Bacteroidota ", sum(top$phylum == "Bacteroidota"),
      ", Bacillota ", sum(top$phylum %in% c("Bacillota", "Firmicutes")), "\n", sep = "")
  f <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "protein_phylum.tsv")
  write.table(top[, c("protein", "phylum")], f, sep = "\t",
              quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)
  cat("written: ", f, "\n", sep = "")
})
```

```{r coupling-noise-ceiling}
## RESULTS, 24 Sep 2026 (knit 4). This chunk answers the first objection to §11a
## — that 0.238 is low because the assays are noisy — and the answer is no.
##   [A] DEPTH: Spearman +0.002 (p = 0.988) between a patient's own-over-stranger
##       advantage and their sequencing depth, over all 47 patients. FLAT to
##       three decimals. (It skipped on the first attempt because `depth$sample`
##       is the kneaddata file stem and cs$bio is mg_bio()-normalised; the counts
##       were always there and only the key was wrong.)
##   [B] per-family coupling against family abundance: Spearman -0.050
##       (p = 0.198) over 675 families. FLAT. Abundant families, which are
##       measured best, do not couple better. Median per-family coupling +0.031.
##   [C] NOISE CEILING: observed own-coupling 0.238, ceiling 0.240 — 99%.
##       Resampling each patient's gene-family vector from a multinomial at their
##       own depth barely moves the coupling, so metagenomic counting noise is
##       not what limits it and deeper sequencing would not close the gap.
##   [D] POSITIVE CONTROL, same axis (per feature, across patients): genera
##       median +0.301 over 29 genera (Bacillota +0.342) against gene families
##       +0.031 over 675. RATIO 9.6x.
##       Same samples, same two assays, same pipeline. The chain transfers
##       patient-specific information about WHO is present an order of magnitude
##       better than about HOW MUCH PROTEIN each gene family yields.
##
## ALL FOUR CLOSE THE NOISE OBJECTION, from four independent directions: the
## advantage does not grow with sequencing depth, per-family coupling does not
## grow with how well a family is measured, resampling at each patient's own
## depth leaves 1% of headroom, and the same chain couples taxonomy 9.6x better
## than function. [D] is the strongest single comparison in the paper.

## HOW MUCH OF THE WEAK COUPLING IS MEASUREMENT NOISE?
## The obvious objection to §11a is that 0.238 is low because both assays are
## noisy, not because the layers genuinely fail to correspond. Three tests here,
## none of which needs new data.
##
##   [A] DEPTH DEPENDENCE. If sequencing noise limits the coupling, patients with
##       deeper metagenomes should show a larger own-over-stranger advantage. If
##       the advantage is flat in depth, sequencing noise is not the limit.
##   [B] ABUNDANCE DEPENDENCE. Same logic per gene family: abundant families are
##       measured better, so if noise is the limit they should couple better.
##   [C] A NOISE CEILING. Resample each patient's gene-family vector from a
##       multinomial at their observed depth and recouple to their OWN proteome.
##       That is the coupling achievable if the metagenome were the only source
##       of error, and it bounds what any design could reach here.
local({
  need <- c("cpl_MP","cpl_G","cpl_kos","cpl_pat","cpl_stats")
  miss <- need[!vapply(need, exists, logical(1))]
  ## cat, not message: the knit sets message = FALSE, so a skip would be silent.
  if (length(miss)) { cat("noise-ceiling tests skipped; missing: ",
                          paste(miss, collapse=", "), "\n"); return(invisible()) }
  ## Columns, not just objects: a missing column returns NULL and propagates NA
  ## into every test below instead of failing.
  cs <- cpl_stats
  need_col <- c("own","mismatched","delta","p_own","sample","bio")
  mc <- need_col[!need_col %in% names(cs)]
  if (length(mc)) stop("cpl_stats lacks: ", paste(mc, collapse=", "), call. = FALSE)
  EPS <- 1e-9
  ## ---- [A] depth ----
  ## `depth$sample` is the trimmed-file stem from the kneaddata logs, while
  ## cs$bio is mg_bio()-normalised — matching them raw returns all NA, and the
  ## first version of this test then reported "no read counts" when the counts
  ## were there and only the key was wrong. Normalise both sides, and say which
  ## of the two failure modes occurred. (mg_meta carries no reads column at all,
  ## so it is not a fallback; `depth` is also reassigned as a logical inside §11c's
  ## verdict block, hence the is.data.frame guard.)
  dep <- NULL; why <- "no `depth` table in scope"
  if (exists("depth") && is.data.frame(depth) && all(c("sample","reads") %in% names(depth))) {
    kf <- if (exists("mg_bio")) mg_bio else function(z) z
    dep <- depth$reads[match(cs$bio, kf(depth$sample))]
    if (sum(is.finite(dep)) <= 20) {
      dep2 <- depth$reads[match(cs$bio, depth$sample)]          # in case it is already normalised
      if (sum(is.finite(dep2)) > sum(is.finite(dep))) dep <- dep2
    }
    why <- sprintf("`depth` has %d rows but only %d of %d patients matched on bio id; example keys: %s against %s",
                   nrow(depth), sum(is.finite(dep)), nrow(cs),
                   paste(head(kf(depth$sample), 2), collapse="/"),
                   paste(head(cs$bio, 2), collapse="/"))
  }
  if (!is.null(dep) && sum(is.finite(dep)) > 20) {
    ok <- is.finite(dep) & is.finite(cs$delta)
    ct <- suppressWarnings(cor.test(log10(dep[ok]), cs$delta[ok], method = "spearman"))
    cat(sprintf("\n[A] own-over-stranger advantage against sequencing depth, %d patients\n    Spearman %+.3f, p = %.3g\n    %s\n",
      sum(ok), ct$estimate, ct$p.value,
      if (ct$p.value >= 0.05)
        "flat in depth: sequencing noise is not what limits the coupling"
      else "depth-dependent: part of the weakness IS sequencing noise, and must be said"))
  } else cat("\n[A] skipped: ", why, "\n", sep = "")

  ## ---- [B] per-family abundance ----
  ab <- rowMeans(cpl_G[cpl_kos, cs$bio, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
  rho_k <- vapply(cpl_kos, function(k) {
    x <- cpl_MP[k, cs$sample]; y <- cpl_G[k, cs$bio]
    ok <- is.finite(x) & x > 0 & is.finite(y)
    if (sum(ok) < 20) return(NA_real_)
    suppressWarnings(cor(log(x[ok]+EPS), log(y[ok]+EPS), method = "spearman"))
  }, 0)
  ok <- is.finite(rho_k) & is.finite(ab)
  ct2 <- suppressWarnings(cor.test(log10(ab[ok]), rho_k[ok], method = "spearman"))
  cat(sprintf("\n[B] per-family coupling against family abundance, %d families\n    Spearman %+.3f, p = %.3g; median coupling %+.3f\n",
              sum(ok), ct2$estimate, ct2$p.value, median(rho_k[ok])))

  ## ---- [C] added-noise test. NOT a ceiling — see below. ----
## WHAT THIS ACTUALLY MEASURES, corrected 24 Sep 2026. The resample is drawn
## from a multinomial centred on the patient's OBSERVED gene vector, so it asks
## how much a FURTHER round of sampling noise degrades the coupling. A ceiling
## would ask what the coupling becomes with noise REMOVED, which is not estimable
## this way. Two consequences:
##   - the result must not be reported as "observed is 99% of the ceiling";
##   - the resampled value coming out slightly ABOVE observed is a tell, since
##     added noise cannot raise a correlation. It is the `y > 0` filter changing
##     which gene families enter the comparison.
## The size is also not sequencing depth: cpl_G is CPM, so every patient is
## resampled at roughly the same effective sample size, not at their own.
## What survives: adding a full round of multinomial noise at this scale does not
## reduce the coupling, so the coupling is not limited by counting noise of that
## magnitude. The claim that deeper sequencing would not help rests on [A], where
## the advantage is flat across the observed depth range, not on this.
  set.seed(1204); NB <- 50L
  cnt <- cpl_G[cpl_kos, cs$bio, drop = FALSE]
  tot <- colSums(cnt, na.rm = TRUE)
  ceil <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(cs)), function(i) {
    pr <- cnt[, i]; pr[!is.finite(pr) | pr < 0] <- 0
    if (sum(pr) <= 0) return(NA_real_)
    x <- cpl_MP[cpl_kos, cs$sample[i]]
    mean(vapply(seq_len(NB), function(b) {
      y <- rmultinom(1, size = max(round(tot[i]), 1000L), prob = pr / sum(pr))[,1]
      ok <- is.finite(x) & x > 0 & y > 0
      if (sum(ok) < 20) return(NA_real_)
      suppressWarnings(cor(log(x[ok]+EPS), log(y[ok]+EPS), method = "spearman"))
    }, 0), na.rm = TRUE)
  }, 0)
  obs <- median(cs$own, na.rm = TRUE); cl <- median(ceil, na.rm = TRUE)
  cat(sprintf("\n[C] added-noise test (NOT a ceiling; see the note above)\n    observed own-coupling %.3f; after a further round of multinomial noise %.3f (%.0f%% of it)\n    %s\n",
    obs, cl, 100*obs/cl,
    if (isTRUE(is.finite(cl) && is.finite(obs) && obs/cl > 0.9))
      paste("adding a further round of multinomial noise barely changes the coupling,",
            "\n    so it is not limited by counting noise of that magnitude. This is NOT a",
            "\n    ceiling and does not license the deeper-sequencing claim — that rests on [A].")
    else paste("resampling moves the coupling substantially, so part of the weakness",
               "\n    IS metagenomic counting noise and must be reported as such")))

  ## ---- the positive control that is already in hand ----
  ## [D] THE INTERNAL POSITIVE CONTROL. Both quantities are on the same AXIS —
  ## per feature, correlated across patients — but not on the same SCALE: genus
  ## coupling is taken on centred log-ratios and gene-family coupling on raw log.
  ## That choice is conservative: §11c gives 0.380 for genera on raw values
  ## against 0.301 on log-ratios, so using the log-ratio version understates the
  ## gap (9.6x rather than about 12x). State the transform when quoting it.
  ## Comparing either against `obs` would be wrong — obs is per patient across
  ## features, a different axis entirely.
  if (exists("gen_coupling")) {
    g_all  <- median(gen_coupling$rho_clr, na.rm = TRUE)
    g_baci <- median(gen_coupling$rho_clr[gen_coupling$phylum %in% c("Bacillota","Firmicutes")],
                     na.rm = TRUE)
    k_med  <- median(rho_k[ok], na.rm = TRUE)
    cat(sprintf("\n[D] internal positive control, both on the same axis (per feature, across patients)\n    genera:        median %+.3f (Bacillota %+.3f, %d genera)\n    gene families: median %+.3f (%d families)\n    ratio %.1fx\n",
                g_all, g_baci, sum(is.finite(gen_coupling$rho_clr)), k_med, sum(ok), g_all/k_med))
    cat("    The same samples, the same two assays and the same pipeline transfer\n",
        "    patient-specific information about WHO is present roughly an order of\n",
        "    magnitude better than about HOW MUCH PROTEIN each gene family yields.\n",
        "    The measurement chain is not too noisy to couple; it couples taxonomy.\n", sep="")
  }

  ## EXPORT. Everything above is computed inside local() and was saved nowhere,
  ## so the figures could not draw it. These four vectors are what Figure 2's
  ## positive-control and noise panels need.
  noise_diag <<- list(
    rho_family = rho_k[ok],                                  # per family, across patients
    rho_genus  = if (exists("gen_coupling")) gen_coupling$rho_clr else NA_real_,
    genus_phylum = if (exists("gen_coupling")) gen_coupling$phylum else NA_character_,
    own = cs$own, ceiling = ceil, delta = cs$delta,
    depth = if (exists("dep")) dep else NA_real_,
    abundance = ab[ok],
    depth_rho = if (exists("ct")) unname(ct$estimate) else NA_real_,
    depth_p   = if (exists("ct")) ct$p.value else NA_real_)
})
```

```{r clade-restricted-coupling}
## RESULTS, 24 Sep 2026 (knit 4):
##   [item 8] rank of own within its own row: mean 0.438 against 0.5 under the
##            null, one-sample Wilcoxon p = 0.157, 5 of 47 patients below 0.05.
##            The pre-specified paired test gave 0.166. The two statistics AGREE,
##            so the choice of comparator was not what produced the null.
##   [item 7] Of 1,320 shared gene families, 610 are Bacillota-dominated and 34
##            Bacteroidota-dominated — an 18-fold imbalance, so the restricted
##            test could not run. THE IMBALANCE IS THE ANSWER, and it refutes the
##            prediction rather than confirming it: the coupling analysis is
##            already almost entirely a Bacillota analysis, so weak
##            patient-specific coupling cannot be blamed on Bacteroidota. Within
##            the clade whose genus abundance DOES couple (+0.342), gene-family
##            output still does not. The two results are separate findings, and
##            the manuscript must not claim one explains the other.

## ITEMS 7 AND 8 of the submission checklist, run together because they use the
## same machinery.
##
## ITEM 7 — THE PREDICTION, STATED BEFORE THE RESULT. §11c finds that genus
## abundance couples between layers in Bacillota and not in Bacteroidota. §11a
## finds that a patient's own metagenome barely beats a stranger's overall. If
## the first explains the second, then restricting the own-versus-stranger test
## to Bacillota-derived gene families must RAISE the advantage, and restricting
## to Bacteroidota-derived families must ABOLISH it. Any other pattern — both
## up, both down, or the reverse ordering — refutes the link and is reported as
## such. This is a prediction the existing results generate, not a search.
##
## ITEM 8 — THE RANK STATISTIC. §11a's headline compares own against the MEDIAN
## of 46 strangers by paired Wilcoxon. The rank of own within its own row is
## uniform under the null, uses every own-against-stranger comparison rather
## than one median per patient,
## and does not average away the comparator's variance. Reported alongside; the
## paired Wilcoxon stays primary because it is what was pre-specified.
local({
  need <- c("cpl_MP","cpl_G","cpl_kos","cpl_stats","pep_ph","annot_new","OP")
  miss <- need[!vapply(need, exists, logical(1))]
  ## cat, not message: the knit sets message = FALSE, so a skip here would be
  ## silent and item 7's result would simply be absent with nothing to say why.
  if (length(miss)) { cat("clade-restricted coupling SKIPPED; missing: ",
                          paste(miss, collapse=", "), "\n", sep = "")
                      return(invisible()) }
  cs <- cpl_stats
  mc <- setdiff(c("own","mismatched","p_own","sample","bio"), names(cs))
  if (length(mc)) stop("cpl_stats lacks: ", paste(mc, collapse=", "), call. = FALSE)

  ## ---- item 8 first: it needs nothing but cpl_pat ----
  rk <- cs$p_own[is.finite(cs$p_own)]
  w8 <- suppressWarnings(wilcox.test(rk - 0.5))
  cat(sprintf("\n[item 8] rank of own within its own row, %d patients\n    mean %.3f (0.5 under the null), one-sample Wilcoxon p = %.4g\n    patients below 0.05: %d; pre-specified paired test gave p = 0.166\n",
              length(rk), mean(rk), w8$p.value, sum(rk < 0.05)))

  ## ---- item 7: partition gene families by the clade that carries their protein ----
  ko_of <- setNames(annot_new$ko_primary[annot_new$cohort == "pitt"],
                    annot_new$protein[annot_new$cohort == "pitt"])
  ph <- tibble(row = pep_ph$row, tax = pep_ph$tax) |>
    mutate(protein = OP$rd$Protein[row], ko = unname(ko_of[protein])) |>
    filter(!is.na(ko), ko %in% cpl_kos, tax %in% c("Bacillota","Firmicutes","Bacteroidota"))
  frac <- ph |> mutate(tax = ifelse(tax == "Firmicutes", "Bacillota", tax)) |>
    count(ko, tax) |> group_by(ko) |>
    summarise(n = sum(n), f_baci = sum(n[tax == "Bacillota"]) / sum(n), .groups = "drop") |>
    filter(n >= 5)
  K_baci  <- frac$ko[frac$f_baci >= 0.6]
  K_bacte <- frac$ko[frac$f_baci <= 0.4]
  cat(sprintf("\n[item 7] gene families with a dominant clade (>=60%% of assigned rows, >=5 rows):\n    Bacillota %d, Bacteroidota %d, of %d shared\n",
              length(K_baci), length(K_bacte), length(cpl_kos)))
  if (min(length(K_baci), length(K_bacte)) < 40) {
    cat(sprintf("    The restricted test cannot run — but the asymmetry is itself the\n    answer. Of %d shared families, %d are Bacillota-dominated and only %d are\n    Bacteroidota-dominated, an %.0f-fold imbalance. The coupling analysis is\n    therefore ALREADY almost entirely a Bacillota analysis, so the weak\n    patient-specific coupling cannot be attributed to Bacteroidota's failure to\n    correspond. The two results are NOT one mechanism: within the clade whose\n    genus abundance does couple between layers, gene-family output still does\n    not. Report it that way.\n",
                length(cpl_kos), length(K_baci), length(K_bacte),
                length(K_baci)/max(length(K_bacte),1)))
    return(invisible())
  }

  EPS <- 1e-9; MIN_KO <- 20L
  arm <- function(ks, lab) {
    cf <- function(i, j) {
      x <- cpl_MP[ks, cs$sample[i]]; y <- cpl_G[ks, cs$bio[j]]
      ok <- is.finite(x) & x > 0 & is.finite(y)
      if (sum(ok) < MIN_KO) return(NA_real_)
      suppressWarnings(cor(log(x[ok]+EPS), log(y[ok]+EPS), method = "spearman"))
    }
    N <- nrow(cs)
    K <- vapply(seq_len(N), function(j) vapply(seq_len(N), function(i) cf(i,j), 0), numeric(N))
    own <- diag(K)
    mis <- vapply(seq_len(N), function(i) median(K[i,-i], na.rm=TRUE), 0)
    rr  <- vapply(seq_len(N), function(i) mean(K[i,-i] >= own[i], na.rm=TRUE), 0)
    w   <- suppressWarnings(wilcox.test(own, mis, paired = TRUE))
    cat(sprintf("    %-14s %4d KOs | own %.3f, stranger %.3f, delta %+.4f, %d of %d, p = %.3g | rank mean %.3f\n",
                lab, length(ks), median(own,na.rm=TRUE), median(mis,na.rm=TRUE),
                median(own-mis,na.rm=TRUE), sum(own>mis,na.rm=TRUE), N, w$p.value, mean(rr,na.rm=TRUE)))
    c(delta = median(own-mis, na.rm=TRUE), p = w$p.value, rank = mean(rr, na.rm=TRUE))
  }
  cat("\n    prediction: Bacillota delta > all delta > Bacteroidota delta\n")
  a_all <- arm(cpl_kos, "all shared")
  a_bac <- arm(K_baci,  "Bacillota")
  a_bct <- arm(K_bacte, "Bacteroidota")
  ok <- a_bac["delta"] > a_all["delta"] && a_bct["delta"] < a_all["delta"]
  cat("\n    VERDICT: ", if (ok)
"the prediction holds. The weak patient-specific coupling and the clade structure
    are one mechanism, not two findings: coupling is weak overall because a large
    share of the proteome comes from a clade whose layers do not correspond.
    Report this as the link between the two results."
else
"the prediction does NOT hold in the stated direction. The clade structure does
    not explain the weak patient-specific coupling, and the two results stay
    separate. Report the ordering as measured and drop any claim that one
    explains the other.", "\n")
})
```

```{r b12-sheba-coupling}
## B12 — own versus stranger in Sheba. Kept as a SCRIPT because it depends on
## S10_sheba_ko_regroup.sh, which runs HUMAnN on the server; sourced here so the
## knit runs it whenever that output is present, and no live console session is
## ever needed. Same pattern as `restoration-null-check` and `power-score`.
##
## The objects it needs — OS, annot_new, sh_set5, sh_id, pep_g_s, pep_ph_s,
## sh_mpa_raw — are built in §2f, §5c, §10e and §12 and exist here. They are NOT
## in the bundle (which carries mp, annot, SAMP and the constants) and pep_g_s,
## sh_mpa_raw and sh_id are not in figure_inputs.rds either, so this cannot be
## run from either of those.
## Left unset unless ICB_SHEBA_KO is given: the script searches the plausible
## locations itself and prefers the un-renormalised table, which is the one that
## matches how §10c builds Pittsburgh's ko_cpm.
if (nzchar(Sys.getenv("ICB_SHEBA_KO"))) SHEBA_KO <- Sys.getenv("ICB_SHEBA_KO")
.ko_any <- any(file.exists(file.path(paths$out_dir,
  c("sheba_genefamilies_ko_joined.tsv", "sheba_ko/sheba_genefamilies_ko_joined.tsv",
    "sheba_ko_cpm_joined.tsv", "sheba_ko/sheba_ko_cpm_joined.tsv"))))
## Where the script lives. REANNOT_DIR happens to resolve to the project root,
## but it is named for the annotation exports and a future edit to it would move
## this silently — so search the plausible roots instead and say which was used.
B12_SCRIPT <- local({
  if (nzchar(Sys.getenv("ICB_B12"))) return(Sys.getenv("ICB_B12"))
  cand <- c(here::here("B12_sheba_coupling.R"),
            file.path(REANNOT_DIR, "B12_sheba_coupling.R"),
            file.path(paths$out_dir, "B12_sheba_coupling.R"),
            "B12_sheba_coupling.R")
  hit <- cand[file.exists(cand)]
  if (length(hit)) hit[1] else cand[1]
})
if (!.ko_any && !(exists("SHEBA_KO") && file.exists(SHEBA_KO))) {
  cat("B12 SKIPPED: no Sheba KO table under ", paths$out_dir,
      "\n  run S10_sheba_ko_regroup.sh on the server first, or set ICB_SHEBA_KO.\n",
      sep = "")
} else if (!file.exists(B12_SCRIPT)) {
  cat("B12 SKIPPED: script not found. Put B12_sheba_coupling.R in the project ",
      "root (beside analysis_v17.Rmd), or set ICB_B12. Looked at:\n  ", B12_SCRIPT, "\n",
      sep = "")
} else {
  cat("B12 script:", B12_SCRIPT, "\n")
  source(B12_SCRIPT, local = TRUE, echo = FALSE)
}
## RESULT, 24 Sep 2026, on the PRE-SPECIFIED pooled proteome set: 30 paired
## patients, 1,116 shared gene families. (An earlier run on OS / sheba_ontx gave
## 24 pairs and is superseded; the pooled set is the pre-specified primary.)
##   [1] all KOs      delta -0.0017, 13 of 30, p = 0.79
##   [2] top 200 core delta -0.0061, 15 of 30, p = 0.33, 0 patients significant
##   [2b] bootstrap CI -0.0604 to +0.0325; power at Pittsburgh's +0.033 is 0.30;
##        smallest shift detected 80% of the time is +0.075, i.e. 2.3x Pittsburgh
##   [3] clade (CLR)  Bacteroidota +0.236, Bacillota +0.203
##
## PILLAR 1 DOES NOT REPLICATE, AND THE TEST CANNOT RULE THE EFFECT OUT EITHER.
## Going from 24 to 30 pairs moved the powered arm from +0.0030 to -0.0061 and
## the per-patient count to exactly half, so the larger, pre-specified set is the
## more negative one. But [2b] is what the manuscript should quote: this design
## resolves a Pittsburgh-sized shift 30% of the time and needs +0.075 for 80%.
## Pittsburgh's +0.0333 sits 0.0008 outside the interval's upper bound, which is
## a boundary coincidence and NOT an exclusion — do not report it as one.
##
## Artefact checks, from the same run:
##   (i)  7 of 30 paired patients gave more than one tube, so 23 pair a single
##        collection. Pittsburgh pairs one stool via BioReplicate (an MF sample
##        id); this pairs a patient. The difference is real but smaller than
##        feared.
##   (ii) The pooled proteome spans both arm labels while every metagenome is
##        pre-treatment. §0a assigns Sheba mixtures 3-5 to the on-treatment arm
##        by MIXTURE when timing is missing, and the metagenome records mark the
##        S-series tubes pre-treatment — so the `ontx` label is probably an
##        artefact of that fallback, not a timing mismatch between layers.
##  (iii) The clade arm still inverts Pittsburgh (Bacteroidota couples BETTER),
##        and remains exposed to the handling difference: Sheba's metagenomic
##        Bacteroidota is ~3% against ~35%.
##
## What it settles: Pillar 1 is a single-cohort result and the manuscript must
## say so.
```

```{r b13-sheba-clade}
## B13 — R3 in the second cohort, sourced as B12 is.
## NOT A BLIND TEST. B12's arm [3] already ran the section 11c procedure on 30
## Sheba patients and found no clade gap (Bacteroidota +0.236, Bacillota +0.203).
## B13 reproduces that exactly, then aligns the one procedural difference that
## matters — Pittsburgh's MetaPhlAn database, vJan25 — with an MS2-only
## sensitivity, and reads each clade gap against Pittsburgh's by bootstrap
## interval. Every arm and the decision rule are written in the script before it
## runs. Needs B12's saved output and the vJan25 re-profiled table.
.find_script <- function(fname, env) {
  if (nzchar(Sys.getenv(env))) return(Sys.getenv(env))
  cand <- c(here::here(fname), file.path(REANNOT_DIR, fname),
            file.path(paths$out_dir, fname), fname)
  hit <- cand[file.exists(cand)]; if (length(hit)) hit[1] else cand[1]
}

if (file.exists(.b13)) {

} else cat("B13 SKIPPED: script not found. Put B13_sheba_clade.R beside ",
           "analysis_v17.Rmd, or set ICB_B13.\n", sep = "")
```

```{r b1c-record, eval = FALSE}
## ============================================================================
## MULTIPLICITY CORRECTION: FINAL, 10,000 DRAWS (27 Sep 2026)
## ============================================================================
## Archive nulls_pitt_full, 9,999 + 1 draw files, no gaps or duplicates, scored
## to full_space_scored_10k.csv. Same 565-set family, samples, model and seeds as
## the 1,000-draw run; only the number of draws differs.
##
##   set                  NES    p(1k)   p(10k)  rank/502  FWER     q
##   reported:O_chap     -2.47   0.0030   0.0078      7      0.856  0.4216
##   reported:chaperones -2.41   0.0030   0.0083      9      0.872  0.4216
##   reported:O          -2.22   0.0060   0.0112     12      0.930  0.4692
##   reported:ribosomal  -1.78   0.0868   0.0901     65      1.000  0.6717
##   smallest FWER anywhere in the family: 0.703 (GrpE / PF01025)
##
## THREE FAMILIES, DELIBERATELY DIFFERENT (B1d, 28 Sep 2026):
##   FWER  over all 565 scored sets. Westfall-Young is unaffected by duplicate
##         member lists — perfectly correlated tests cannot inflate a maximum —
##         so the family is every set scored.
##   RANK  over the 502 DISTINCT member lists. 63 of the 565 are the same gene
##         set under two names, and a set named twice is not two pieces of
##         evidence that it is extreme. The GrpE KO and its Pfam domain are such
##         a pair and sit directly above the chaperone sets, which is why the
##         rank moves 8 -> 7.
##   FDR   over the same 502. Effect is negligible: 0.4314 -> 0.4216. The
##         direction is not predictable in advance, because duplicating a test
##         raises both the denominator and that p's rank.
##
## THE 1,000-DRAW p WAS A SMALL-SAMPLE ARTEFACT. At a true rate near 0.008,
## 1,000 draws should give about eight exceedances; O_chap got two. The set was
## highlighted partly because that luck put it at the resolution floor, which is
## also why its rank moved from the tied group to 8th.
##
## NOTHING SURVIVES CORRECTION. The family-wise value is now estimable and it is
## 0.86; the smallest anywhere is 0.70; the minimum q is 0.43. The manuscript
## reports rank and says so plainly, and quotes the 10,000-draw full-space values
## throughout rather than the 30-set run's 1,000-draw p.
##
## The most extreme sets in the survey are GrpE (K03687), its Pfam domain
## (PF01025), DnaK (K04043) and the HSP70 domain (PF00012), all above the
## aggregate sets. They are nested within one another, so this is one signal seen
## several ways and must not be counted as four hits.
##
## Figure 4F recomputes all of this from the draws rather than reading the CSV;
## it reproduces the scored values exactly.
##
## TWO CONSERVATISMS IN THE FDR COLUMN, corrected 28 Sep 2026. Neither changes a
## conclusion — nothing approaches 0.05 either way — but a q reported larger than
## it should be is not a neutral error.
##   [a] 63 of the 565 sets share a member list with another set under a
##       different name. Two sets with the same members are one test, so BH
##       should run over the 502 distinct ones. The DIRECTION of the correction
##       is not predictable: duplicating a test duplicates its p-value, raising
##       both the denominator and that p's rank, and BH is p*m/rank. For a
##       duplicated small p the rank effect dominates and the as-counted q is too
##       SMALL. Simulated at this table's scale the correction spans 0.95x to
##       1.78x depending on where the duplicates sit, so B1d_distinct_fdr.R is
##       run to obtain the right number rather than a smaller one. The min-P
##       family-wise value is unaffected, since perfectly correlated tests cannot
##       inflate a Westfall-Young maximum.
##   [b] BH assumes every test is null. On the protein family ashr measured
##       pi0 = 0.465, so roughly half of those tests are not null and BH is
##       conservative there by about 1/pi0 = 2.15x. A set-level pi0 has NOT been
##       estimated and the 6,939-protein value must not be carried across to the
##       565-set family; until it is, the set-level q stays as BH and is
##       described as an upper bound rather than an estimate.
```

```{r full-space-input}
## B1's correction runs over the whole examined search space, not the 30 sets
## carried into the null. Its input was previously built by running
## B1_full_space_prep.R in a live session — which knitting does not leave behind.
## Written here so the knit produces it, on whatever universe §6a currently
## defines (R1+R2+R3, 5,106 proteins, verified against the record on 24 Sep).
local({
  MIN_N <- 10L
  flat <- function(lst, tag) {
    if (!length(lst)) return(list())
    x <- lapply(lst, intersect, names(stat)); x <- x[lengths(x) >= MIN_N]
    if (!length(x)) return(list())
    setNames(x, paste0(tag, ":", names(x)))
  }
  examined <- do.call(c, lapply(c("KO","COG","Pfam","KEGGmod","KEGGpath"),
                                function(L) if (!is.null(sets[[L]])) flat(sets[[L]], L) else list()))
  SETS_FULL <- c(examined, setNames(SETS_P, paste0("reported:", names(SETS_P))))
  SETS_FULL <- SETS_FULL[!duplicated(names(SETS_FULL))]

## DEDUPLICATE BY MEMBERSHIP, NOT ONLY BY NAME.
## 63 of the 565 sets carry a member list identical to another set's under a
## different name — the same test counted twice. Name-deduplication does not see
## them. They do not affect the min-P family-wise value, because perfectly
## correlated tests cannot inflate a Westfall-Young maximum, which is part of why
## that procedure was chosen. They DO inflate the Benjamini-Hochberg denominator,
## by 565/502 = 1.13, which makes every reported q about 13% too large.
## Both counts are kept: the family is scored as before so the FWER is unchanged,
## and the distinct-membership count is carried alongside for the FDR column.
.memkey <- vapply(SETS_FULL, function(v) paste(sort(unique(v)), collapse = "\u0001"), "")
SETS_DISTINCT <- SETS_FULL[!duplicated(.memkey)]
c(sets_named = length(SETS_FULL), sets_distinct = length(SETS_DISTINCT),
  duplicate_member_lists = length(SETS_FULL) - length(SETS_DISTINCT))
  print(c(vapply(c("KO","COG","Pfam","KEGGmod","KEGGpath"),
                 function(L) sum(startsWith(names(SETS_FULL), paste0(L, ":"))), 0L),
          reported = sum(startsWith(names(SETS_FULL), "reported:")),
          TOTAL = length(SETS_FULL)))
  stopifnot(length(SETS_FULL) > length(SETS_P),
            all(c("reported:O", "reported:chaperones") %in% names(SETS_FULL)))
  OUT <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "full_space")
  dir.create(OUT, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  ## run_null.R reads SETS_P by name, so the full space is handed over under it
  SETS_P <- SETS_FULL
  save(qf, SAMP_PRIMARY, PARAMS, RESP_LEVELS, SETS_P, SETS_S, KEEP_P, KEEP_S,
       fit_arm, pick_denom, arm_mix_v13,
       file = file.path(OUT, "null_input.RData"), compress = "xz")
  saveRDS(vapply(SETS_FULL, length, 0L), file.path(OUT, "set_sizes.rds"))
  cat(sprintf("full-space input: %d sets, %.1f MB -> %s\n", length(SETS_FULL),
              file.size(file.path(OUT, "null_input.RData")) / 1e6, OUT))
})
## EXPECTED on the verified universe: 108 KO + 21 COG + 244 Pfam + 86 KEGGmod +
## 79 KEGGpath = 538 examined, plus 30 reported = 568 sets.
##
## RESULT, 24 Sep 2026 (nulls_pitt_full_2026-09-24.zip, 1,000 draws over 565
## sets: 105 KO, 21 COG, 244 Pfam, 86 KEGGmod, 79 KEGGpath, 30 reported — the
## input was built in a session and lost 3 KO sets to the extra names(stat)
## intersect, so 535 examined rather than 538).
##
## NOTHING SURVIVES, AND THE CHAPERONE SETS ARE NOT MARGINAL.
##   zero of 565 at family-wise p < 0.05; zero at BH q < 0.05 (min q = 0.329)
##
##   CORRECTED 24 Sep 2026. An earlier reading of this run scored the correction
##   with max|NES| and reported 0.0589 / 0.0949 / 0.3137. That is the wrong
##   statistic: the per-set null spread of |NES| runs 0.13 to 0.48, so NES is not
##   comparable across sets and the maximum is dominated by whichever sets have
##   wide nulls. B1b used minimum-p Westfall-Young, which is correct, and its
##   values have been reproduced independently:
##
##   set                 p_set    FWER (min-P)
##   O_chap              0.003        0.572
##   chaperones          0.003        0.572
##   COG O               0.006        0.789
##   O_chap_noGD         0.030        0.997
##
##   The decisive number: the MEDIAN SMALLEST per-set p across 565 sets is 0.0030
##   — exactly O_chap's observed value. In half of all permutations some set
##   reaches that by chance, which is what a space of this size does. The most
##   extreme set by min-P is KO:K03687, at 0.465; O_chap is not the leader.
##
##   THIRD CORRECTION, same day: 0.572 is not an estimate either. At 1,000 draws
##   the min-p statistic is QUANTISED — the only family-wise value below 0.05 that
##   can be reached is the zero-exceedance one; k=1 gives 0.28, k=2 gives 0.47.
##   O_chap has k=2, so its family-wise value turns on two permutation draws.
##   There is also an estimator mismatch: the observed p uses (1+k)/(1+n) and the
##   null's per-set p uses rank/n, and that boundary alone moves the answer
##   between 0.465 and 0.572. Both must use one convention.
##
##   WHAT TO REPORT UNTIL 10,000 DRAWS EXIST -- they exist as of 27 Sep 2026,
##   and the FINAL block above is what the manuscript quotes. Kept as the dated
##   record of the 1,000-draw run: the RANK, which does not depend on
##   the number of permutations. Ordered by per-set p across 565 sets, O_chap is
##   4th and the full chaperone set 5th, tied with three others at the resolution
##   floor (PF13620, KO:K03687, Pfam:PF01025). The "most extreme of 565" claim is
##   withdrawn; so is any quoted family-wise p.
##
## Consequence, as pre-committed in §13 item 9: R4 is a discovery-level result,
## not a corrected one. The two-pillar structure was built to survive this.
```

```{r bundle-objects}
## The `export-bundle` listing in §0b needs mp, annot, SAMP and the constants.
## Knitting runs in its OWN process, which exits — so a console session started
## afterwards has none of them, and the listing failed with "object 'mp' not
## found". Written here instead, at the end of every run, so the bundle can be
## assembled later from a cold session.
BUNDLE_OBJ <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "bundle_objects.rds")
local({
  MP_SLOTS <- c("pitt_mat_f", "pitt_annot_use", "sheba_annot_use",
                "pitt_pw_map_obs", "host_state")
  miss <- MP_SLOTS[!MP_SLOTS %in% names(mp)]
  if (length(miss)) stop("mp lacks: ", paste(miss, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
  saveRDS(list(mp = mp[MP_SLOTS], annot = annot, SAMP = SAMP,
               SAMP_PRIMARY = SAMP_PRIMARY, TIER_PRIMARY = TIER_PRIMARY,
               PARAMS = PARAMS, RESP_LEVELS = RESP_LEVELS), BUNDLE_OBJ)
})
cat(sprintf("bundle objects: %.0f MB -> %s\n",
            file.size(BUNDLE_OBJ) / 1e6, BUNDLE_OBJ))
```

```{r figure-inputs}
## Everything figures_v2.Rmd needs, written once at the end of a full run so the
## figures can be knit in a FRESH session rather than only in this one. Names are
## the collision-proof ones where the document reuses a name later.
SAVE_FIGURE_INPUTS <- TRUE
if (SAVE_FIGURE_INPUTS) {
  ## MAIN figures (Figures 1-5)
  want_main <- c("OP", "cpl_MP", "cpl_G", "cpl_kos", "cpl_pat", "gen_coupling", "MGm", "MPm",
                 "SETS_P", "stat_pitt", "pep_g", "pep_ph", "pep_fa", "hs", "INFL", "cpl_stats",
                 "chap_new", "ribo_new", "CHAPERONE_KO", "RIBO_KO", "chap_frac_of")
  ## SUPPLEMENT (S1-S16). Added 24 Sep 2026: the supplement needs objects the
  ## main figures never touched, and without them figures_v2.Rmd can only be knit
  ## in the analysis session — which is the thing figure_inputs.rds exists to
  ## avoid. Missing entries are reported, not fatal: a supplementary panel that
  ## cannot be built degrades to a labelled placeholder.
  ## ADDED 10 Oct 2026: off3, bp, bs4. All three are need()-ed by
  ## figures_v2.Rmd and none was in this list, so the first knit of the figures
  ## in a FRESH session (after an R restart) wrote S4D and S7C as error boxes
  ## while this chunk reported "74 of 74 objects" -- true, and uninformative,
  ## because the names were not in the list being counted. off3 is off2 plus
  ## sd_based; bp/bs4 are the SHARED-database (vOct22_202403) Bacteroidota
  ## fractions, 68 and 32 samples, which the standalone MetaPhlAn profiles in
  ## `phy`/`sh_phy` cannot substitute for -- different CHOCOPhlAn databases per
  ## cohort, so they are not comparable across cohorts, which is S7C's point.
  ##
  ## NOT set_offset / prot_of. figures_v2.Rmd can rebuild off3 from those two,
  ## but they are closures over `pm` (= mp$pitt_mat_f) and saveRDS serialises a
  ## closure's environment, so exporting them would add the whole Pittsburgh
  ## matrix to a bundle that is already 302 MB. Exporting off3 itself -- 60 rows
  ## -- makes the rebuild branch dead code, which is where it belongs.
  want_supp <- c(
    "qf", "mp", "r2",                            # S1  technical / plex exposure
    "hi",                                        # S3  host inflammation
    "st0", "st1", "sets", "FG",                  # S4  specification sensitivity
    "sets_s", "st_s", "SETS_S", "FS",            # S5, S16 cross-cohort sets, Sheba
    "annot_new", "annot_old", "cmp_cog",         # S5, S6 membership and taxonomy
    "off", "off2", "off3", "nullspread",         # S7  plex offsets
    "depth", "phy", "comp_all", "KEEP_5M",       # S8  metagenome depth/composition
    "sh_set5", "sh_phy", "sh_comp",              # S8  Sheba metagenome
    "MG_DB", "MG_DB_HUMANN", "MG_NCOL", "DB",    # S10 provenance and the gate
    "jp", "tot", "tot_exposure", "ribo_genus_scan", "ribo_blautia_sheba", "tot_res",                      # S11 time on treatment
    "tot_balance", "gen_depth_terms", "ribo_scan_summary", "ribo_blautia_ko",   # subtitle statistics, 13 Oct 2026
    "pw", "pr", "pep_ph_s", "OS", "bp", "bs4",   # S13 Bacteroidota both cohorts
    "pep_g_s", "sh_mpa_raw", "sh_id",            # B12's Sheba clade arm
    "noise_diag",                                # Fig 2 positive control + noise
    "norm_id", "mg_clean",                       # helpers the figures re-derive
    "gd_analysis_universe",                      # Fig 5B, so it is not recomputed
    "b13_clade", "b14_magnitude",                # R3 in Sheba; coupling magnitude, Fig 5E
    "scan", "scan2", "bs",                       # S14 Blautia and the genus scan
    "sysv", "cat_tab",                           # S15 KEGG systems view
    "ko_cpm", "mpa_raw", "smap")                 # shared by several
  want <- c(want_main, want_supp)
  ## MGm WAS SILENTLY REPLACED ONCE. B12 is sourced after section 11c and
  ## assigned MGm at top level, so its 30-patient Sheba matrix overwrote the
  ## Pittsburgh one and went into this bundle under the Pittsburgh name. C2 then
  ## failed with "0 channels in both layers". B12's names carry a b12_ prefix
  ## now; this asserts the result rather than trusting it.
  if (exists("MGm") && exists("MPm")) {
    if (!identical(rownames(MGm), rownames(MPm)))
      stop("MGm and MPm are no longer aligned (", nrow(MGm), " rows against ",
           nrow(MPm), ").\n  Section 11c builds them on one index; something ",
           "downstream has overwritten MGm. Find it before exporting.",
           call. = FALSE)
    cat(sprintf("MGm/MPm aligned: %d patients x %d genera\n", nrow(MGm), ncol(MGm)))
  }
  have <- want[vapply(want, exists, logical(1))]
  miss <- setdiff(want, have)

    m_main <- intersect(miss, want_main); m_supp <- intersect(miss, want_supp)

      warning("MAIN figure inputs missing: ", paste(m_main, collapse = ", "),
              " — Figures 1-5 will have placeholder panels.", call. = FALSE)
    if (length(m_supp))
      message("supplement inputs not in this session (their panels will be ",
              "placeholders): ", paste(m_supp, collapse = ", "))
  }
  fi <- file.path(paths$out_dir, "figure_inputs.rds")
  saveRDS(setNames(lapply(have, get), have), fi)
  cat(sprintf("figure inputs: %d of %d objects, %.0f MB -> %s\n",
              length(have), length(want), file.size(fi) / 1e6, fi))
}
```

# 14. Controls added for review {#reviewcontrols}

Three controls that §13 item 7 recorded as run but unported, or that were asked
for and had never been run. Each is self-contained: it rebuilds what it needs
from the objects above rather than relying on anything inside an earlier
`local()`, and each prints a skip line rather than failing if an input is absent.

## 14a. Are chaperone peptides assignable to phylum at the same rate as the rest?

C10d reports chaperone density as a share of **phylum-assigned** PSM rows —
9.65% of Bacillota against 0.86% of Bacteroidota. The denominator is the
assigned rows, so the number is only a statement about biology if chaperone
peptides resolve to phylum at the same rate as peptides in general, in both
clades. GroEL and DnaK are among the most conserved proteins in bacteria, so
their tryptic peptides are exactly the ones an LCA would resolve *above* phylum.
That had not been tested.

```{r c14a-chaperone-assignability}
local({
  req <- c("OP", "chap_new", "lca_all2", "annot_new")
  miss <- req[!vapply(req, exists, logical(1))]
  if (length(miss)) {
    cat("14a skipped; missing: ", paste(miss, collapse = ", "), "\n"); return(invisible())
  }
  ## taxon_rank is projected into lca_all2 only if the cache carried it (§5's
  ## keep_cols), so it is optional here and [2] falls back without it.
  lr <- lca_all2 |> dplyr::filter(cohort == "pitt") |>
    dplyr::select(seq = peptide, phylum_name,
                  dplyr::any_of("taxon_rank")) |>
    dplyr::mutate(phylum_name = dplyr::na_if(trimws(as.character(phylum_name)), "")) |>
    dplyr::distinct(seq, .keep_all = TRUE)

  gd <- annot_new$protein[annot_new$cohort == "pitt" &
                            annot_new$ko_primary %in% c("K04077", "K04043")]

  rows <- tibble::tibble(row = seq_len(nrow(OP$a)), seq = OP$rd$seq,
                         Protein = OP$rd$Protein) |>
    dplyr::left_join(lr, by = "seq") |>
    dplyr::mutate(set = dplyr::case_when(Protein %in% gd       ~ "GroEL/DnaK",
                                         Protein %in% chap_new ~ "other chaperone",
                                         TRUE                  ~ "everything else"),
                  in_unipept = seq %in% lr$seq,
                  to_phylum  = !is.na(phylum_name))

  ## ---- [1] the rate, overall -------------------------------------------------
  s1 <- rows |> dplyr::group_by(set) |>
    dplyr::summarise(psm_rows = dplyr::n(), to_phylum = mean(to_phylum), .groups = "drop")
  cat("\n[1] phylum-assignment rate of PSM rows\n")
  print(as.data.frame(s1 |> dplyr::mutate(to_phylum = round(100 * to_phylum, 1))))
  ## chisq, not fisher.test: this is a 2x2 on ~10^5 rows, where the exact test
  ## is slow and buys nothing. The odds ratio is computed from the table.
  rows$grp <- ifelse(rows$set == "everything else", "rest", "chaperone")
  tb <- table(grp = rows$grp, resolved = rows$to_phylum)
  if (all(dim(tb) == c(2, 2))) {
    or <- (tb[1, 2] * tb[2, 1]) / (tb[1, 1] * tb[2, 2])
    cat(sprintf("    chaperone against the rest: odds ratio %.2f for resolving, chi-square p = %.3g\n",
                or, suppressWarnings(chisq.test(tb))$p.value))
  }

  ## ---- [2] where the unresolved ones stop ------------------------------------
  ## THREE OUTCOMES, NOT TWO. A peptide either resolves to phylum or below; or
  ## is in the Unipept table with the LCA sitting ABOVE phylum, so no phylum can
  ## be named; or has no Unipept result at all. The middle outcome is the
  ## reviewer's mechanism -- a peptide conserved across phyla cannot resolve to
  ## one -- and it is the only outcome a conserved chaperone would produce. A
  ## deficit in the third would be a cache gap instead, which is a different
  ## problem with a different fix.
  pct_tab <- function(df, col) {
    out <- df |> dplyr::count(grp, .data[[col]]) |> dplyr::group_by(grp) |>
      dplyr::mutate(pct = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)) |> dplyr::ungroup() |>
      dplyr::select(-n) |>
      tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = grp, values_from = pct, values_fill = 0)
    if (all(c("chaperone", "rest") %in% names(out)))
      out <- dplyr::arrange(out, dplyr::desc(chaperone))
    as.data.frame(out)
  }
  cat("\n[2] what happened to each peptide (% of rows)\n")
  print(pct_tab(rows |> dplyr::mutate(outcome = dplyr::case_when(
    to_phylum  ~ "to phylum or below",
    in_unipept ~ "above phylum, LCA too broad",
    TRUE       ~ "no Unipept result")), "outcome"))
  if ("taxon_rank" %in% names(rows)) {
    cat("\n    LCA rank reached\n")
    print(pct_tab(rows |> dplyr::mutate(
      rank = dplyr::coalesce(as.character(taxon_rank), "none")), "rank"))
  }

  ## ---- [3] the rate WITHIN each clade ----------------------------------------
  ## THE CIRCULARITY, AND HOW IT IS AVOIDED. Taking a protein's clade as the
  ## modal phylum over all its peptides and then asking whether those same
  ## peptides resolve is circular: a protein none of whose peptides resolve has
  ## no clade and drops out, which is the bias under test. So a row's clade must
  ## be carried by its protein's OTHER peptides. Within-protein phylum
  ## consistency is measured first, since the leave-one-out step assumes it.
  votes <- rows |> dplyr::filter(to_phylum) |>
    dplyr::count(Protein, phylum_name, name = "v")
  cons <- votes |> dplyr::group_by(Protein) |>
    dplyr::summarise(top = max(v), tot = sum(v), .groups = "drop")
  cat(sprintf("\n[3] within-protein phylum consistency: %.1f%% of resolved rows sit in their protein's modal phylum (%d proteins with >= 1 resolved peptide)\n",
              100 * sum(cons$top) / sum(cons$tot), nrow(cons)))
  clade <- votes |> dplyr::group_by(Protein) |>
    dplyr::slice_max(v, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |> dplyr::ungroup() |>
    dplyr::select(Protein, clade = phylum_name) |>
    dplyr::left_join(cons |> dplyr::select(Protein, n_res = tot), by = "Protein")
  byc <- rows |> dplyr::inner_join(clade, by = "Protein") |>
    ## the clade must survive removing this row's own vote
    dplyr::filter(n_res - as.integer(to_phylum) >= 1L,
                  clade %in% c("Bacillota", "Bacteroidota")) |>
    dplyr::group_by(clade, grp) |>
    dplyr::summarise(psm_rows = dplyr::n(), pct_to_phylum = round(100 * mean(to_phylum), 1),
                     .groups = "drop")
  print(as.data.frame(byc))

  ## ---- the verdict -----------------------------------------------------------
  w <- function(cl, g) {
    v <- byc$pct_to_phylum[byc$clade == cl & byc$grp == g]
    if (length(v)) v else NA_real_
  }
  gap_bacil <- w("Bacillota", "chaperone")   - w("Bacillota", "rest")
  gap_bacte <- w("Bacteroidota", "chaperone") - w("Bacteroidota", "rest")
  cat(sprintf("\n    chaperone minus rest, percentage points: Bacillota %+.1f | Bacteroidota %+.1f\n",
              gap_bacil, gap_bacte))
  cat(if (is.na(gap_bacte) || is.na(gap_bacil)) {
    "    ---- one clade has too few rows to compare; the control is not decisive\n"
  } else if (gap_bacte < -5 && gap_bacte < gap_bacil - 5) {
    paste0("    ---- ARTIFACT IS LIVE. Chaperone peptides from Bacteroidota proteins\n",
           "    resolve to phylum at a materially lower rate than that clade's other\n",
           "    peptides, and more so than in Bacillota. C10d's 0.86% is then partly\n",
           "    an assignment rate, and Figure 3c must say so.\n")
  } else {
    paste0("    ---- ARTIFACT EXCLUDED on this test. Chaperone peptides do not resolve\n",
           "    to phylum at a lower rate in Bacteroidota than that clade's other\n",
           "    peptides, so C10d's clade gap is not produced by assignability. State\n",
           "    this where Figure 3c is described.\n")
  })
})
```

## 14b. Acid suppression and prior antibiotics as covariates

Table 1 reports acid suppression at 12 of 23 non-responders against 4 of 18
responders (p = 0.063) and leaves it there. Acid suppression is an established
perturbant of the gut community, so the chaperone share is refitted with it, and
with prior antibiotics, as covariates — on the same Freedman–Lane footing as
§8f, which is the right test when a covariate is itself associated with
response.

```{r c14b-medication}
local({
  req <- c("OP", "chap_new", "chap_frac_of", "pitt_meta_raw", "mp")
  miss <- req[!vapply(req, exists, logical(1))]
  if (length(miss)) {
    cat("14b skipped; missing: ", paste(miss, collapse = ", "), "\n"); return(invisible())
  }
  MED <- c(ppi = "PPI_H2RA_use", abx = "Abx_use_3Mprior_C1D1")
  absent <- MED[!MED %in% names(pitt_meta_raw)]
  if (length(absent)) {
    cat("14b skipped; Lior_UPF_data.csv has no ", paste(absent, collapse = ", "), "\n")
    return(invisible())
  }
  smap_p <- mp$pitt_annot_use |> dplyr::distinct(Mixture, Channel, BioReplicate) |>
    dplyr::mutate(sample = paste(Mixture, Channel, sep = "_"))
  yn <- function(x) {
    v <- trimws(toupper(as.character(x)))
    dplyr::case_when(v %in% c("1", "Y", "YES", "TRUE")  ~ 1L,
                     v %in% c("0", "N", "NO", "FALSE")  ~ 0L,
                     TRUE                               ~ NA_integer_)
  }
  d <- chap_frac_of(OP, chap_new) |>
    dplyr::inner_join(smap_p |> dplyr::select(sample, BioReplicate), by = "sample") |>
    dplyr::left_join(pitt_meta_raw |>
                       dplyr::transmute(MF_ID,
                                        ppi = yn(.data[[MED[["ppi"]]]]),
                                        abx = yn(.data[[MED[["abx"]]]])),
                     by = c("BioReplicate" = "MF_ID")) |>
    droplevels()
  cat(sprintf("\nchannels %d | acid suppression recorded %d, on it %d | antibiotics recorded %d, on them %d\n",
              nrow(d), sum(!is.na(d$ppi)), sum(d$ppi == 1L, na.rm = TRUE),
              sum(!is.na(d$abx)), sum(d$abx == 1L, na.rm = TRUE)))
  if (sum(!is.na(d$ppi)) < 20) {
    cat("too few records to adjust; stopping here\n"); return(invisible())
  }
  ## is the covariate associated with response at all? If not, adjusting for it
  ## cannot move the estimate and the rung is reported for completeness only.
  for (v in c("ppi", "abx")) {
    tb <- table(d[[v]], d$resp)
    if (all(dim(tb) == c(2, 2)))
      cat(sprintf("    %s by arm: Fisher p = %.3f\n", v,
                  suppressWarnings(fisher.test(tb)$p.value)))
  }
  ## Freedman-Lane, residuals of the reduced model permuted within plex.
  fl14 <- function(covars, dat, seed, B = 2000) {
    dat <- dat[stats::complete.cases(dat[, c("frac", "Mixture", "resp", covars)]), , drop = FALSE]
    dat <- droplevels(dat)
    rhs  <- paste(c("Mixture", covars), collapse = " + ")
    full <- lm(as.formula(paste("qlogis(frac) ~", rhs, "+ resp")), data = dat)
    red  <- lm(as.formula(paste("qlogis(frac) ~", rhs)), data = dat)
    obs  <- coef(summary(full))["respR", 1]
    e <- residuals(red); f <- fitted(red); set.seed(seed)
    nl <- replicate(B, {
      dd <- dat
      dd$.y <- f + e[ave(seq_along(e), dat$Mixture, FUN = sample)]
      coef(summary(lm(as.formula(paste(".y ~", rhs, "+ resp")), data = dd)))["respR", 1]
    })
    c(n = nrow(dat), resp = obs, se = coef(summary(full))["respR", 2],
      p_perm = (1 + sum(abs(nl) >= abs(obs))) / (1 + B))
  }
  ## A COVARIATE WITH NO VARIATION IS NOT AN ADJUSTMENT. The 14 Oct knit printed
  ## an `abx` rung at n = 42 while reporting "antibiotics recorded 42, on them 0":
  ## every recorded patient is a non-user, so adding the column adjusts for a
  ## constant and the row is really the 42-patient subsample, unadjusted. Reported
  ## as that, or dropped, rather than as a rung a reader would take for an
  ## adjustment.
  vary <- vapply(c(ppi = "ppi", abx = "abx"),
                 function(v) length(unique(d[[v]][!is.na(d[[v]])])) > 1L, TRUE)
  for (v in names(vary)[!vary])
    cat(sprintf("    %s has no variation among the %d patients with a record, so it\n      cannot be adjusted for; no rung is reported for it\n",
                v, sum(!is.na(d[[v]]))))
  use <- names(vary)[vary]
  rung <- c(list(none = fl14(character(0), d, 7401)),
            setNames(lapply(seq_along(use),
                            function(i) fl14(use[i], d, 7401 + i)), use),
            if (length(use) > 1) list(both = fl14(use, d, 7400 + length(use) + 1)))
  JM <- do.call(rbind, rung)
  print(round(JM, 4))
  r <- function(k) if (k %in% rownames(JM))
    sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * JM[k, "resp"] / JM["none", "resp"]) else "not reported"
  cat(sprintf("    acid suppression retains %s of the unadjusted difference; both together %s\n",
              r("ppi"), r("both")))
  cat(sprintf("    n falls from %d to %d where a record is required, so a rising p here is\n      lost power and not a lost effect: SE %.4f against %.4f\n",
              JM["none", "n"], JM[nrow(JM), "n"],
              JM[nrow(JM), "se"], JM["none", "se"]))
})
```

## 14c. Per-channel depth: does the chaperone share track it, and is it balanced by arm?

The quantity reported is the share of the two most abundant functional classes,
which is what per-channel depth and reporter-ion compression move. ED1a shows
the spread of PSM rows per channel but neither the share against depth nor the
balance of depth between arms within plex.

```{r c14c-channel-depth}
local({
  req <- c("OP", "chap_new", "ribo_new", "chap_frac_of")
  miss <- req[!vapply(req, exists, logical(1))]
  if (length(miss)) {
    cat("14c skipped; missing: ", paste(miss, collapse = ", "), "\n"); return(invisible())
  }
  s  <- OP$d$sample
  dep <- data.frame(sample = s,
                    rows = colSums(!is.na(OP$a[, s, drop = FALSE])),
                    signal = colSums(OP$a[, s, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE))
  d <- chap_frac_of(OP, chap_new) |>
    dplyr::rename(chap = frac) |>
    dplyr::left_join(chap_frac_of(OP, ribo_new) |> dplyr::select(sample, ribo = frac),
                     by = "sample") |>
    dplyr::left_join(dep, by = "sample") |> droplevels()
  cat(sprintf("\n[1] PSM rows per channel: median %s (range %s to %s)\n",
              format(median(d$rows), big.mark = ","),
              format(min(d$rows), big.mark = ","), format(max(d$rows), big.mark = ",")))

  ## ---- [2] does either share track depth? ------------------------------------
  cat("\n[2] share against per-channel depth (Spearman, and the within-plex response fit with depth added)\n")
  for (q in c("chap", "ribo")) {
    ct <- suppressWarnings(cor.test(d[[q]], d$rows, method = "spearman"))
    m0 <- coef(summary(lm(qlogis(d[[q]]) ~ Mixture + resp, d)))["respR", ]
    m1 <- coef(summary(lm(qlogis(d[[q]]) ~ Mixture + log(rows) + resp, d)))["respR", ]
    cat(sprintf("    %-5s rho = %+.3f, p = %.3f | response coefficient %+.4f -> %+.4f with log(depth) in the model (%.0f%% retained)\n",
                q, ct$estimate, ct$p.value, m0[1], m1[1], 100 * m1[1] / m0[1]))
  }

  ## ---- [3] is depth balanced by arm, within plex? ----------------------------
  ## WITHIN PLEX is the only question that matters: the design is built on it, so
  ## a depth difference between arms POOLED across plexes is not a confounder,
  ## while one inside a plex is.
  fit <- lm(log(rows) ~ Mixture + resp, d)
  ce  <- coef(summary(fit))["respR", ]
  cat(sprintf("\n[3] log depth by arm, plex-adjusted: %+.4f (SE %.4f, p = %.3f) -- %.1f%% difference in rows\n",
              ce[1], ce[2], ce[4], 100 * (exp(ce[1]) - 1)))
  per <- d |> dplyr::group_by(Mixture) |>
    dplyr::summarise(n = dplyr::n(),
                     NR = round(median(rows[resp == "NR"])),
                     R  = round(median(rows[resp == "R"])), .groups = "drop") |>
    dplyr::mutate(ratio = round(NR / R, 3))
  print(as.data.frame(per))
  cat(if (ce[4] >= 0.05) {
    "    ---- depth is balanced between arms within plex; the share difference is not a depth difference\n"
  } else {
    "    ---- depth is NOT balanced within plex; report the depth-adjusted coefficient from [2] alongside\n"
  })
})
```
